title_en: A2P 10DLC Campaign Approval Best Practices
source_md:
A2P 10DLC Campaign approval depends on whether your Campaign information clearly and consistently explains **who is sending messages, what is being sent, why recipients receive the messages, and how they consented**.

Use this guide before submitting or resubmitting a Campaign to catch common approval problems with your use case, sample messages, website, consent flow, Privacy Policy, and Terms & Conditions. HighLevel provides the registration workflow, but carriers and registration partners make the final approval decision.

[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/OiOt7SLXXXk?&wmode=opaque)
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/OiOt7SLXXXk)

If the video does not display, [watch it on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OiOt7SLXXXk).

---

## **Table of Contents**

- [What Is A2P 10DLC Campaign Vetting?](#What-Is-A2P-10DLC-Campaign-Vetting?)
- [Key Benefits of Following Campaign Approval Best Practices](#Key-Benefits-of-Following-Campaign-Approval-Best-Practices)
- [Campaign Approval Checklist](#Campaign-Approval-Checklist)
- [Campaign Use Case and Description](#Campaign-Use-Case-and-Description)
- [Sample Messages](#Sample-Messages)
- [Consent and Web Form Opt-In](#Consent-and-Web-Form-Opt-In)
- [Providing Verifiable Opt-In Proof](#Providing-Verifiable-Opt-In-Proof)
- [Text Message and Offline Opt-In](#Text-Message-and-Offline-Opt-In)
- [Website, Privacy Policy, and Terms & Conditions](#Website,-Privacy-Policy,-and-Terms-&-Conditions)
- [Restricted and Forbidden Messaging](#Restricted-and-Forbidden-Messaging)
- [How to Prepare Your A2P Campaign for Approval](#How-to-Prepare-Your-A2P-Campaign-for-Approval)
- [What to Do if Your Campaign Is Rejected](#What-to-Do-if-Your-Campaign-Is-Rejected)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Is A2P 10DLC Campaign Vetting?**

A2P 10DLC Campaign vetting reviews how your business intends to use SMS or MMS messaging. Reviewers compare your Campaign use case, description, sample messages, website, and consent process to confirm that the information is accurate, verifiable, and consistent.

Your Campaign should tell one consistent story:

- **Brand:** Who is sending the messages
- **Use Case:** Why messages are being sent
- **Campaign Description:** Who receives them and what they can expect
- **Sample Messages:** Examples of the actual messages you plan to send
- **Opt-In Flow:** How recipients give consent
- **Website:** A working site that represents the registered business
- **Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions:** Publicly accessible policies that support the messaging program

**IMPORTANT:** Completing these recommendations improves submission quality but does not guarantee approval. Final Campaign approval is handled by carriers and registration partners.

---

## **Key Benefits of Following Campaign Approval Best Practices**

A complete and consistent Campaign submission makes it easier for reviewers to understand and verify your messaging program before approval.

- **Fewer Avoidable Rejections:** Catch missing, conflicting, or unverifiable information before submission.
- **Clearer Consent Verification:** Show reviewers exactly where and how contacts agree to receive messages.
- **Better Campaign Consistency:** Keep your use case, description, sample messages, website, and opt-in language aligned.
- **Faster Troubleshooting:** Make rejection reasons easier to identify and correct.
- **Stronger Messaging Compliance:** Reduce the risk of registering a Campaign that does not match the messages you actually send.

---

## **Campaign Approval Checklist**

A reviewer should be able to understand your messaging program without making assumptions. Check each item before submitting or resubmitting your Campaign.

- Your **Campaign Use Case** matches the messages you actually plan to send.
- Your **Campaign Description** identifies the sender, recipients, message purpose, and consent method.
- Your **sample messages** reflect real messages your business will send.
- Your business or sender name appears in your sample messages.
- Your sample messages match the selected Campaign Use Case.
- Your website is live, accessible, and represents the registered business.
- Your opt-in method can be verified by a reviewer.
- Your consent language explains what messages the contact agrees to receive.
- Your opt-out workflow clearly explains how contacts can stop messages and what confirmation they receive.
- Your HELP response identifies the business and provides a valid support method.
- Your Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions are publicly accessible.
- Your Campaign does not involve restricted or prohibited messaging.
- If your Campaign includes both promotional and informational messaging, your sample messages represent both message types.

---

## **Campaign Use Case and Description**

The Campaign Use Case defines the type of messaging you plan to send, while the Campaign Description explains how that messaging works for your business. Both should match the messages recipients will actually receive.

Choose the use case that most accurately represents your messaging purpose, such as Marketing, Customer Care, 2FA, Account Notifications, or another supported Campaign type.

A strong Campaign Description should answer:

- Who is sending the messages?
- Who receives the messages?
- What types of messages are sent?
- Why are the messages being sent?
- How do recipients opt in?

**Good example:**

Acme sends appointment reminders and service updates to existing customers who provide SMS consent through our online appointment form.

**Avoid:**

This Campaign sends messages to customers.

The second example does not provide enough information for a reviewer to clearly understand the Campaign.

---

## **Sample Messages**

Sample messages show reviewers what recipients can expect after opting in. They should represent actual messaging content and match both your Campaign Use Case and Campaign Description.

Include:

- Your business or sender name
- Realistic message content
- The same messaging purpose described in the Campaign
- Appropriate opt-out language, such as **Reply STOP to unsubscribe**
- Bracketed placeholders for variable content, such as **[First Name]** or **[Appointment Date]**

```
If your Campaign includes multiple message types, make sure the samples represent each type of messaging you plan to send. For mixed messaging, include at least one promotional/marketing example and one transactional/informational example when applicable.
```

**Example:**

Acme Dental: Hi [First Name], your appointment is scheduled for [Date] at [Time]. Reply STOP to unsubscribe.

**IMPORTANT:** Make sure your sample messages accurately represent the content your Campaign will send and match the use case selected during registration.

Avoid public URL shorteners in Campaign sample messages. Use full, direct HTTPS URLs when a URL is included.

---

## **Consent and Web Form Opt-In**

Consent must clearly show that the contact knowingly agreed to receive the type of messages described in your Campaign. Reviewers also need to be able to verify how consent is collected.

For a web form opt-in:

- Clearly identify the business sending the messages.
- Explain the type of messages the contact agrees to receive.
- Include message frequency information.
- Include a **Message and data rates may apply** disclosure.
- Include applicable HELP and STOP instructions.
- Provide accessible Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions links.
- Do not preselect SMS consent checkboxes.
- Do not require SMS consent in order to submit the form.
- Clearly separate marketing and non-marketing consent when both are collected.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078635848/original/F6Y1drLv6aaBQx61bG6oQI1QmAezeMqsGg.png?1786992315)**

```
Collecting a contact's phone number does not by itself establish consent to receive SMS messages.
```

A reviewer should be able to understand what the contact is agreeing to by viewing the form itself.

For detailed requirements, see [A2P Opt-In Form - Privacy Policy and Terms and Conditions Guidelines](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001426-a2p-opt-in-form-privacy-policy-and-terms-and-conditions-guidelines).

---

## **Providing Verifiable Opt-In Proof**

Reviewers must be able to verify the consent method described in your Campaign. If the original opt-in experience cannot be viewed publicly, provide accessible evidence showing what the recipient sees before consenting.

This commonly applies to:

- Paper forms
- Forms behind a login
- Unpublished or pre-launch forms
- QR-code flows
- Offline promotional materials
- Other opt-in methods that cannot be directly opened by a reviewer

You can upload a screenshot of the opt-in evidence to HighLevel Media Storage and obtain a shareable link.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078635814/original/Xys31S-Vy5CP42TzboodN6ojXz34YeydNg.png?1786992261)**  
**Video: Preparing Verifiable Opt-In Proof**

Watch this example to understand how supporting opt-in evidence can be prepared for Campaign review.

[ Your browser does not support the video element.](https://storage.googleapis.com/msgsndr/mHhVPt7zuyQB5MWsQAL2/media/67cf2f1aad861da8cb7824d3.mp4)

If the video does not display, [open the video directly](https://storage.googleapis.com/msgsndr/mHhVPt7zuyQB5MWsQAL2/media/67cf2f1aad861da8cb7824d3.mp4).

Your supporting evidence should clearly show the consent language and applicable disclosures. Do not provide a URL that requires the reviewer to sign in.

---

## **Text Message and Offline Opt-In**

Text-to-join and offline Campaigns still need a clear Call to Action that explains what the recipient is joining before they opt in.

Include information such as:

- Business or program name
- Opt-in keyword and destination number
- Type of messages the contact will receive
- Message frequency
- Message and data rate disclosure
- HELP information
- STOP instructions
- Privacy Policy and Terms information when applicable

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078635742/original/PDPUSTtjApU6GIGnJg6759Iuub8zDrmbwg.png?1786992193)**

When registering this type of opt-in, provide enough information and supporting evidence for a reviewer to verify the consent experience.

### **HELP and STOP Responses**

### 

HELP and STOP responses give recipients a clear way to manage their messaging preferences and get support. These responses should identify your business and provide enough information for recipients and reviewers to understand what happens after a keyword is sent.

- **STOP response:** Acknowledge the opt-out request, identify the business or brand, and confirm that no further messages will be sent.
- **HELP response:** Identify the business or brand and provide a valid phone number, email address, or other support contact method.
- Make sure the HELP and STOP behavior described in your Campaign matches the actual messaging experience.

---

## **Website, Privacy Policy, and Terms & Conditions**

Your website helps reviewers confirm that the Campaign belongs to the business being registered. Your business identity, Campaign information, website, and consent flow should remain consistent.

Before submitting, verify that:

- The website URL works.
- The website represents the registered business or declared DBA.
- Business information on the website matches the Campaign.
- The opt-in page can be accessed if website opt-in is being used.
- Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions pages are publicly accessible.
- The Privacy Policy appropriately addresses SMS opt-in data and consent.

For detailed policy requirements, see [A2P Opt-In Form - Privacy Policy and Terms and Conditions Guidelines](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001426-a2p-opt-in-form-privacy-policy-and-terms-and-conditions-guidelines).

---

## **Restricted and Forbidden Messaging**

Selecting an available Campaign Use Case does not make prohibited messaging eligible for A2P 10DLC. Certain business categories and message types may be restricted, rejected, filtered, suspended, or subject to additional requirements.

Examples can include certain:

- High-risk financial services
- Third-party lead generation
- Debt-related services
- Illegal or controlled substances
- Gambling
- Firearms or vaping-related messaging
- Other restricted or regulated content

Review [Forbidden Message Categories for SMS and MMS in the U.S. and Canada](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001219617-forbidden-message-categories-for-sms-and-mms-in-the-us-and-canada) before registering if you are unsure whether your business or messaging content is eligible.

---

## **How to Prepare Your A2P Campaign for Approval**

Reviewing the Campaign as one complete customer journey helps uncover inconsistencies that may not be obvious when each registration field is completed separately.

1. Go to **Settings → Phone System → Trust Center**.
2. Open **Brand & Campaigns** from the A2P Messaging card.
3. Confirm that your Brand represents the business that will actually send the messages.
4. Choose a Campaign Use Case that matches your messaging purpose.
5. Write a Campaign Description that identifies the sender, recipient, message purpose, and consent method.
6. Add realistic sample messages that match the selected use case.
7. Verify your opt-in flow, website, Privacy Policy, and Terms & Conditions.
8. Check for mismatched names, URLs, messaging purposes, or consent language before submission.

For the complete registration workflow, see [A2P Campaign Registration: Step-by-Step Guide and FAQs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004539-a2p-campaign-registration-step-by-step-guide-and-faqs).

---

## **What to Do if Your Campaign Is Rejected**

A rejection reason identifies an issue discovered during Campaign vetting. Review the complete submission before resubmitting so another issue does not cause an additional rejection.

1. Go to **Settings → Phone System → Trust Center**.
2. Open your A2P Brand and Campaign information.
3. Locate the rejected Campaign.
4. Review the displayed failure or rejection reason.
5. Open any available required-fix information.
6. Correct the identified issue.
7. Review the complete Campaign again before resubmitting.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078635549/original/9zpvA1YqZvu5W9VTWjgPRCo8Z5Ecb2TiUg.png?1786992078)**

**IMPORTANT:** Do not review only the field named in the rejection. Recheck your Campaign description, use case, sample messages, website, consent flow, and policy links before resubmitting.

```
IMPORTANT: Some Campaign fields may not be editable during resubmission. If the required fix involves a locked field, such as the Campaign use case or opt-in message, you may need to create and submit a new Campaign. Review the displayed required fixes before making changes.
```

For detailed rejection guidance, see [A2P Campaign Rejections, Required Fixes & Vetting Errors](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007572-a2p-campaign-rejections-required-fixes-vetting-errors).

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Does following every recommendation guarantee Campaign approval?**

No. These practices improve the quality and consistency of your submission, but carriers and registration partners make the final approval decision.

**Q: Why can a correct-looking Campaign still be rejected?**

Reviewers evaluate the Campaign as a whole. A working website does not correct a sample message that conflicts with the selected use case or an opt-in flow that cannot be verified.

**Q: What should my HELP response contain?**

Your HELP response should identify the business or brand and provide a valid way for the recipient to get assistance, such as a phone number or email address.

**Q: What should happen after a contact replies STOP?**

The response should acknowledge the opt-out request, identify the business or brand, and confirm that the recipient will no longer receive messages from the messaging program.

**Q: What if my Campaign uses more than one opt-in method?**

Describe every opt-in method selected during registration and provide enough information or supporting evidence for reviewers to verify each consent experience.

**Q: What should I do if my Campaign is rejected more than once?**

Review the latest required fixes and recheck the entire Campaign rather than correcting only the most recent issue.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [A2P Campaign Registration: Step-by-Step Guide and FAQs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004539)
- [A2P Campaign Rejections, Required Fixes & Vetting Errors](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000007572)
- [A2P 10DLC Campaign Use Cases](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000000235)

## **What is the Prospecting Tool?**

The Prospecting Tool is a software tool designed to help businesses and agencies find potential customers, generate marketing audit reports for them and start outreach all at once place!. It uses search parameters like location and keywords to identify potential customers and then generates a marketing audit report that provides insights into the prospects' online presence regarding their listings and reviews, and then start outrach by sending personalised Email or SMS.

 The tool identifies gaps in the prospects' online marketing strategies and provides recommendations for improvement. Thus, our Prospecting Tool not only streamlines the lead generation process, but also post lead generation nurturing which saves time and resources, and helps businesses and agencies target potential customers more efficiently.

**Who is this feature most useful for?**

The Prospecting Tool can be used by various businesses and agencies that want to generate leads and find potential customers. It can be particularly beneficial for:

1. **Marketing Agencies:**Marketing agencies can use the Prospecting Tool to generate leads for their clients and provide them with detailed insights into their online presence.
2. **Small Business Owners:**Small business owners can use the Prospecting Tool to identify potential customers in their local area and target them more efficiently.
3. **Digital Marketers:** Digital marketers can use the Prospecting Tool to generate leads for their clients and provide them with detailed insights into their online presence.
4. **Sales Professionals:** Sales professionals can use the Prospecting Tool to find potential customers and generate leads for their sales pipeline.
5. **SEO Specialists:** SEO specialists can use the Prospecting Tool to identify businesses that need help with their online listings and reviews and provide them with recommendations for improvement.

---

## **What are the benefits of the Prospecting Tool?**

The Prospecting Tool has several benefits, including:

- **Finding Local businesses nearby:** The Prospecting Tool helps you find local businesses near you, making it easier to target and convert them into potential customers. Find more than 50 leads per search!
- **Generating Marketing Audit Reports:**The Marketing Audit Report provides detailed insights into the prospects' online presence regarding their Listings and Reviews. This information can be used to target and convert potential customers more efficiently.
- **Automate Lead Generation:**With Prospect AI which comes with both basic free tier prospecting and with Premium Prospecting as well. Setup you niche, Zipcode, etc., and let AI finds and recommend you leads every week!
- **Automate Outreach: The Prospecting Tool is live on Sub Accounts, which automates and streamlines the post lead generation nurturing actions using workflows such as sending personalised email, welcome SMS which include link to audit reports to leads. Add leads to opportunities and much more**
- **Saving time and resources:**The Prospecting Tool automates and streamlines the lead generation process, enabling agencies to reach more potential clients with a more targeted and efficient approach.

---

**Manage prospects on the dashboard**

Prospect Cards let you track lead outcomes directly in Prospecting.  
  
**Open** is the default state.  
Use the Prospect Card dropdown to mark a lead as **Won** or **Lost**.


## **Generating Reports using GHL's Prospecting Tool**

## **1. Access the Prospecting Tool**

- Inside Agency: Click on the Prospecting Tab from the left menu
- Inside a Sub Account 
  - Enable Prospecting in a Sub Account: Either via Turning ON Prospecting in Reselling Tab or deploying it your Agency's specific Sub Account only, [read more here.](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005777-prospecting-at-sub-accounts-complete-guide-benefits-setup)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083316485/original/JoVqxHVYkbSy0_mUD4ge-CjyK7iRyq9NUw.png?1791984770)

## **2. Search Options**

Click on the "Add Prospect" Button. You will be redirected to the search page. You have multiple ways to search for leads:

### **A. Keyword Search**

- Enter any business type or keyword (e.g., “Dentist”, “Real Estate Agent”, “Contractor”).
- You can also enter a specific brand name (e.g., “KFC”) to find exact matches.

### **B. Location Search (in Labs currently)**

- Enter a location like a city, postal code, or full address (e.g., *77024, Houston, TX 77024, USA*).
- You can also select a location directly on the map.
- If you want to find leads near your current location, type **“near me”** — we’ll use your IP location for search.

### **C. Set Search Radius**

- Choose the radius from your center location (up to **31.1 miles**).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083316816/original/STl2-yLQOjXEFfOEWXnVdLIvws-B5aclZg.png?1791984868)

###

3. You will be redirected to the prospect's detail page. If you know any Point of contact (POC) for that location, enable the POC toggle and enter their details. Click on Save Location to Proceed.

When adding a prospect from search results, you can choose whether to generate a Marketing Audit Report immediately or save the prospect and generate the report later.

4. Choose whether to generate the report:

   - **Checked:** Saves the prospect and automatically generates a Marketing Audit Report.
   - **Unchecked:** Saves the prospect without generating a Marketing Audit Report.
5. Click **Add prospect** to save the prospect.

If the option is disabled, the prospect is saved without an audit, which you can generate later from the Prospect Details page.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083317248/original/iWeenplznI6kn2NwJsWwz6UEBcxPfaB2nw.png?1791985050)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083317647/original/WX2JAcYucRe4QqhYNXFhvk_iqDPbfD-rhQ.png?1791985249)

8. You can prospect for 50 leads in day with basic plan and unlimited with Prospecting Premium Subscription. You can always come back later and prospect more.

## Analyzing the Marketing Audit Report

The Marketing Audit report comprises two major sections - the Listings and the Reviews.

For more on Marketing Audit Reports, refer to [Enhanced Listings Audit in Prospecting & Marketing Audit Reports](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007345-enhanced-listings-audit-in-prospecting-marketing-audit-reports).

Local Businesses need accurate listings on many business directories to ensure people can find them online. The availability of accurate listings ensures customers can find your business locations while it's still open for business.

Google My Business profile contains a significant amount of valuable information to potential customers. This includes your contact info, reviews, website, hours of operation, etc. Local Businesses need plenty of positive online reviews to keep them on par with their competitors.for

## **Website Hosting in Marketing Audit Reports**

title_en: How to Create Flow-Based Voice AI Agents Using Ask AI
source_md:
Creating a flow-based Voice AI agent is now easier with Ask AI in HighLevel. Instead of building complex conversation flows from scratch, you can describe what you want your agent to do, answer a few guided questions, and let Ask AI generate a visual flow. You can review the build plan, customize the generated flow, and test your agent before putting it to use. This makes it easier to create structured voice conversations while maintaining control over your agent's behavior.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is Flow-Based Voice AI Agent Creation in Ask AI?](#What-is-Flow-Based-Voice-AI-Agent-Creation-in-Ask-AI?)
- [Key Benefits of Creating Flow-Based Voice AI Agents Using Ask AI](#Key-Benefits-of-Creating-Flow-Based-Voice-AI-Agents-Using-Ask-AI)
- [Guided Requirement Collection in Ask AI](#Guided-Requirement-Collection-in-Ask-AI)
- [Visual Build Plan and Approval](#Visual-Build-Plan-and-Approval)
- [Editing, Saving, Testing, and Rebuilding Voice Flows](#Editing,-Saving,-Testing,-and-Rebuilding-Voice-Flows)
- [Editing the Generated Voice Flow](#Editing-the-Generated-Voice-Flow)
- [Saving Your Changes](#Saving-Your-Changes)
- [Testing the Generated Flow](#Testing-the-Generated-Flow)
- [Rebuilding the Generated Flow](#Rebuilding-the-Generated-Flow)
- [How to Create a Flow-Based Voice AI Agent Using Ask AI](#How-to-Create-a-Flow-Based-Voice-AI-Agent-Using-Ask-AI)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is Flow-Based Voice AI Agent Creation in Ask AI?**

Flow-Based Voice AI Agent Creation in Ask AI allows you to build structured voice conversations using natural-language instructions. Rather than manually adding and connecting individual nodes, you can describe your business requirements and have Ask AI create an initial flow based on your instructions.

Ask AI guides you through the creation process by gathering your requirements, preparing a visual build plan, and generating an editable voice flow. You can review the conversation paths, make changes directly on the canvas, save and test your work, or open the flow in the full Voice Flow Builder for additional configuration.

For example, you can ask Ask AI to create a voice agent that welcomes callers, identifies whether they need sales or customer support, and routes them to the appropriate conversation path.

```
Note: Prompt-Based Voice AI agent creation remains available. The new Ask AI experience provides an additional method for creating Flow-Based Voice AI agents.
```

---

## **Key Benefits of Creating Flow-Based Voice AI Agents Using Ask AI**

Creating Voice AI agents through Ask AI reduces the manual effort required to build structured call flows. It combines conversational instructions with visual editing tools, making it easier to turn your business requirements into an organized voice-agent workflow.

- **Faster Agent Creation:** Generate an initial voice flow from a natural-language request instead of manually building every conversation path from a blank canvas.
- **Guided Setup:** Answer follow-up questions that help Ask AI understand your business requirements, conversation goals, and expected caller interactions.
- **Visual Build Planning:** Review the proposed flow structure before generation to confirm that the planned conversation matches your requirements.
- **Editable Voice Flows:** Customize the generated conversation paths and configurations using the visual canvas.
- **Flexible Rebuilding:** Request another version of the flow when you need to refine its overall structure or behavior.
- **Testing and Validation:** Test your generated voice flow to identify potential conversation issues before using it with callers.
- **Full Builder Access:** Open your generated flow in the Voice Flow Builder whenever you need additional configuration or advanced editing.

---

## **Guided Requirement Collection in Ask AI**

Clear requirements help Ask AI generate a voice flow that matches your intended business process. When you request a flow-based agent, Ask AI can ask follow-up questions to clarify what the agent should do, what information it needs to collect, and how it should respond to different caller scenarios.

Start by describing the main purpose of your Voice AI agent. Include relevant details such as:

- **Agent Purpose:** What the agent should accomplish, such as qualifying leads, answering customer questions, or assisting with appointment scheduling.
- **Caller Information:** Details the agent should collect, such as the caller's name, contact information, or reason for calling.
- **Conversation Paths:** Different ways the conversation should proceed based on caller responses.
- **Expected Outcomes:** What should happen when a caller completes a particular conversation path.
- **Required Actions:** Any supported actions or integrations needed to complete the workflow.

For example, you could enter the following request into Ask AI:

"Create a flow-based Voice AI agent for my dental clinic. The agent should greet callers, determine whether they want to book an appointment, ask about office hours, or speak to the staff, and direct the conversation accordingly. Collect the caller's name and phone number when they request an appointment."

Ask AI can then ask additional questions to clarify the desired behavior before preparing the build plan.

---

## **Visual Build Plan and Approval**

A build plan outlines how Ask AI intends to organize your Voice AI conversation before generating the actual flow. Reviewing this plan helps you identify missing steps, unnecessary conversation paths, or incorrect assumptions before proceeding.

After gathering your requirements, Ask AI prepares a proposed build plan for your review.

Depending on your requested workflow, the plan may describe:

- The agent's primary responsibilities.
- The expected sequence of the conversation.
- Different conversation paths based on caller intent.
- The actions needed to complete supported tasks.
- How the conversation should conclude.

Review the proposed plan and confirm that it reflects your requirements. If the plan does not match your intended workflow, provide additional instructions or request changes before approving it.

Once you approve the build plan, Ask AI generates the corresponding editable voice flow.

---

## **Editing, Saving, Testing, and Rebuilding Voice Flows**

Generating a voice flow is only the starting point. The editable canvas allows you to review the resulting conversation structure and make adjustments before using the agent. Saving your work and testing different caller scenarios help ensure that the flow behaves as expected.

### **Editing the Generated Voice Flow**

After Ask AI generates the flow, review its structure on the visual canvas. Depending on the generated configuration and the editing controls available, you may need to review or adjust:

- Individual AI Agent nodes and their responsibilities.
- Conversation paths and routing conditions.
- Supported actions and integrations.
- Connections between different stages of the conversation.
- How each conversation path ends.

Review the entire flow to confirm that callers can follow the expected conversation paths.

### **Saving Your Changes**

Saving your edits helps preserve the changes you make to the generated voice flow. After modifying the canvas, use the available save option to retain your changes.

```
Important: Save any canvas edits before requesting a rebuild. This helps prevent your latest changes from being left unsaved when Ask AI generates another version of the flow.
```

### **Testing the Generated Flow**

Testing helps you understand how the Voice AI agent responds to different caller requests and whether the generated conversation paths work as intended.

After saving your flow:

1. Use the available testing option to start a test conversation.
2. Interact with the agent using realistic caller questions.
3. Check whether the agent responds appropriately and follows the expected conversation path.
4. Test different caller requests to verify the configured routing behavior.
5. Review the results and make changes where necessary.
6. Save your updates and test again.

The full Voice Flow Builder also provides Web Call and Phone Call testing options for validating conversation behavior.

For more detailed testing and configuration instructions, refer to [How to Create and Configure Voice AI Flows in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009148-how-to-create-and-configure-voice-ai-flows-in-highlevel).

### **Rebuilding the Generated Flow**

Rebuilding allows you to request another generated version of the flow when the current structure does not fully meet your requirements.

Before rebuilding:

1. Review the changes you have already made to the canvas.
2. Save your existing edits.
3. Describe the adjustments you want Ask AI to make.
4. Request a rebuild using the available control.
5. Review the newly generated flow and confirm that it matches your updated requirements.

**Important:** Always save canvas edits before requesting a rebuild.

---

## **How to Create a Flow-Based Voice AI Agent Using Ask AI**

Creating a flow-based Voice AI agent through Ask AI begins with a description of your business requirements. Following the guided creation process, reviewing the proposed build plan, and testing the resulting flow help you produce an agent that supports your intended calling experience.

**Before You Begin:**

- Make sure your HighLevel sub-account has access to Ask AI and Voice AI.
- Identify the main purpose of the Voice AI agent you want to create.
- Prepare a basic outline of the conversation and expected caller outcomes.
- Identify any information, actions, or integrations the agent may require.

**Note:** This feature is rolling out to sub-accounts with Ask AI and Voice AI access. It may not appear in every eligible sub-account immediately.

**Step 1: Open Ask AI**

1. Log in to your HighLevel account.
2. Switch to the sub-account where you want to create the Voice AI agent.
3. Click the **Ask AI** icon in the top navigation bar to open the assistant.
4. Start a new conversation or use the available prompt field.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083406521/original/86-LgoycOf4yMs7z3psjQSd_auilZb1U0g.png?1792065929)

**Step 2: Request a Flow-Based Voice AI Agent**

1. Enter a request describing the Voice AI agent you want to build.
2. Specify that you want a **flow-based Voice AI agent**.
3. Include the agent's purpose, expected conversation paths, and any relevant business requirements.
4. Submit your request.

Example prompt:

"Build a flow-based Voice AI agent for my business that greets callers, identifies whether they need sales or support, collects their contact details, and directs them to the appropriate conversation path."

Providing specific requirements helps Ask AI prepare a more relevant build plan.

**Step 3: Answer the Guided Questions**

1. Review the follow-up questions presented by Ask AI.
2. Provide the requested details about your business and conversation requirements.
3. Clarify how the agent should respond to different caller scenarios.
4. Continue answering questions until Ask AI has enough information to prepare the build plan.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083408111/original/Y8gzZLLiyXHpelkuVXLMTlP-rXnq6CZqTA.png?1792066472)

**Step 4: Review and Approve the Build Plan**

1. Review the visual build plan generated by Ask AI.
2. Check whether the proposed conversation paths match your intended workflow.
3. Identify any missing steps or adjustments.
4. Request changes to the plan if necessary.
5. Approve the plan when you are satisfied with the proposed structure.

Ask AI uses the approved plan to generate the voice flow.

**Step 5: Review and Edit the Generated Voice Flow**

1. Examine the generated flow on the visual canvas.
2. Review the conversation paths, connected nodes, and available configurations.
3. Make any necessary adjustments using the available editing controls.
4. Confirm that the flow includes the required conversation outcomes.
5. Save your changes.

**Step 6: Test or Rebuild the Flow**

1. Use the available testing option to evaluate the generated agent.
2. Test different caller scenarios to verify the conversation behavior.
3. Identify any areas that need improvement.
4. Make and save additional edits as needed.
5. If the flow requires broader changes, save the existing canvas edits before requesting a rebuild.
6. Review and test the updated flow.

**Step 7: Open the Full Voice Flow Builder**

1. Locate the option to open your generated flow in the full Voice Flow Builder.
2. Open the flow in the builder.
3. Review its node configurations, routing paths, and supported actions.
4. Complete any additional settings or integrations required for your use case.
5. Save and test the completed configuration before deploying the agent.

For additional guidance on configuring and deploying flows, see [How to Create and Configure Voice AI Flows in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009148-how-to-create-and-configure-voice-ai-flows-in-highlevel).

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why don't I see the option to create flow-based Voice AI agents in Ask AI?**

The feature is being released gradually to sub-accounts with Ask AI and Voice AI access. If the option is unavailable, confirm that your sub-account has access to both products and check again as the rollout progresses.

**Q: Can I continue creating Prompt-Based Voice AI agents?**

Yes. Prompt-Based Voice AI agent creation remains available. The new Ask AI experience provides an additional option for generating flow-based agents.

**Q: Do I need to know how to configure Voice AI nodes before using Ask AI?**

No prior experience with manually building flows is required to begin. Ask AI can generate the initial structure from your instructions. However, understanding the available nodes and actions can help when reviewing or customizing complex flows.

**Q: Can I create a Voice AI agent for a specific business scenario?**

Yes. You can describe scenarios such as lead qualification, appointment inquiries, customer support, or call routing. Ask AI uses the requirements you provide to prepare a build plan and generate the initial flow. Any required actions or integrations must be supported and properly configured.

**Q: What should I do if Ask AI generates a flow that doesn't match my requirements?**

Review the generated flow and identify what needs to change. You can edit the flow or request a rebuild with updated instructions. Save any canvas edits before rebuilding.

**Q: Can I test the agent without assigning a live phone number?**

The full Voice Flow Builder supports browser-based Web Call testing, allowing you to evaluate supported conversation behavior without assigning a phone number. Some capabilities, such as call transfers, require Phone Call testing.

**Q: Will Ask AI automatically configure every external integration my agent needs?**

Not necessarily. Some actions and integrations require additional configuration, credentials, permissions, or authentication. Review these requirements in the full Voice Flow Builder before relying on the flow for live calls.

**Q: Can I edit the generated flow after opening it in the full Voice Flow Builder?**

Yes. The full Voice Flow Builder supports editing nodes, routing conditions, supported actions, and other available configuration settings.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Ask AI Assistant](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005327)
- [Build with AI for Voice AI Flows](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008311)
- [Getting Started with the Flow-Based Builder for Voice AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009134-getting-started-with-the-flow-based-builder-for-voice-ai)
- [How to Create and Configure Voice AI Flows in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009148-how-to-create-and-configure-voice-ai-flows-in-highlevel)
- [How to Use Voice AI Flow Builder Templates and Guided Setup](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008604-how-to-use-voice-ai-flow-builder-templates-and-guided-setup)
- [How to Create Voice AI Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004107-how-to-create-voice-ai-agents)

title_en: Getting Started - Launch a Website from Blank
source_md:
Launching your own website from scratch can feel overwhelming, but don't let the blank page stop you. With these instructions you can go from idea to published in record time.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [Preparation & Planning](#Preparation-&-Planning)
- [Create Blank Website](#Create-Blank-Website)
- [Build the Home Page](#Build-the-Home-Page)
- [Add More Pages](#Add-More-Pages)
- [Add Navigation](#Add-Navigation)
- [Previewing, Settings & Publishing](#Previewing,-Settings-&-Publishing)

---

## **Preparation & Planning**

Before you even log into GoHighLevel or drag your first element, taking some time to plan your website will save you significant time and effort, and result in a much more effective site.

1. Define Your Website's **Purpose**:  
     
   1. What is the primary goal of this website? Is it to generate leads, sell products, provide information, build brand awareness, or book appointments? Knowing this will guide all your design and content decisions.
   2. Who is your target audience? Understanding their needs, preferences, and pain points will help you tailor the website's content and design to resonate with them.
2. Outline Your **Content & Structure**:  
     
   1. What pages do you need? Most business websites start with a Home, About, Services/Products, and Contact page. You might need more or fewer depending on your goals.
   2. What key information or call-to-action needs to be on each page? Think about what you want visitors to do or learn on each page.
   3. Gather your assets: Do you have your logo, brand colors, images, videos, and written content (or at least an idea of it) ready?
3. A Simple **Plan**: A table can help you map this out. Your plan might look something like this:

| Page/Element | Purpose | Sections & Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | Introduce the business, highlight key offerings, main call to action | Main Headline (ex: Welcome to Business)  Sub Headline (ex: We help you do Thing)  Call To Action (ex: Book a Call)  Intro Media (ex: hero image or video sales letter)  Overview of each product/service |
| About Us | Build trust, tell your story, introduce the team | Company history/mission Team member photos & bios Values/What makes us different |
| Contact | Allow visitors to get in touch, provide a location | Contact form Phone number, email Address Map |
| Services/Products | Details about what you offer | List and description of products/services Pricing information Benefits Case studies |
| Navigation Menu | Easy site-wide navigation | Logo, links to pages |
| Footer | Important links, copyright, contact info | Copyright notice Privacy policy Terms of service Contact info Social media icons |

---

## **Create Blank Website**

1. **Navigate**to Sites > Websites > New Website > From Blank and click Create.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698235/original/ifjG4aDUFMTAtvjgGnrnDe1gj4kJNuY19g.png?1748997405)
2. Click **Add New Page** then give it a **name** (ex: Home) and click **Create New Page****.**  
     
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698279/original/JJWbpt8NVcaPzzftQOe4-idhjuIaGw04tA.png?1748997618)**

---

## **Build the Home Page**

1. Click**Create From Blank**  
     
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698353/original/UdEab0LhcqO5CmtXPxrMXPrKvEisQ-Jb4g.png?1748997941)**
2. Open the **Website Builder.**  
     
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698356/original/-KYYzy_8kB1lOB_DMvuEuP8EV_vHpZCreQ.png?1748997970)**
3. **Understand the Editor:**
   1. **Control Panel:** Control what appears in the Left Panel (4) such as elements, pages, and metadata.
   2. **Device Switcher:** Switch between desktop and mobile views to test responsiveness.
   3. **Meta Controls**: History, undo, preview, save, publish, etc.
   4. **Left Panel**: Elements and settings for the page.
   5. **Center Panel:** Live editable preview of your page.
   6. **Right Panel:** Settings and styling options for the selected Section, Row, or Element.
   7. **Breadcrumb Bar:** Shows the hierarchy of the selected element at the bottom of the builder. Hover over an ancestor to highlight it on the canvas, or click it to select and edit it.  
        
      ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698398/original/QDiRTb63ytLpjq98Gt1sdpVAhq9Uh6Ok6w.png?1748998154)

      ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081120423/original/VWMmzo5_kE0JL045HkIvElK_yvhxXefe0Q.png?1789584510)
4. **Add a Section:**In the center (if empty) or by clicking the **+ (Add Element/Section)** icon on the left sidebar, choose **Sections**, then select a section width (e.g., **Full Width**).  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698493/original/cGm1FC7mWXzX2SfeJVTEAiqXBsLfPDaCQw.png?1748998456)
5. **Add a Row:**Inside the new green-bordered section, drag to add a **Row**and select **1 Column**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698531/original/6wVfOs8If9n6aO0h1i9B0qirKVd5q6yPzA.png?1748998544)
6. **Add Headline and Sub-Headline:**In the 1 Column Row, click **Add Element.**  
     
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698576/original/UiIY-XU86f874ZalvNuPpixdwx8wWC1yxw.png?1748998710)**
   1. **Headline:** Drag a "Headline" element into the row. Click the text to edit it (e.g., "Welcome"). Use the right panel to change font, size, color, etc.
   2. **Sub-Headline:** Click **+ Add Element** again, drag a "Sub-Headline" below the main headline. Edit its text and style (ex: We Help You Grow).  
        
      ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698666/original/JJVlNXis0a_d4eIVKhuLgAVPG3y2ZINXUQ.png?1748998951)
7. **Add a Button**: Under the sub-headline add a **button**. Then, edit the text of the button to **"Call Us Now"**,  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698716/original/HkLKAh7sZ9skwbbsVJ7ndEn77OJLh1RoRQ.png?1748999107)
8. **Add an Action**: In the button's settings (Right Panel) scroll down to **Button Actions,** select **Call,**then input your phone number.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047698771/original/W1YGOMCjH8d-43vYXTarzQmDe5LTuXOz-w.png?1748999331)
9. **Repeat:** Continue adding sections, rows, and elements to build out your homepage.
10. **Save**: Click the save icon.  
      
    ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047837288/original/BxqzElKxlWxuGPZ4HioWk5P4OgNM3V4tbA.png?1749158065)

---

## **Add More Pages**

1. **Navigate to**Sites > Websites > Site Details (if you are still in the page editor click the back button).  
     
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047837334/original/pqUOdYOO67hcYinkakEn2C3wYzoHag_dZg.png?1749158183)**
2. **Add a New Page:**Click the Add New Page button. Name the page (Ex: About Us) Click **Create New Page****.**  
     
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047837365/original/ruKFpJyU3RewT1UUNYpvW6eXPRLtCWa6rg.png?1749158290)**
3. **Create From Blank**: In this case, click the Create From Blank button.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047837419/original/2G6lY1DtVJ4ig6NfhVbDtchrwB9WmH39hQ.png?1749158529)
4. **Build Page**: Add elements and content to the page in the same way. You can add a **text** element and an **image** element. Make sure to click **Save** and then **Back**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839680/original/xvKmjTd2POp13ipuNNvn1Jvb7fDSeI0fPg.png?1749169525)

---

## **Add Navigation**

1. **Navigate**to Sites > Websites > Site Details (if you are still in the page editor click the back button).  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839818/original/eofvlKtYnxl5ODFlMN4dNchnvOzqFMkmKw.png?1749170157)
2. **Edit the Home Page**: Under the page card titled "home" click **Edit**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839828/original/s-5G36HpE0-yJ0790d9oJDrn1I3PnamSCQ.png?1749170223)
3. **Add new top full width section**: At the very top of the page, above all the other sections, add a new full width section.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839841/original/8vHXgHci7z2NollPbGl2ounXymJvoWFEFQ.png?1749170320)
4. **Add a 1 column row and Navigation Menu**: Inside the new top section, add a 1 column row, then add the element called Navigation Menu.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839852/original/6aK7AGNk7ykqWfBMnzL-ts5mmE3HSUbibA.png?1749170415)
5. **Edit Navigation Menu Settings**: Click to select the navigation menu, then in the right settings bar, make sure each link goes to the right page, add a logo, etc.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839868/original/odLao3e1VufSLSsrW8pl0saAwq9B2Me9_Q.png?1749170517)

   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839907/original/tkcnS-AEOcYBoVsheA3aLs9LJY4YE04aYg.png?1749170737)
6. **Add a new bottom full width section**: At the bottom of the page, under all the other sections, add a new full width section.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839947/original/vztXlKPm6YMHNi8rnIBmMeISSt5g-npYJw.png?1749170854)
7. **Add a prebuilt footer**: Open Elements > Prebuilt Elements > Footer and drag a footer into the bottom section.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047839959/original/D1xvDgvFF8BDwI0vuR-mOeffs5OE5ZGpmw.png?1749170949)
8. **Edit Navigation Menu and Footer**: Select each element and delete it or edit its settings in the **Right Panel**. When you're done, click **Save** and **Back**.

---

## **Previewing, Settings & Publishing**

1. **Navigate**to Sites > Websites > Site Details and click the **preview page button**(box with arrow icon). **OR** if you are in the page builder, click the **preview button** (eyeball icon).  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840048/original/nLKHQNFbWUf27WnN1zJWFw0tzv8hLwAQ3Q.png?1749171792)

   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840066/original/xjzAWw8YqEE8K8qXMyJAsJb3tIT9geEuYA.png?1749171851)  
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840074/original/j6BNAiqF2edfQzlfxItz-_mAUZ9EXKPs5A.png?1749171894)
2. **Preview mobile**: In the page builder, click the mobile phone icon to switch between desktop and mobile views. OR in the preview, right click and select inspect, then in the inspector panel click the desktop/mobile icon.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840081/original/O9ovDRTyjykYl-3591rTk7Jyde2804tMcg.png?1749171966)  
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840103/original/exkQkuGacXNM3TTl5kwW6Z03DXRqr-C3Hw.png?1749172045)  
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840114/original/gfZ9Qnqyv-mQL8CU6nv5ouhCSDeGSfspVg.png?1749172105)
3. **Adjust for responsiveness**: In the page editor, adjust the elements and settings until everything looks good on both desktop and mobile. If you can't get one element looking the way you want, you can duplicate it and in **advanced settings**make one element **visible on desktop** and the other **visible on mobile**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840151/original/dpGn72JVodMarIFL1hEEv5Q1GgbNICpvrg.png?1749172283)
4. **Save and Publish**: You should be frequently saving and maybe publishing. When you're done, make sure to save and publish for the last time.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840175/original/YLOuKz-eNuF1lFmlujLwPioqV5oo6DFtvA.png?1749172457)
5. **SEO Meta Data**: In the page builder, click the SEO icon to open the SEO Meta Data panel. Edit SEO and meta data details (title, description, etc).  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155047840190/original/rPXLzadIM8ABWS-9jCBNVmrsNggWfK3Acg.png?1749172554)
6. **Connect a domain**: Optional, but if you have a custom domain you can attach it to your site. To connect a domain, leave the page builder and go to the **Settings**tab. From here, you can select a domain, add a favicon, add tracking code, add a chat widget and more.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068547621/original/qr6JiyZFBcKVyqGuSrxP-pIPOPn5mvHsqw.png?1775504166)

---

## **Troubleshooting Website Launch Issues**

If your website does not look or behave as expected after publishing, use the checks below.

### 

### **The live website still shows old content**

Saving a page does not always make the latest version live.

1. Open the affected page in the Website Builder.
2. Click **Save**.
3. Click **Publish**.
4. Open the live URL in an incognito or private browser window and check the page again.

Make sure each page that should be live has been published.

### 

### **The domain shows as pending or is not connecting**

If the domain has not finished connecting:

- Confirm the DNS records match the values provided by HighLevel.
- Check the record type, host/name, and value for typing errors.
- Remove conflicting DNS records when applicable.
- Allow time for recent DNS changes to propagate.

If automatic domain connection is unavailable, use the manual DNS configuration option provided during setup.

### 

### **The website opens a 404 page**

Confirm that:

- The domain is assigned to the correct website.
- The intended page has been published.
- The page URL path is configured correctly.
- The correct page is configured as the website's default or home page.

### 

### **The website shows an SSL or privacy warning**

Check for incorrect or conflicting DNS records.

If you use Cloudflare, confirm that records requiring direct DNS resolution are configured as **DNS only** when instructed by HighLevel.

After correcting the DNS records, allow time for the SSL certificate to be issued.

### 

### **Navigation links open the wrong page**

Open the **Navigation Menu** element and confirm that every menu item points to the correct page or URL.

If pages were added, renamed, or reordered, review the navigation links again before publishing.

### 

### **The website looks incorrect on mobile**

Open the page in the Website Builder and switch to the mobile view.

Check:

- Element spacing and alignment.
- Font and button sizes.
- Section and row widths.
- Elements configured as desktop-only or mobile-only.

Adjust the mobile layout as needed, then save and publish the page again.

### 

### **Forms, calendars, or buttons are not working**

Before sharing the site publicly:

- Submit each form as a test visitor.
- Test calendar booking links.
- Click each button and call-to-action.
- Confirm links open the intended page or destination.
- Verify that test submissions create the expected record or notification.

### 

### **Final Website Launch Check**

Before sharing your website, confirm that:

- The domain is connected and verified.
- The website loads securely over `https://`.
- The correct homepage appears.
- All required pages are published.
- Navigation links work.
- Forms and buttons work.
- Desktop and mobile layouts display correctly.
- The latest published content appears on the live site.

title_en: How to Connect and Use MCP Servers in Conversation AI
source_md:
Conversation AI bots can now connect to MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to use external applications and tools during supported customer conversations. This allows bots to perform actions such as booking appointments through Cal.com, sending Stripe payment links, and updating Google Sheets without leaving the conversation. You can connect ready-made MCP servers from the Marketplace or add your own custom server. This guide covers connecting servers, configuring usage instructions, managing tool access, and monitoring MCP activity in Agent Logs.

---

**Table of Contents**

- [What is MCP Servers Support in Conversation AI?](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-6a90cfd8d9a481919356a2811bb36973-highlevel-t1-t2-article-bot/c/6ad8fb3a-1b90-8322-b20d-59c54584f0b7#what-is-mcp-servers-support-in-conversation-ai)

# **What is MCP Servers Support in Conversation AI?**

MCP Servers Support allows prompt-based Conversation AI bots to connect with external applications and use their available tools while responding to customers. Instead of only providing information, a bot can perform supported actions in connected systems based on the customer's request and the instructions you configure.

Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way for AI agents to interact with external tools and services.

For example, a Conversation AI bot can check appointment availability through Cal.com, create a booking, or use Stripe to send a payment link. It can also work with external applications such as Google Sheets and Notion, depending on the connected server and its available tools.

MCP tools work alongside existing Conversation AI capabilities, including Custom API actions, Knowledge Base retrieval, and Workflows.

---

## **Key Benefits of MCP Servers in Conversation AI**

MCP servers extend what Conversation AI bots can accomplish during customer conversations. By connecting external applications and configuring their available tools, you can support more tasks without creating a separate custom integration for every application.

- **Perform external actions:** Allow bots to complete supported tasks such as booking appointments, sending payment links, and updating external records during conversations.

- **Connect ready-made applications:** Choose from 40+ Marketplace MCP servers, including Stripe, Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Notion, and Zapier.

- **Connect custom tools:** Add your own MCP server using its name and HTTPS URL, with optional authentication credentials.

- **Control tool access:** Choose which tools each connected MCP server makes available to your Conversation AI bot.

- **Configure when tools are used:** Define the situations in which the bot should call each server and optionally specify what it should say afterward.

- **Monitor execution:** Review MCP tool calls in Agent Logs, including their Success or Failed status.

---

## **Prerequisites and Limitations**

Before connecting MCP servers, make sure your Conversation AI bot meets the supported configuration requirements. MCP availability depends on the bot type, operating mode, and Labs activation.

**Prerequisites**

- Enable **MCP support for Conversation AI** in Labs.
- Use a **Prompt Based Bot** in Conversation AI.
- Configure the bot to operate in **Auto-Pilot** mode for inbound conversations.
- Have an account with the external application you want to connect, when required by that application's connection flow.
- For custom MCP servers, have the server's **HTTPS URL** and any required authentication details.

**Limitations**

- **Supported mode:** MCP servers currently work with prompt-based bots in Auto-Pilot mode on inbound conversations.

- **Unsupported modes:** MCP servers are not yet supported in Suggestive mode or Flow bots.

- **Server limit:** You can connect up to five MCP servers per bot.

- **Tool limit:** The release specifies a maximum of 100 tools.
- **Tool availability:** The actions available to the bot depend on the tools exposed by each connected MCP server.

---

## **How To Setup MCP Servers in Conversation AI**

Setting up MCP support involves enabling the Labs feature, connecting an external or custom server, and defining which tools your bot can use. Complete these steps before testing MCP activity through a supported conversation.

### 

### **Step 1: Enable MCP Support in Labs**

MCP support must be enabled in Labs before the new MCP Servers section becomes available in the Conversation AI bot builder.

- From the **Sub-Account View**, select **Settings** in the left-hand navigation menu.
- Select **Labs**.
- Locate the feature named **MCP support for Conversation AI**.
- Turn on the feature.
- Return to Conversation AI and reopen the relevant bot editor.

### 

### **Step 2: Open MCP Servers in the Conversation AI Bot Builder**

The MCP Servers section appears inside the prompt-based bot editor. This is where you connect external applications and manage the servers available to the bot.

- From the **Sub-Account View**, select **AI Agents** in the left-hand navigation menu.
- Select **Conversation AI**.
- Open **Agent List**.
- Select the existing prompt-based bot you want to configure.
- In the right-hand configuration panel, locate and expand **MCP Servers**.
- Click **Connect MCP Server**.

The MCP server selection window opens, allowing you to choose an existing Marketplace connector or add a custom server.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084013734/original/U8XGmQQA6XXlCDNSAmMj_iQ2p4-7oAGF-g.png?1792719807)

### **Step 3: Connect an MCP Server from the Marketplace**

The MCP Marketplace provides ready-made connectors for supported external applications. You can search the list, review a server's details, and connect the external account you want the bot to use.

- In the MCP server selection window, locate the **Search apps...** field.
- Search for the application you want to connect, such as **Cal.com**, **Stripe**, or **Google Sheets**.
- Select the application from the **NOT CONNECTED** list.
- Review its description, author, and connector URL.
- Click **Connect**.
- Complete the application's connection or authorization process.

  For example, the Cal.com connector displays an authorization prompt asking whether LeadConnector can access your Cal.com account.
- If prompted, review the authorization request and select **Allow** to authorize the connection.
- Return to the MCP server window and verify that the application appears under **CONNECTED**.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084013750/original/o4hn1qfggAbyQocq9ceKMLcdUOsOfotvlQ.png?1792719881)

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084013753/original/avBlonPQht5tUc1-htgSX8m7LuPYQdxxZg.png?1792719921)

### **Step 4: Add a Custom MCP Server**

If the application you need is not available as a ready-made Marketplace connector, you can add a custom MCP server using its HTTPS URL. This lets you connect a compatible external or internally managed server and use its exposed tools.

To add a custom server:

- From the **Sub-Account View**, select **AI Agents** in the left-hand navigation menu.
- Select **Conversation AI**.
- Open **Agent List**.
- Select the prompt-based bot you want to configure.
- Expand **MCP Servers** and click **Connect MCP Server**.
- In the server selection window, select **+ Add custom MCP**.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084013548/original/iDgoS2oTS6fT2aZTei9BuOl2W4hTj87TNQ.png?1792718999)

- Enter the required details:

  - **Name:** Enter a descriptive name for the custom MCP server.
  - **MCP server URL:** Enter the server's HTTPS URL.
- If your connection requires additional authentication configuration, expand **Advanced**.
- Review or enter the applicable fields:

  - **Client ID:** Optional.
  - **Client secret:** Optional.
  - **Redirect URI:** Review the URI displayed by the interface for the applicable authentication setup.
- Click **Add MCP**.

The custom server is then available in the MCP server configuration interface.

### 

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084013621/original/rCgsMK3hJ4rGeJIhmCLeiicuVMlc4vV9Lw.png?1792719363)

### **Step 5: Configure When the Bot Should Use the MCP Server**

After selecting a connected MCP server, define when the bot should call it. Clear instructions help the bot associate customer requests with the external tools needed to complete them.

- In the selected server's configuration panel, locate **When should this MCP be used?**
- Enter instructions describing when the bot should use the server.

  This field is **required** and supports up to **500 characters**.  
  **Example**: When a customer wants a visit, check open slots and book the one they pick.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084013653/original/ViOvd77s7mg-vB2mGYedbkxTzau3YyCZpA.png?1792719451)

When a customer wants a visit, check open slots and book the one they pick.

- Locate **What to say after using this MCP server**.
- Optionally enter instructions describing what the bot should communicate after using the server.

  This field supports up to **300 characters**.

### **Step 6: Choose the Connected Account and Configure Tools**

Each MCP server exposes a list of tools that the bot can use. Reviewing this list helps ensure the bot only has access to the operations needed for its assigned tasks.

- In the selected MCP server's configuration panel, locate **Accounts**.
- Select the connected account you want to use.

  The interface also provides **+ Add account** for connecting another account.
- Scroll to the **Tools** section.
- Review the tools available from the connected server.
- Use the tool search field if you need to locate a specific tool.
- By default, all available tools are selected.
- Clear the checkbox beside any tool the bot should not use.

For example, a Cal.com MCP server can expose tools such as:

- `get_availability`
- `get_busy_times`
- `get_event_types`
- `get_bookings`
- `create_booking`
- `reschedule_booking`
- `cancel_booking`

If the bot only needs to check availability and create bookings, you can deselect other tools that are not needed for that task.

```
Important: Available tools depend on the connected MCP server. Review the current tool list rather than assuming every integration offers the same operations.
```

  

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084013674/original/T6z3N0uq1v_hmy0kiuZHQFQW9zCcYXy7AQ.png?1792719555)

### **Step 7: Save and Test the MCP Configuration**

Saving the configuration applies your selected server instructions, account, and tool choices. Testing helps you check whether the bot follows the intended instructions before using the setup in customer conversations.

- Review the selected MCP server's usage instructions.
- Confirm that the correct connected account is selected.
- Check that only the intended tools remain enabled.
- Click **Save** at the bottom of the MCP configuration panel.
- From the **Sub-Account View**, select **AI Agents**, then **Conversation AI**.
- Open **Agent List**, select the configured prompt-based bot, and open **Bot Goals**.
- Locate **Test Your Bot** and enter a sample customer request related to the MCP server.

  For example, test an appointment request when using a Cal.com connector.
- Review the bot's response against the instructions you configured.
- Validate MCP execution through a controlled inbound conversation handled by the bot in Auto-Pilot mode.
- Review the resulting MCP tool calls in **Agent Logs**.

---

## **How to Monitor MCP Tool Calls in Agent Logs**

Agent Logs provide visibility into the actions a Conversation AI bot performs during a conversation. For MCP servers, the logs identify which external tool was called and whether the call succeeded or failed.

To review MCP activity:

- From the **Sub-Account View**, select **AI Agents** in the left-hand navigation menu.
- Select **Agent Logs**.
- Open the **Sessions** view.
- Locate the session you want to review. Use the available filters to narrow the results by contact, agent, channel, or time range.
- Open the relevant session.
- Review the conversation and its execution timeline.
- Locate entries beginning with **MCP -**, followed by the tool name.
- Check whether each call displays **Success** or **Failed**.

For example, an appointment-booking conversation may produce entries such as:

- `MCP - get_availability`
- `MCP - create_booking`

A conversation involving Stripe may also show a payment-related tool call.

The logs help identify which external tools were called while processing the conversation. They can also be used to investigate failed calls or unexpected results.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084013720/original/i80tri_AgfWb0bM6f4QVEDW_0ru9nY8-MA.png?1792719733)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I connect Marketplace MCP servers and custom MCP servers to the same Conversation AI bot?**

Yes. A bot can have Marketplace connectors and custom MCP servers in its configuration. The supplied example shows Cal.com and Stripe alongside a custom Shop inventory server.

**Q: Can a bot use tools from multiple MCP servers during the same conversation?**

Yes. The release demonstrates a conversation where the bot uses Cal.com for appointment scheduling and Stripe for payment-related actions, alongside other Conversation AI capabilities.

**Q: Does every custom MCP server require a Client ID and Client secret?**

No. The custom MCP configuration lists both fields as optional. Enter them when required by the authentication configuration of the MCP server you are connecting.

**Q: Does the bot call every enabled MCP tool during every conversation?**

No. The **When should this MCP be used?** field defines when the bot should use a server. Tool selection determines which operations are available when the bot calls that server.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Labs Features - Complete Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003588-labs-features-complete-overview)

- [How to Set Up a Conversation AI Bot](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004401-setting-up-conversation-ai)

- [Bot Goals Overview - Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004417-bot-goals-overview-conversation-ai)

- [How to Customize Conversation AI Agent Responses with Prompts and Instructions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002255-customize-your-ai-responses-using-prompts)

- [Conversation AI - Agent Logs](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007996-conversation-ai-agent-logs)

- [Appointment Booking in Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000210-how-to-use-conversation-ai-to-book-appointments)

title_en: Email Sequences in HighLevel
source_md:
Email Sequences in HighLevel help you automate multi-step email follow-ups while keeping messages connected in a single conversation thread.

You can schedule follow-up emails, apply conditions based on recipient activity, and stop future messages when a contact replies. This makes it easier to manage sales outreach, lead nurturing, customer onboarding, and other communications that require multiple touchpoints.

You can also monitor sequence performance and review individual email steps to improve your follow-up strategy.

```
IMPORTANT: Email Sequences are documented as available in Private Beta for selected opted-in customers. Current broader availability has not been confirmed.
```

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Email Sequences?](#What-are-Email-Sequences?)
- [Key Benefits of Email Sequences](#Key-Benefits-of-Email-Sequences)
- [Email Sequences vs. Regular Email Campaigns](#Email-Sequences-vs.-Regular-Email-Campaigns)
- [Email Sequences vs. Workflow Email Automation](#Email-Sequences-vs.-Workflow-Email-Automation)
- [Single-Threaded Email Conversations](#Single-Threaded-Email-Conversations)
- [Stop on Reply](#Stop-on-Reply)
- [Delays and Conditions](#Delays-and-Conditions)
- [Designed and Plain-Text Emails](#Designed-and-Plain-Text-Emails)
- [Sequence and Step-Level Statistics](#Sequence-and-Step-Level-Statistics)
- [How To Setup Email Sequences](#How-To-Setup-Email-Sequences)
  - [How to Pause an Email Sequence?](#How-to-Pause-an-Email-Sequence?)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What are Email Sequences?**

Email Sequences allow you to send a series of automated emails to selected contacts, lists, or segments. Instead of sending each follow-up manually, you can organize multiple email steps into a sequence with configurable delays, conditions, and reply-based stopping.

Unlike regular email campaigns that deliver a single message to an audience, Email Sequences support ongoing, multi-step communication. Messages are organized into a single threaded conversation, helping recipients maintain context as they receive follow-ups.

For example, a sales team can send an introductory email, wait before sending a follow-up, and stop additional emails once the recipient replies.

---

## **Key Benefits of Email Sequences**

Email Sequences help you automate follow-up without losing the personal feel of a connected conversation. By combining delays, conditions, and threaded emails, users can create more relevant outreach while reducing repetitive manual work.

- **Threaded Conversations:**Keep automated follow-up emails in one email thread so recipients can easily understand the full conversation history.
- **Behavior Based Follow-Ups:** Send follow-up emails based on recipient behavior, such as open or delivery status.
- **Time Savings:**Automate repetitive outreach instead of manually sending each follow-up email.
- **Reply Based Stopping**: Stop future sequence emails when a recipient replies, helping avoid unnecessary follow-ups.
- **Flexible Email Formats:**Use designed emails or plain-text emails depending on the communication style needed.
- **Performance Visibility:**Review sequence-level and step-level statistics to understand how each email performs.

---

## **Email Sequences vs. Regular Email Campaigns**

Regular Email Campaigns and Email Sequences serve different communication needs. Regular campaigns are designed for individual broadcasts, while sequences help automate a series of related messages over time.

| Feature | Regular Email Campaigns | Email Sequences |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary purpose | Send one email to an audience | Automate multiple follow-up emails |
| Email delivery | Immediate, scheduled, or supported batch delivery | Multiple steps with configured timing |
| Follow-up steps | Not part of the same regular campaign | Built into the sequence |
| Behavior-based conditions | Not the primary purpose of regular campaigns | Supports step conditions based on email activity |
| Threaded follow-ups | Not a core regular campaign feature | Designed to keep follow-ups connected |
| Stop on Reply | Not a standard campaign sequence setting | Available for automated stopping |
| Performance tracking | Campaign-level reporting | Sequence-level and step-level reporting |

**When to use a Regular Email Campaign:** Send a newsletter, promotional announcement, or one-time update to a selected audience.

**When to use an Email Sequence:** Send an introduction followed by multiple scheduled messages to nurture a lead or continue a conversation.

For more information, see [Send or Schedule an Email Campaign](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001215263).

---

## **Email Sequences vs. Workflow Email Automation**

Workflows are broader automations that can include many types of actions, triggers, channels, and business logic. Email Sequences are focused specifically on automated email follow-up from the email campaign area.

Use Email Sequences when your goal is to create a structured email follow-up series. Use workflows when your automation requires multiple channels, complex branching, pipeline changes, task creation, or other non-email actions.

For example:

- **Use Email Sequences** to send a series of sales follow-up emails that stop when a contact replies.
- **Use Workflows** to automate a process that sends an email, updates an opportunity, creates a task, or includes SMS communication.

---

## **Single-Threaded Email Conversations**

Single-threaded email conversations allow each email in the sequence to appear as part of the same ongoing conversation. This helps recipients understand the context of each follow-up and reduces the chances that messages feel disconnected.

Threaded sequences are especially helpful for outreach where each message builds on the previous one, such as lead follow-up, sales outreach, onboarding, or appointment-related communication.

---

## **Stop on Reply**

Stop on Reply prevents unnecessary automated follow-ups when a recipient responds to a sequence email. Enabling this setting helps you avoid continuing an automated outreach series after a contact has engaged in the conversation.

When Stop on Reply is enabled:

- A contact receives sequence emails according to the configured steps and conditions.
- If the contact replies, future emails from that sequence stop for that contact.
- The conversation can continue through manual communication without additional automated sequence follow-ups.

**For example**, if a contact replies to the first email in a three-step sales sequence, the remaining sequence emails will not be sent to that contact.

Stop on Reply is especially useful for sales prospecting, lead nurturing, and other outreach where a response should transition the conversation to direct communication.

```
Note: Stop on Reply is an optional setting. Review its configuration before activating your sequence.
```

---
