## **Delays and Conditions**

Delays and conditions determine when follow-up emails are sent and whether a contact qualifies for a specific step. These settings help space out communication and make follow-ups more relevant to recipient activity.

**1. Delays**

Delays control the amount of time between sequence steps.

For example, a three-step sequence could be organized as follows:

- **Email 1:** Send the initial introduction.
- **Email 2:** Send a follow-up after the configured delay.
- **Email 3:** Send another follow-up after an additional delay.

This approach allows you to maintain consistent communication without manually scheduling each email.

**2. Conditions**

Conditions control whether an email step should be sent based on supported recipient activity.

Email Sequences support conditions based on:

- **Email Open Status:** Determine whether a recipient has opened a previous email.
- **Email Delivery Status:** Determine whether a previous email has been delivered.

For example, you can configure a follow-up email to send only when a previous message meets an open-status condition.

Conditions can be configured for individual steps, allowing different emails in the sequence to have different delivery requirements.

```
Important: Review the conditions attached to each step before activating the sequence. A condition can affect whether a contact receives the corresponding email.
```

---

## **Designed and Plain-Text Emails**

Email Sequences support both designed emails and plain-text emails. Designed emails are useful for branded communication, newsletters, or visually formatted outreach. Plain-text emails are useful when you want messages to feel more direct, personal, and conversational.

You can choose the format that best matches the purpose of each sequence. For example, a sales follow-up sequence may use plain-text emails, while a customer onboarding sequence may use designed emails with helpful links and visual formatting.

---

## **Sequence and Step-Level Statistics**

Email Sequences include performance analytics at both the sequence level and the individual step level. Sequence-level statistics help you understand overall performance, while step-level statistics help you identify which specific emails are performing well or need improvement.

---

## **How To Setup Email Sequences**

Proper setup helps ensure each contact receives the right follow-up at the right time. Before creating a sequence, confirm the audience, timing, email content, and stopping rules so the sequence supports your outreach goal without sending unnecessary emails.

1. Navigate to Marketing → Email → Campaigns.  
     
   **![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083872352/original/I1fVTYfdENbDjG5aSZLI8TbWUVOYbNgWjQ.png?1792589381)**
2. Click to create a new campaign or email asset, then select Create an Email Sequence.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083872487/original/6q7qgHSuO7gj8M3UUIcEC-mjsrHMQeR3cQ.png?1792589424)
3. Set the sequence trigger. Choose whether the sequence should start immediately or be scheduled for a later time.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083872583/original/rSCv4SgMQCZS78Lp3hpvon_Kiwy5OFQYvg.png?1792589464)
4. Choose the sequence audience. Select the contacts, lists, or segments that should enter the sequence.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083872728/original/AHrca9CAAsX-eKMrSyG2GQWhKsCFIn6xGQ.png?1792589530)
5. Configure Stop on Reply. Enable this option when you want the sequence to stop sending future emails after a recipient replies.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070032008/original/MeV95_QpdsgRBPCY_KpJRvU6J32Q3jgvMQ.png?1777294657)
6. Add email steps. Create the emails that should be sent as part of the sequence. Add delays between steps to control when each follow-up is sent.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070032253/original/JIKDbC5ZMOD66qN__DDSWaA0ngbYy5f19Q.png?1777294781)

   7. Select Your Audience

   - Choose from:

     - Lists
     - Segments
     - Individual contacts
   - Enable Stop on Reply if needed

   8. Add Email Steps

   - Add multiple steps to your sequence
   - Define delays between each step  
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073498929/original/ZOSfszurMpzteYezypUOHlsITjbwRewx_g.png?1781199937)

   9. Configure Each Step

   For every email:

   - Select or design a template (or use plain text)
   - Set conditions (e.g., send only if previous email was opened/delivered)
   - Enable tracking as needed![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073498974/original/4tt52cnhZimOStO7jOTIiraEPlS1rfvIIw.png?1781199963)

   10. Review and Launch

   - Double-check your sequence flow
   - Activate the sequence.
   - You would find all emails are threaded in a sequence in our conversations section as well![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073499021/original/Iv38DJ5V4pqs6UTZxpb3twCyJcsRIPM4PQ.png?1781199982)  
       
     ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073499023/original/5iDRHO314e89EfPSXcd8zgFcGTDAKkYTXQ.png?1781199990)

   11. In the list view, click on three dots to access all the statistics - individual email step level and overall email action level.

   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155068523657/original/FwCWCB3rKgQkApDtZaNZciGhcGhMVlOwwg.png?1775476084)

   12. To look at all sequences statistics, you can also check the statistics dashboard in email marketing.![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155073499027/original/F0E3oy2eiGNVehd227qTGtpSRx7gKjtJpg.png?1781200006)

   Review and activate the sequence. Confirm the audience, trigger, delays, conditions, and email content before starting the sequence.  
     
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155070032533/original/QS6BLAqCbad9H55RMY0V44ohMh56ruTZCw.png?1777294995)

From the sequence list, open the three-dot menu and select Statistics to review sequence-level and step-level performance.

---

### How to Pause an Email Sequence?

Users can move a published sequence back to draft. However, any contacts who become eligible for the next step while the sequence is paused or in draft will be skipped.

**For example**, if Email 2 is set to send only after Email 1 is opened, and Contact A opens Email 1 while the sequence is paused, Contact A will not receive Email 2 and will be skipped.

**Also note**: once Step 1 has been executed, or the first email in Step 1 has been sent, users cannot pause the sequence to edit the trigger or Email Step 1.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Who can access Email Sequences?**A: Email Sequences are currently available in Private Beta for selected opted-in customers.

**Q: Are Email Sequences the same as regular email campaigns?**A: No. Regular email campaigns are typically used for one-time email sends, while Email Sequences are used for automated multi-step follow-up.

**Q: Are Email Sequences the same as workflows?**A: No. Workflows support broader automation across multiple actions and channels. Email Sequences are focused on automated email follow-up from the email campaign area.

**Q: What does single-threaded conversation mean?**A: It means the emails in the sequence are sent as part of one ongoing email conversation, helping the recipient keep context across follow-ups.

**Q: What does Stop on Reply do?**A: Stop on Reply stops future sequence emails for a recipient once that recipient replies.

**Q: Can I use both designed and plain-text emails?**A: Yes. Email Sequences support designed emails and plain-text emails.

**Q: Can I send sequence steps based on recipient behavior?**A: Yes. Email Sequences support conditional targeting based on open or delivery status.

**Q: Where can I view Email Sequence statistics?**A: Open the three-dot menu for the sequence and select Statistics to view performance analytics.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Getting Started - Launch an Email Campaign](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005059)
- [How to Send or Schedule a Regular Email Campaign](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001215263)
- [How to Build Recipient Segments in Email Campaigns](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005485)
- [Email Statistics](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001215386)
- [How to Use the Plain Text Editor for Emails](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000003104)
- [How to Use the Email Builder and its In-line Editor](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000000087)

title_en: GoDaddy Dedicated Sending Domain Setu (LC Email)
source_md:
Email Infrastructure

LC Email Dedicated Domain Setup — GoDaddy

A step-by-step guide to adding and verifying your dedicated sending domain using GoDaddy DNS.

What You'll Learn

This article walks you through connecting a dedicated sending domain to LC Email using GoDaddy as your DNS provider. You will add 5 DNS records in total: 2 TXT records, 2 MX records, and 1 CNAME record.

Unlike some DNS providers, GoDaddy requires you to save each record individually. Follow the steps in order and click **Save** after each record before adding the next.

## Add Your Domain in Email Services

Step 1

Navigate to Dedicated Domain settings

In your sub-account, go to **Settings → Email Services → Dedicated Domain** and click **+ Add Domain**.

![Navigating to Settings > Email Services > Dedicated Domain > + Add Domain](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292765242/original/jQLugI8wtvQRfs38XJDujiQd2QnIgjQqSA.gif)

Navigating to Settings → Email Services → Dedicated Domain → + Add Domain

Step 2

Choose your domain type

If your domain is **companyname.com**, you can register either the root domain or a subdomain as your dedicated sending domain.

**Main domain** (companyname.com) — must not already be in use with Google Workspace or another email provider.

**Subdomain** — enter any prefix before your root domain, for example **replies.companyname.com** or **support.companyname.com**.

Note

If you use Google Workspace or another email provider on your root domain, adding the root domain here will conflict with your existing MX records. Use a subdomain instead. See [Can I use the same domain for Mailgun and Google Apps?](https://help.mailgun.com/hc/en-us/articles/203357040-Can-I-Use-the-Same-Domain-Name-for-Mailgun-and-for-Google-Apps-Or-Another-Email-Server-)

Step 3

Click Add & Verify

After entering your domain name, click **Add & Verify**. The next screen will display the 5 DNS records you need to add. Keep this tab open — you will copy values from it in the steps below.

![Add & Verify button](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292766472/original/5TxDqQG542C3YtKLt6stGIAfwcbDmmcesg.png)
![DNS records screen showing 5 records to add](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48293298198/original/xGMUZ9x0JoahqbofrVsYVWEjEF9LDDvsMQ.png)

Keep this DNS records screen open — you will copy values from it in the steps below.

Tip

Migrating from Mailgun? See [How to move a sending domain from Mailgun to LeadConnector](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001226115-how-to-set-up-a-dedicated-sending-domain-lc-email-#How-to-move-sending-domain-from-Mailgun-to-LeadConnector?).

## Access GoDaddy DNS

In a new browser tab, sign in to your [GoDaddy Domain Portfolio](https://dcc.godaddy.com/control/portfolio). Then follow these steps to open the DNS editor for your domain.

Step 1

Click the **three-dot menu** next to your domain to open the Edit Options.

Step 2

Select **Edit DNS**. You may need to scroll down to see this option.

![GoDaddy domain portfolio — click three dots then Edit DNS](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284383735/original/cgJYei63pjBqxqUREcrgnMBHMYjimo-FBA.png)

GoDaddy Save Behavior

GoDaddy requires you to click **Save** after each individual DNS record. You cannot batch all records and save once — complete each section below in full before moving to the next.

DNS Setup Guide

Adding Your 5 DNS Records

Sections 3–7 cover each record. Click Add, fill in the fields, then click Save before starting the next record.

## Add the 1st TXT Record (SPF)

In the GoDaddy DNS editor, click **Add** to create a new record.

![GoDaddy Add button for new DNS record](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284383808/original/H6np93jJkfJVHPLdTaLTLmRgo2mB_c6JRA.png)
![New DNS record form in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284384102/original/N9CKo-PVMexPIY_hCkU3qz4FgWu5LCmiKw.png)

A. Type

Select **TXT** from the Type menu.

B. Host — do not include the root domain

Enter only the subdomain prefix. GoDaddy appends the root domain automatically:

- Setting up **lc**.companyname.com → enter **lc**
- Setting up **replies**.companyname.com → enter **replies**
- Setting up root domain companyname.com → enter **@**

![GoDaddy Host field — enter subdomain prefix only](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292767095/original/U0Uh3wPJ901NXe3E0tAj8DzwIys4kzuXFA.png)

C. TXT Value — same for everyone

Paste the following SPF record value exactly as shown:

v=spf1 include:mailgun.org ~all

![SPF TXT record filled in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292767368/original/n_1Mu3Av0f2EYEvZG9iBeM-knKybDa2RPg.png)

D. Save

Click **Save** to confirm this record.

![Saving the 1st TXT record in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292760158/original/whQOMoD2hGeHEbJgNmnIm1fdwCQhF1Mz9g.png)

## Add the 2nd TXT Record (DKIM)

Important

Everyone's 2nd TXT record hostname and value is **unique to their domain**. Copy both values directly from your platform's DNS records screen — do not use values from screenshots in this article.

Click **Add** in the GoDaddy DNS editor to create a new record.

![GoDaddy Add button for new DNS record](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284383808/original/H6np93jJkfJVHPLdTaLTLmRgo2mB_c6JRA.png)
![New TXT record form for DKIM](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284384815/original/FlVncn3L0vrYLOa9P1vI4X9Pt16_Q-FUOg.png)

A. Type

Select **TXT** from the Type menu.

B. Host — copy everything before the root domain

Look at the 2nd TXT hostname in your DNS records screen. Copy only the portion **before** your root domain — do not include the root domain itself.

![DKIM hostname — copy highlighted portion only](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292768165/original/xN_6s9kcDwkztqKLFUlRtJJJlE7M_GD54w.png)

| Scenario | Copy this as hostname | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Using a subdomain | mx.\_domainkey.helpdesk | Subdomain DKIM hostname example |
| Using the root domain | mailo.\_domainkey | Root domain DKIM hostname example |

C. TXT Value

Paste the full 2nd TXT record value from your platform's DNS records screen (the long highlighted value). This is unique to your domain.

![2nd TXT value — copy the highlighted long value](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292768735/original/cUIeRsQGsIF81ZCW8a-cj-v7iGlndoLiKw.png)

D. Save

Click **Save** to confirm this record.

![Saving the 2nd TXT record in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292760542/original/dHr8OmpttMWN0VMOkXNfAi5G8Ou_hQUiVQ.png)

## Add the 1st MX Record (mxa.mailgun.org)

Google Workspace Users

If you use Google Workspace to send and receive mail on your root domain, adding MX records to the root domain will break your existing email. Use a subdomain for LC Email instead. See [Can I use the same domain for Mailgun and Google Apps?](https://help.mailgun.com/hc/en-us/articles/203357040-Can-I-Use-the-Same-Domain-Name-for-Mailgun-and-for-Google-Apps-Or-Another-Email-Server-)

Click **Add** in the GoDaddy DNS editor to create a new record.

![GoDaddy Add button for new DNS record](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284383808/original/H6np93jJkfJVHPLdTaLTLmRgo2mB_c6JRA.png)
![MX record form in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284385352/original/nEr12soR47bfSHjwNBS075J4Dr_Fd3jqUQ.png)

A. Type

Select **MX** from the Type menu.

B. Host

Same logic as the TXT records — enter only the subdomain prefix:

- **lc**.companyname.com → enter **lc**
- **replies**.companyname.com → enter **replies**
- Root domain companyname.com → enter **@**

![MX record host field](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292769400/original/UKCDaverUyyLQpklJb1Jxf15cmXUamb0VQ.png)

C. Points To — same for everyone

Paste the following value:

mxa.mailgun.org

![MX Points To field — mxa.mailgun.org](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292769476/original/xvdURibcJ1cBG-y1bc5ngzqpnSNCdRALmA.png)

D. Priority — same for everyone

Set Priority to **10**. This value is the same regardless of which domain you are setting up.

![MX Priority field set to 10](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292769807/original/1wmkWSsWNVmgj5fdec3hG0a9KbuWBxPhnA.png)

E. Save

Click **Save** to confirm this record.

![Saving the 1st MX record in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292761314/original/r1sCz03HEK4u2NnzjZxK6TRXfTixx9qJpg.png)

## Add the 2nd MX Record (mxb.mailgun.org)

Click **Add** in the GoDaddy DNS editor to create a new record.

![GoDaddy Add button for new DNS record](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284383808/original/H6np93jJkfJVHPLdTaLTLmRgo2mB_c6JRA.png)
![2nd MX record form in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284385634/original/wYOidp2P0QPZbDYtP60qHBim2dahkciEMw.png)

A. Type

Select **MX** from the Type menu.

B. Host

Same as the 1st MX record — enter only the subdomain prefix:

- **lc**.companyname.com → enter **lc**
- **replies**.companyname.com → enter **replies**
- Root domain companyname.com → enter **@**

![2nd MX record host field](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292770778/original/1YS3yCM8yCVGkdwvDlET1DiZvGimSLDnCA.png)

C. Points To — same for everyone

Paste the following value:

mxb.mailgun.org

![2nd MX Points To field — mxb.mailgun.org](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292770829/original/lo34kUcHgQ_jNcW7DaT0x3DUPiEu1AubLw.png)

D. Priority — same for everyone

Set Priority to **10**.

![2nd MX Priority field set to 10](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292770920/original/Fw8uyagc8TOy9xxMDsHe3atzfkyEu3QnKw.png)

E. Save

Click **Save** to confirm this record.

![Saving the 2nd MX record in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292770952/original/JOROtyvxFT7kuhgJS6UKxsSCMfE6_5IS8A.png)

## Add the CNAME Record

Click **Add** in the GoDaddy DNS editor to create a new record.

![GoDaddy Add button for new DNS record](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284383808/original/H6np93jJkfJVHPLdTaLTLmRgo2mB_c6JRA.png)
![CNAME record form in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284385821/original/Z_H7aEV9Fj-ulIPJTmhnmpgRUG-CWVntNA.png)

A. Type

Select **CNAME** from the Type menu.

B. Host — copy from the platform DNS records screen

The CNAME hostname is prefixed with **email.** followed by your subdomain prefix. Copy the portion before the root domain from the platform's DNS records screen:

- lc.companyname.com → enter **email.lc**
- replies.companyname.com → enter **email.replies**
- Root domain companyname.com → enter **email**

![CNAME host field in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292771034/original/ey4vFuccg-PcVOVNEqKhNZR24VOtPxjuCA.png)

C. Points To — same for everyone

Paste the following value:

mailgun.org

![CNAME Points To field — mailgun.org](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292771083/original/z9S5z7FviH8eq6xc6sXjhiBRLNZCCKQ5LA.png)

D. Save

Click **Save** to confirm this record.

![Saving the CNAME record in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292761511/original/Q-pg6CdROQ4wXlfIoOIOkvDgY1yJdVN1Ug.png)
![All 5 DNS records saved in GoDaddy](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48284386112/original/kW6t3s2sXMcjCylHMSgGSwJy8HDwA4momQ.png)

All 5 Records Saved

All 5 DNS records have been added to GoDaddy. Proceed to Section 8 to verify your domain.

## Verify Your Domain

Switch back to the platform tab and click **Verify Domain** on the Email Services screen.

![Verify Domain button in Email Services](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292771391/original/DSHng9iQ27K8gMmkLYLkL7mpGKnMfyFSkA.png)

Some records still not green?

DNS propagation can take a few minutes. Click **Verify Domain** again after waiting a moment. If records remain unverified after 10+ minutes, go back to GoDaddy and confirm each record's Type, Host, and value are correct.

You're All Set

Once all records show a green checkmark, your dedicated sending domain is active. Next, confirm your [SSL Certificate for Dedicated Sending Domain (LC Email)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001227438) is properly set up.

Then send a test email to confirm everything is working. [Learn how to send a test email in the Conversation.](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001208887)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why do I need to save after each record in GoDaddy?

GoDaddy's DNS editor saves records one at a time. Unlike some providers that let you queue multiple records and save at once, GoDaddy requires each record to be individually confirmed. Follow the steps in order and click Save after each one.

Q: Can I use my root domain if I already use it with Google Workspace?

No. Adding MX records to a root domain that is already in use with Google Workspace will conflict with your existing email setup. Use a subdomain (e.g. **replies.companyname.com**) for LC Email instead.

Q: Why do I add two separate MX records instead of one?

The two MX records (**mxa.mailgun.org** and **mxb.mailgun.org**) provide redundancy — if one mail server is temporarily unavailable, the other can receive messages. Both should be added with Priority 10. GoDaddy requires each MX record to be added and saved separately.

Q: Why is the 2nd TXT record hostname different from what I see in examples?

The 2nd TXT record is a DKIM key generated uniquely for your domain. Its hostname and long value are always different per account. Always copy both from your own DNS records screen — never use values shown in screenshots in this article.

Q: How long does DNS propagation take in GoDaddy?

GoDaddy DNS changes typically propagate within a few minutes to an hour. If records are still not verifying after 10 minutes, wait a bit longer before troubleshooting. Full propagation can take up to 48 hours in rare cases.

Q: What is the difference between a dedicated and a shared sending domain?

A **shared domain** is used by multiple accounts, meaning your sender reputation is pooled with others. A **dedicated domain** is exclusive to your account, giving you full control over your deliverability reputation as it builds over time.

Q: My domain shows as verified but emails are not delivering — what should I check?

First, send a test email from the Conversations area to confirm basic sending is working. Then check that the [SSL Certificate for your Dedicated Sending Domain](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001227438) is active. If issues persist, review each of your 5 GoDaddy DNS records for typos in the Host or Points To fields.

Q: Can I set up multiple dedicated domains for different sub-accounts?

Yes. Each sub-account can have its own dedicated sending domain. Each domain requires its own complete set of 5 DNS records to be added and verified separately in GoDaddy.

title_en: Client Portal Appointments: Book and Manage Meetings
source_md:
Client Portal

Client Portal Appointments: Book and Manage Meetings

Let clients book, review, reschedule, and cancel eligible appointments directly from the HighLevel Client Portal.

What You'll Learn

Client Portal Appointments lets clients book, view, and manage meetings without leaving the HighLevel Client Portal. Clients can review appointments in **Today**, **Upcoming**, and **Past** views, use a calendar view, and book from one or more calendars you make available.

Available client information is automatically filled during booking, while businesses remain in control of which calendars accept Client Portal bookings and whether the Appointments app appears in the portal.

Current Availability

**Appointments are currently available only in the new Client Portal UI.** Support for branded apps is coming soon.

Release Scope

This article covers the currently released calendar-based appointment experience. Service-menu booking and additional appointment-related event-management capabilities referenced as future enhancements are not part of the setup documented below.

# **What is Client Portal Appointments?**

Client Portal Appointments brings scheduling directly into the Client Portal so clients can access meetings and booking options from the same place they use for other business resources. Keeping appointment activity inside the portal reduces the need to search through booking links, confirmation emails, or separate scheduling tools.

Once Appointments and at least one eligible calendar are enabled, clients can:

- View appointments under **Today**, **Upcoming**, and **Past**.
- Use a calendar view to locate appointments by date.
- Book new appointments without leaving the Client Portal.
- Select from one or multiple calendars enabled for Client Portal booking.
- Review appointment details.
- Reschedule or cancel eligible appointments.
- Start another booking after an appointment has been completed.

## **Key Benefits of Client Portal Appointments**

Bringing appointment access and booking into the Client Portal gives clients more control over scheduling while allowing businesses to determine exactly which booking options are available. This creates a more connected self-service experience without changing the calendar rules used to manage availability.

- **Centralized Appointment Access:** Clients can review and manage appointments from the Client Portal instead of relying only on emails or separate booking links.
- **Simplified Booking:** Clients can choose an available calendar, date, and time without leaving the portal.
- **Multiple Calendar Options:** Businesses can make one or several eligible calendars available for clients to choose from.
- **Less Repeated Data Entry:** Existing client contact information is automatically filled where available during booking.
- **Appointment Self-Service:** Clients can cancel or reschedule appointments when those actions are permitted by the calendar's policies.
- **Faster Repeat Booking:** Clients can begin another booking after an appointment has been completed.
- **Administrative Control:** Businesses control both the Appointments app's visibility and which individual calendars accept Client Portal bookings.

## **Availability and Configuration Requirements**

Client Portal Appointments depends on both the portal experience and calendar-level configuration. Understanding each requirement helps prevent situations where the Appointments app is visible but clients cannot select a calendar or complete a booking.

| Requirement | What It Controls | Required? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **New Client Portal UI** | Provides the currently supported Client Portal Appointments experience. | Yes |
| **Appointments App Permission** | Controls whether Appointments appears in the Client Portal navigation. | Yes |
| **Client Portal Booking on a Calendar** | Controls whether that individual calendar appears as a booking option. | Yes, for each calendar |
| **Branded Client Portal App** | Branded-app support is not included in the current release. | Not currently supported |

Two-Part Setup

Enabling the Appointments child app does not automatically enable calendar booking. At least one individual calendar must also have **Client Portal booking** enabled.

## **View and Manage Appointments**

Appointment views help clients understand what is happening now, what is scheduled next, and what has already taken place. Clients can also open individual appointments to review meeting information and access the management actions allowed by the calendar's policies.

From **Appointments** in the Client Portal, clients can use **Today**, **Upcoming**, and **Past** to organize their meetings. A calendar view provides another way to locate appointments by date.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080525228/original/qqq_9YFew4gq9Hy6BelIW4UDfXtTSHBHVQ.png?1788971394)

**Screenshot:** Client Portal Appointments page showing the calendar view, Today/Upcoming/Past tabs, appointment cards, and More details links.

### **View Appointment Details and Available Actions**

Opening an appointment gives clients a focused view of the meeting information and any actions currently available. Cancellation and rescheduling options appear only when the appointment remains eligible under the calendar's configured policies.

1. Open **Appointments** from the Client Portal navigation.
2. Locate the appointment you want to review.
3. Click **More details**.
4. Review the appointment information.
5. If available, select **Cancel** or **Reschedule**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080525282/original/0cGLDz1m9ov8FthhQR4r6J4Xm9409PAvdg.png?1788971421)

Whether an appointment can be canceled or rescheduled depends on the cancellation and rescheduling rules configured for that calendar. For more information, see [Cancellation & Reschedule Policy (Booking Widget)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002738-cancellation-reschedule-policy-booking-widget-).

## **Book Appointments from the Client Portal**

The Client Portal booking flow lets clients choose from the calendars you make available and select an eligible date and time without leaving the portal. Existing contact information is automatically filled where available, while the selected calendar continues to determine which dates and times can be booked.

1. Open **Appointments** in the Client Portal.
2. Click **Book Appointment**.
3. Select an available calendar.
4. Select an available date.
5. Choose an available time.
6. Complete the booking.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080525340/original/Z0DyFwUzuPOCTxVAfPeXD1S7Z8DeRPbJxA.png?1788971442)

The dates and times shown to the client are determined by the selected calendar's availability and scheduling rules. Office hours, slot duration, minimum scheduling notice, buffers, appointment limits, existing bookings, and connected-calendar conflicts can affect which time slots appear.

For more information, see [Adjusting Availability Settings for Individual Calendars](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001155718).

## **Use Multiple Calendars for Client Portal Booking**

Enabling multiple calendars gives clients a choice of booking options while allowing you to control exactly which calendars appear in the Client Portal. This is useful when separate calendars represent different appointment types, departments, locations, or team members.

**Client Portal booking is enabled individually for each calendar.** You can enable one calendar or repeat the configuration for each additional calendar clients should be able to select.

| Option | Purpose | Required for Multiple Client Portal Calendars? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Client Portal Calendar Selector** | Displays the individual calendars that have Client Portal booking enabled. | Yes |
| **Group Calendar** | Combines calendars into a separate grouped booking experience under a shared link. | No |

A Group Calendar is not required solely to expose several individual calendars through Client Portal Appointments. For more information about Group Calendars, see [HighLevel Group Calendar Overview and Setup Guide](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001161037-highlevel-group-calendar-overview).

## **How to Set Up Client Portal Appointments**

Client Portal Appointments requires configuration in both calendar settings and Client Portal App Permissions. App Permissions controls whether clients can access the Appointments app, while the individual calendar setting determines which calendars can be selected for new bookings.

**Complete both setup steps.** Enabling only the Appointments child app does not make a calendar available, and enabling only a calendar does not make the Appointments app visible.

### **Step 1: Enable Client Portal Booking for a Calendar**

Each calendar must be explicitly enabled for Client Portal booking before clients can select it. This lets you expose only the calendars appropriate for Client Portal users while keeping other calendars unavailable through this booking channel.

1. Go to **Calendars** and open **Calendar settings**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080525360/original/4Hlu9qVu7dSx77OJiiSz-RvgWFTC-6XgbA.gif?1788971461)

2. Under **Meetings → Calendars**, locate the calendar you want to make available.
3. Click the **Edit calendar** icon.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080525458/original/zcXDyWkEXx7ZFxkRVdyCFFJVft_HPAINZQ.png?1788971548)

4. In the calendar editor, expand **Advanced settings**.
5. Select **Booking channels**.
6. Turn on **Client Portal booking**.
7. Click **Save changes**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080525528/original/lG-JMQVf0wBx0UvHA0frdE19Y7KrTQ3WDw.png?1788971589)

Repeat these steps for every additional calendar clients should be able to select when booking through the Client Portal.

### **Step 2: Enable Appointments in Client Portal App Permissions**

Enabling the Appointments child app makes the appointment experience visible inside the Client Portal. App Permissions are configured at the sub-account level, so the selected child-app visibility applies to contacts using that sub-account's Client Portal.

1. Go to **Memberships**.
2. Open **Client Portal**.
3. Select **Settings**.
4. Open **App Permissions**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080525542/original/mnjZJ-E2lap5gbw2NVQ0GtQrcXyXIBOK0A.png?1788971616)

5. Locate **Appointments** in the child-app list.
6. Enable **Appointments**.
7. Click **Save Settings**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080525579/original/hVk_lHQtBAVXmfKv_RUaaUq9spsP5zs9FQ.png?1788971652)

**Important:** Enabling Appointments in App Permissions does not automatically make every calendar available for booking. Each calendar you want clients to select must also have **Client Portal booking** enabled under its Booking channels settings.

For more information about controlling Client Portal apps, see [App Permissions in Client Portal: Enabling/Disabling Child Apps and Authentication](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002136-app-permissions-in-client-portal-enabling-disabling-a-child-app).

## **Troubleshooting Client Portal Appointments**

Most Client Portal appointment issues are caused by one of the two required permissions, an individual calendar rule, or use of an unsupported portal experience. Compare the client's experience with the checks below before changing the calendar or recreating an appointment.

| Issue | What to Check |
| --- | --- |
| **Appointments does not appear in the portal** | Confirm the client is using the new Client Portal, Appointments is enabled in App Permissions, and the changes were saved. |
| **Appointments appears, but no calendars are available** | Enable Client Portal booking under Advanced settings → Booking channels for at least one individual calendar. |
| **A calendar appears, but a time slot is missing** | Review availability, scheduling notice, buffers, appointment limits, existing bookings, and connected-calendar conflicts. |
| **Cancel or Reschedule is unavailable** | Review whether the calendar permits the action and whether its cancellation or rescheduling restriction window has passed. |
| **The time-zone selector is missing** | Check whether Disable Contact Timezone is enabled for the sub-account. |
| **A recent permission change is not visible** | Confirm the change was saved, then have the client refresh the portal or sign out and sign back in. |

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

Q: Does enabling Appointments automatically make every calendar available?

No. Enabling Appointments makes the app visible, but each calendar must separately have **Client Portal booking** enabled under **Advanced settings → Booking channels**.

Q: Can I make only certain calendars available in the Client Portal?

Yes. Client Portal booking is enabled individually, allowing you to select exactly which calendars clients can choose from.

Q: Do I need to create a Group Calendar to show multiple calendars?

No. The Client Portal can display multiple individually enabled calendars through its calendar selector. Group Calendars are a separate grouped booking feature.

Q: Do the calendar's existing availability rules still apply?

Yes. The Client Portal booking flow uses the selected calendar's availability and scheduling rules when determining which dates and times clients can book.

Q: Can Appointments be enabled for only one client?

App Permissions are configured at the sub-account level. Enabling or disabling Appointments controls its visibility for contacts using that sub-account's Client Portal rather than for one individual contact.

Q: What happens if I disable the Appointments child app later?

Appointments is removed from the Client Portal experience, but the calendars and appointment records configured elsewhere in HighLevel are not deleted. You can re-enable the app later.

Q: Are Client Portal Appointments available in branded apps?

Not in the current release. Client Portal Appointments is currently available only in the new Client Portal UI.

Q: Can clients book services or use additional event-management features from this screen?

The current release covers standard calendar-based appointments. Service-menu booking and additional appointment-related event-management capabilities are outside the workflow documented in this article.

### **Related Articles**

[App Permissions in Client Portal: Enabling/Disabling Child Apps and Authentication](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002136-app-permissions-in-client-portal-enabling-disabling-a-child-app) [How to Set Up a Booking Calendar in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005061) [Cancellation & Reschedule Policy (Booking Widget)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002738-cancellation-reschedule-policy-booking-widget-) [Adjusting Availability Settings for Individual Calendars](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001155718) [Disable Contact Timezone - How to Remove Ability to Adjust Timezones When Scheduling](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48000982200-disable-contact-timezone-how-to-remove-ability-to-adjust-timezones-when-scheduling) [Unified Client Portal Experience](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008402-unified-client-portal-experience)

title_en: How to Use the Custom Fonts in the Email Builder ?
source_md:
Custom fonts can help your emails better match your brand, but font support varies across email clients. HighLevel provides native options for adding Google Fonts and using Brand Board fonts, while advanced users can use custom HTML or CSS when necessary. Because some email clients may replace unsupported fonts with a fallback, always test your email before sending.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Custom Fonts in the Email Builder?](#What-are-Custom-Fonts-in-the-Email-Builder?)
- [Key Benefits of Custom Fonts in Emails](#Key-Benefits-of-Custom-Fonts-in-Emails)
- [Choosing the Right Font Method](#Choosing-the-Right-Font-Method)
- [Email Client Limitations and Fallback Fonts](#Email-Client-Limitations-and-Fallback-Fonts)
- [Using Brand Fonts Across Emails](#Using-Brand-Fonts-Across-Emails)
- [Using Advanced Custom HTML or CSS](#Using-Advanced-Custom-HTML-or-CSS)
- [Font Hosting and Licensing Considerations](#Font-Hosting-and-Licensing-Considerations)
- [How to Add a Google Font in the Email Builder](#How-to-Add-a-Google-Font-in-the-Email-Builder)
- [Testing Custom Fonts Before Sending](#Testing-Custom-Fonts-Before-Sending)
- [Best Practices for Using Custom Fonts](#Best-Practices-for-Using-Custom-Fonts)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles%E2%80%8B)

---

# **What are Custom Fonts in the Email Builder?**

Custom fonts let you expand beyond the standard typography available in the Email Builder and apply fonts that better match your brand or campaign design.

HighLevel provides several ways to manage email typography:

- **Built-in fonts:** Fonts already available in the Email Builder.
- **Brand Fonts:** Fonts saved to the default Brand Board and made available in the Email Builder font picker.
- **Google Fonts:** Fonts you can add directly from the Email Builder using the **Add fonts** option.
- **Advanced custom styling:** Custom HTML or CSS added through the Code Element when native font options do not meet your needs. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002353-how-to-add-google-fonts-in-email-templates-and-campaigns))

Custom fonts should be treated as an enhancement rather than a guaranteed experience. Some email clients do not 

load external fonts and will display a fallback font instead.

---

## **Key Benefits of Custom Fonts in Emails**

Using brand-aligned typography can help create a more consistent visual experience while still allowing email clients to fall back to supported fonts when necessary.

- **Brand consistency:** Use typography that matches your website, funnels, and other branded materials.
- **More design flexibility:** Expand beyond the standard fonts available in the Email Builder.
- **Reusable brand styling:** Access Brand Board fonts directly from the Email Builder when a default Brand Board is configured.
- **Native Google Font support:** Add supported Google Fonts without manually writing CSS.
- **Fallback support:** Maintain readable email content when a recipient's email client does not display the preferred font.

---

## **Choosing the Right Font Method**

HighLevel offers multiple ways to manage typography in emails. Starting with the simplest supported option reduces unnecessary custom code and makes emails easier to maintain.  
  
**Built-In Fonts**

Built-in fonts are the simplest option because they are available directly from the Email Builder's text formatting controls.

Use a built-in font when:

- Maximum compatibility is the priority.
- Exact brand typography is not required.
- You want to minimize rendering differences between email clients.

**Brand Board Fonts**

Brand Boards let you store brand colors, fonts, and logos so they can be accessed while designing emails. Fonts from the **default Brand Board** appear in the Email Builder under **Brand Fonts**. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003137-how-to-use-brand-boards-in-email-campaign-templates))

Brand Fonts are useful when your team wants to reuse approved typography across email templates and campaigns.

To apply a Brand Font:

1. Open the email in the Design Editor.
2. Select the text you want to customize.
3. Open the **Font** dropdown.
4. Select the desired font under **Brand Fonts**. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003137-how-to-use-brand-boards-in-email-campaign-templates))

**Google Fonts**

Google Fonts can be added directly from the Email Builder without manually creating an `@font-face` rule.

To add a Google Font:

1. Open an email campaign or template in the Email Builder.
2. Select a text element.
3. Open the **Font** selector.
4. Click **Add fonts**.
5. Select the Google Font you want to add.
6. Click **Add font**.
7. Select the newly added font from the font dropdown. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002353-how-to-add-google-fonts-in-email-templates-and-campaigns))

Once added, the font becomes available in the builder's font selector. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002353-how-to-add-google-fonts-in-email-templates-and-campaigns))

---

## **Email Client Limitations and Fallback Fonts**

Email clients do not all render custom fonts the same way. Planning for fallback behavior ensures your message remains readable even when the preferred font cannot be displayed.

HighLevel notes that Google Fonts may not work consistently in clients such as:

- Gmail
- Outlook on several platforms
- Outlook.com
- Yahoo Mail ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002353-how-to-add-google-fonts-in-email-templates-and-campaigns))

When the preferred font is unavailable, the email client can display an alternative font instead.

For that reason, choose a fallback font that:

- Has similar proportions to the preferred font.
- Uses a similar weight.
- Remains easy to read.
- Does not significantly change the layout when substituted.

For example, a conceptual font stack could use:

`Brand Font → Helvetica → Arial → sans-serif`

The exact font shown to the recipient depends on what the email client supports.

---

## **Using Brand Fonts Across Emails**

Brand Board fonts make it easier to keep typography consistent across multiple templates and campaigns. They are available from the Email Builder when the appropriate Brand Board is set as the default.

Only fonts from the **default Brand Board** appear in the Email Builder's Brand Fonts list. If the expected fonts do not appear, confirm that the correct Brand Board is set as the default. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003137-how-to-use-brand-boards-in-email-campaign-templates))

Changing the typography saved in a Brand Board does not mean that previously designed email content will automatically be restyled. Existing text should be reviewed and updated as needed when brand typography changes.

---

## **Using Advanced Custom HTML or CSS**

The Code Element provides an advanced option for adding custom HTML or CSS when the standard Email Builder controls do not support a specific design requirement. Because email clients have limited support for custom code, this approach should be used carefully.

The **Code Element** is a drag-and-drop element that lets advanced users add custom HTML or CSS to an email. HighLevel recommends testing any custom code before sending because rendering can differ between email clients. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006827-code-element-in-email-builder))

To add a Code Element:

1. Go to **Marketing > Emails > Templates**.
2. Open an existing email template or create a new one.
3. Click the **Add Elements (+)** icon.
4. Drag the **Code** Element into the email.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155082203519/original/Bl89xPi0JXAUskNBTm8ob-xLefu5MiySeQ.png?1790770457)
5. Select the element to open its editing controls.
6. Add the required HTML or CSS.
7. Preview and test the email before sending. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006827-code-element-in-email-builder))

Custom code should be kept self-contained wherever possible so it does not unintentionally affect other email elements.

---

## **Font Hosting and Licensing Considerations**

Using a custom typeface requires both technical compatibility and the appropriate rights to use the font in an email or web environment. A font that is licensed for desktop use is not necessarily licensed for web or email embedding.

Before using a non-standard font:

- Review the font's license.
- Confirm that your intended email or web use is permitted.
- Use approved hosting methods required by the font provider.
- Avoid distributing licensed font files unless the license explicitly allows it.

HighLevel's current Email Builder documentation provides native workflows for Google Fonts and Brand Fonts. Direct custom-font file upload capabilities available in other HighLevel products, such as Funnels and Websites, should not 

be assumed to work the same way in the Email Builder.

---

## **How to Add a Google Font in the Email Builder**

Using the native Google Fonts option is the recommended workflow when the required font is available through the Email Builder. It avoids the additional complexity of manually writing font-loading CSS.

1. Navigate to **Marketing > Emails**.
2. Open an existing email campaign or template, or create a new one.
3. Select the **Text Element** containing the text you want to customize.
4. Open the **Font** selector.
5. Click **Add fonts**. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002353-how-to-add-google-fonts-in-email-templates-and-campaigns))
6. Select the required Google Font from the available options.
7. Click **Add font**.
8. Return to the font selector and apply the font to the selected text.
9. Review the email in desktop and mobile preview modes.
10. Send a test email and confirm how the typography appears in the email clients most relevant to your audience.

---

## **Testing Custom Fonts Before Sending**

Testing helps you confirm both the preferred-font experience and the fallback experience before recipients receive the campaign. Email previews are useful, but a real test send is also important because individual email clients can render HTML and CSS differently.

Before sending your campaign, verify:

- The preferred font appears where supported.
- Fallback text remains readable where the custom font is unavailable.
- Headings do not wrap unexpectedly.
- Buttons and CTA text still fit their containers.
- Mobile layouts remain readable.
- Font weight and size remain visually appropriate.
- Custom Code Elements do not affect surrounding sections.
- The email looks acceptable even when the custom font fails to load.

HighLevel recommends previewing and testing custom-code email content because email clients have varying levels of HTML and CSS support. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006827-code-element-in-email-builder))

---

## **Best Practices for Using Custom Fonts**

Custom typography works best when brand consistency is balanced with readability and email-client compatibility. A simple font strategy usually produces more predictable results.

- Use built-in, Brand Board, or native Google Font options before using custom code.
- Always plan for a fallback font.
- Use decorative fonts primarily for headings or short text.
- Keep body text easy to read.
- Avoid relying on a custom font to communicate important meaning.
- Test desktop and mobile layouts.
- Send test emails to multiple email clients before launching important campaigns.
- Keep custom CSS limited and targeted when using the Code Element.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can I add Google Fonts without writing custom CSS?**

Yes. Select a text element, open the Font selector, click **Add fonts**, choose the Google Font, and save it. The font will then be available in the builder's font selector. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002353-how-to-add-google-fonts-in-email-templates-and-campaigns))

**Q: Why does my custom font look different in Gmail or Outlook?**

Some email clients do not consistently load Google Fonts or other external fonts. In those cases, the recipient may see a fallback font instead. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002353-how-to-add-google-fonts-in-email-templates-and-campaigns))

**Q: Can I use Brand Board fonts in email campaigns?**

Yes. Fonts from the default Brand Board are available from the Email Builder under **Brand Fonts**. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003137-how-to-use-brand-boards-in-email-campaign-templates))

**Q: Why don't I see my Brand Board font in the Email Builder?**

Only fonts from the current default Brand Board appear in the Email Builder's Brand Fonts list. Confirm that the correct Brand Board is set as the default. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003137-how-to-use-brand-boards-in-email-campaign-templates))

**Q: Will changing a Brand Board font automatically update my existing emails?**

Do not assume existing email content will automatically be restyled. Review previously designed emails and apply the new font where needed.

**Q: Do I need a fallback font?**

Yes. Some email clients may not display the preferred custom font, so a readable fallback helps preserve the design and readability of the message.

**Q: Can I use custom HTML or CSS for fonts?**

Yes, advanced users can add custom HTML or CSS through the Code Element. Email-client support varies, so test the email before sending. ([help.gohighlevel.com](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006827-code-element-in-email-builder))

**Q: Can I upload a font file directly into the Email Builder?**

Current HighLevel Email Builder documentation provides native options for built-in fonts, Brand Fonts, and Google Fonts, along with custom HTML/CSS through the Code Element. Do not assume that direct font-file upload options available in Funnels or Websites are available in the Email Builder.

**Q: Should I use a custom font for body text?**

You can, but the email should remain readable when a fallback font is displayed. For critical body content, prioritize readability and predictable rendering over exact typography.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Add Google Fonts in Email Templates and Campaigns](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002353-how-to-add-google-fonts-in-email-templates-and-campaigns)
- [Code Element in Email Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006827-code-element-in-email-builder)
- [How to Use HighLevel Email Builder & In-line Editor](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000087)
- [How to Use Brand Boards in Email Campaign/Templates](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003137-how-to-use-brand-boards-in-email-campaign-templates)
- [How to Create a Brand Board in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003136-how-to-create-a-brand-board-)
- [Text Element in Email Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006820-text-element-in-email-builder)

title_en: Restaurant Website: How to Customize and Publish Your Site
source_md:
Restaurant Website lets you create a branded website where guests can order pickup or delivery and reserve a table. Your website uses your existing restaurant details, menu, and settings, so you can focus on customizing its appearance and making it your own. This article explains how to edit your pages, configure your website settings, track visitor activity, and publish your website.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Is Restaurant Website?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-Is-Restaurant-Website?)
- [Key Benefits of Restaurant Website](#Key-Benefits-of-Restaurant-Website)
- [Accessing Restaurant Website and the Dashboard](#Accessing-Restaurant-Website-and-the-Dashboard)
- [Customize Your Restaurant Website Pages](#Customize-Your-Restaurant-Website-Pages)
- [Customize Your Website Design](#Customize-Your-Website-Design)
- [Configure Website Setup, Domain, and Tracking](#Configure-Website-Setup,-Domain,-and-Tracking)
- [How to Preview and Publish Restaurant Website](#How-to-Preview-and-Publish-Restaurant-Website)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Is Restaurant Website?**

Restaurant Website is a built-in website solution in HighLevel that helps restaurants manage their online presence without building a website from scratch. It connects your menu, restaurant details, ordering options, and reservations to a customizable website.

Restaurant Website includes three main tabs:

| Tab | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Dashboard | See whether pickup, delivery and reservations are ready, see how your website is doing, and preview or publish it. |
| Restaurant pages | Edit every page guests see, with a live preview, and choose your template, colors and fonts. |
| Setup and sharing | Choose the page your web address opens on, how guests sign in, your contact details, your web address, how links look when shared, and tracking. |

---

## **Key Benefits of Restaurant Website**

Restaurant Website helps you create a consistent online experience while keeping your restaurant's website connected to the information you already manage in HighLevel.

- Ready from day one: Your website uses the menu, hours, address and brand you already added, so it is ready to preview right after setup.
- Orders and bookings in one place: Guests order pickup or delivery and book a table on the same website.
- Edit with a live preview: Turn sections on or off, reorder them and change the text, and see each change as you make it.
- Your brand, your way: Choose a template, your color, light or dark mode, spacing, corners and fonts.
- Your own domain: Use the free web address, or connect a domain you own.

---

## **Accessing Restaurant Website and the Dashboard**

The Restaurant Website dashboard provides an overview of your website's readiness and performance. Before accessing it, complete Restaurant Setup, including your restaurant details, menu, payment provider, and relevant pickup, delivery, and reservation settings.

To access Restaurant Website:

1. Navigate to Restaurants from the left navigation menu.
2. Select Restaurant Website.
3. The Dashboard tab opens automatically.

![Click Restaurants, then Restaurant Website.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084913168/original/Rwcf6XfNjw85jRVbUde6B9-kl1c5oyyQ1A.png?1793783552 "Click Restaurants, then Restaurant Website.")

The dashboard contains the following information:

- Setup complete: Click Preview website to check your website, or Publish website to make it live.
- Ways guests order and book: Pickup, Delivery and Reservations each show whether they are ready. Click Pickup settings, Delivery settings or Reservation settings to change them.
- How your website is doing: Choose Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days or Custom to see your online Orders, Net sales and Online reservations, with a chart for each day.

![The dashboard after setup, with ways guests order and book, and how your website is doing.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084913192/original/_VAwrmim6YQUfJ96z2JFVb3em9ArH4T2bA.png?1793783566 "The dashboard after setup, with ways guests order and book, and how your website is doing.")

```
Tip: Select the arrow next to Restaurant Website in the navigation panel to access its tabs directly. The dashboard also opens automatically after completing Restaurant Setup.
```

---

## **Customize Your Restaurant Website Pages**

The Restaurant pages editor lets you manage the content visitors see on your website. Changes appear in a live preview, allowing you to review the layout while customizing each page.

Your website includes the following pages:

| Page | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Home | The page a guest lands on. It can show your best dishes, categories, photos, hours and location. |
| Menu page, Cart drawer, Checkout, and Order confirmation | Browse your menu, add items to the cart, check the order and pay, then see the order confirmation. |
| Reservations page, Booking page, Booking confirmation, and Manage reservation | Choose a time, book a table, see the confirmation, and change or cancel the booking later. |
| Sign-in page | Sign in with their email and a 6-digit code. |
| Dine-in menu | Look at your menu at the table after they scan the code on their table. Your team takes their order. |

**![The pages on your restaurant website.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084913707/original/SxYB_6NaBS4QDWUB4zW9XhPVxIWdKcVE9w.png?1793783778 "The pages on your restaurant website.")**

### 

### **Edit Website Pages**

The page editor separates content editing from the live preview, helping you update individual pages without changing your restaurant's underlying menu configuration.

1. Click the Restaurant pages tab.
2. In the list on the left, click the page you want to edit, for example Home.
3. Make your changes. The preview on the right shows them as you go.

![Restaurant pages: choose a page on the left, edit its sections in the middle and check the live preview on the right.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084913816/original/QvU97weLi3yq78rzbAVHzKxKmscaUW4Vyg.png?1793783811 "Restaurant pages: choose a page on the left, edit its sections in the middle and check the live preview on the right.")

For the Home page, you can customize these sections:

- Hero banner: The first thing guests see, with your name, a short line of text, buttons and a photo.
- Featured items and Featured categories: Dishes and categories from your menu.
- Text and image and Image gallery: Your story and photos.
- Order Now band: A strip that sends guests to order.
- Hours and location: Your address, phone, opening hours and directions.

Select any section to edit its content. You can also:

- Drag sections to change their order.
- Toggle sections on or off to control visibility.
- Click Add section to include more content.
- Select Remove section to delete an existing section.

For the Hero banner, you can update the heading, text, Order and Book buttons, and image. Leaving the Book button field empty hides that button.

Supported image formats include PNG, JPG, GIF, and WEBP, with a maximum file size of 5 MB. A resolution of 2160 × 1080 pixels is recommended.

![The Hero banner section, open for editing.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084913948/original/ycSyabHQk1AfNv8VQyek5EhXUYNAMAvcSQ.png?1793783863 "The Hero banner section, open for editing.")

Other pages have their own editable options. For example, you can modify the Sign-in page title or the Checkout page text and tip settings.

Use Header & navigation and Footer under Every page to update elements shared across your website.

Note: Menu items, prices, and categories are managed separately under Restaurants → Menu. Their visibility may depend on menu availability and ordering channel settings.

---

## **Customize Your Website Design**

Website styles control the visual appearance of your pages. Choosing a consistent design helps keep your restaurant's branding recognizable throughout the ordering and reservation experience.

Navigate to Restaurant pages → Design → Style to configure:

| Setting | Available options |
| --- | --- |
| Template | Classic, Modern, or Bold |
| Primary color | Choose your brand's primary color, initially derived from your logo. |
| Page mode | Light, Dark, or Auto |
| Density | Compact, Comfortable, or Spacious |
| Corners | Sharp, Soft, or Rounded |
| Fonts | Preset font pairings, such as Modern sans, Editorial, or Classic, or individually selected heading and body fonts. |

The templates have different layouts: Classic positions the image beside the title, Modern places the title over the image, and Bold uses larger text with an inset image.

![Style: choose your template, primary color and page mode. Density, corners and fonts are further down.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084914077/original/EuoWCFkMzwyNNYcs4N_vCHg-QIPmWIu-fA.png?1793783918 "Style: choose your template, primary color and page mode. Density, corners and fonts are further down.")

---

## **Configure Website Setup, Domain, and Tracking**

The Setup and sharing tab controls how guests access your website, how your website appears when shared, and how supported visitor actions are tracked.

### **Landing Page, Guest Sign-In, and Contact Information**

These settings determine which page guests see first, how they sign in during checkout, and where they find your restaurant's support information.

1. Navigate to Setup and sharing → Setup.
2. Under Landing page, select the page visitors should see when opening your website address.
3. Review the Sign-in settings. Guests sign in using a one-time code sent to their email, and their saved details make future checkouts faster.
4. Under Contact and footer, enter your Support email and Copyright line.
5. Click Save changes.

You can use {{name}} and {{year}} in the copyright line to keep the restaurant name and year updated automatically.

```
Note: Under When guests check out, Require it is currently the available option. Never ask and Offer it are marked Coming soon.
```

**![Setup: choose your landing page, how guests sign in, and your contact details.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084938898/original/z2fglsIbiwLXTw752YVnJAo9jFsS57_Uxg.png?1793795600 "Setup: choose your landing page, how guests sign in, and your contact details.")**

### **Domain and SEO Settings**

Domain and SEO settings control your website address and how your restaurant website appears in browser tabs and shared links.

1. Navigate to Setup and sharing → Link and SEO.
2. Under Web Address, configure either:
   - Subdomain: Edit the first part of your free website address, which ends in .app.clientclub.net. Use the copy icon to copy the full address.
   - Custom domain: Enter a domain you own and click Add domain.
3. Under Search and Sharing, configure:
   - Website title: The title displayed in browser tabs and shared links, up to 70 characters.
   - Share image: The image shown when your website link is shared. Your logo is used by default until you replace it.
   - Favicon: The icon displayed in the browser tab. Your logo is used by default.
4. Click Save changes.

**![Link and SEO: your web address, your website title and the image shown when your link is shared.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084939187/original/BKTopgwLi1gdNUPvevEvhjJZv_UA_fEuwA.png?1793795683 "Link and SEO: your web address, your website title and the image shown when your link is shared.")**

### **Meta Pixel Tracking**

Meta Pixel tracking helps you measure supported visitor interactions on your published restaurant website. Event mapping connects website actions to Meta events for reporting and campaign measurement.

To configure tracking:

1. **Click the Setup and sharing tab, then Tracking.**
2. **Enter your Meta Pixel ID. You can find it in Meta Events Manager under Data sources.**
3. **Check the Event mapping. It shows which Meta event is sent when guests view a page, view or add a dish, start checkout, enter payment details, complete an order, start a booking, pay a deposit or complete a booking.**
4. **Click Save changes.**

**![Enter your Meta Pixel ID. The event mapping shows which Meta event each guest action sends.](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084939337/original/eLz_H3maaKVhidzPlgkreuLlrCyw0DRUtw.png?1793795762 "Enter your Meta Pixel ID. The event mapping shows which Meta event each guest action sends.")**

```
Important: Enter your Pixel ID only in the dedicated Tracking settings, not in Custom code, to avoid duplicate tracking. Events are sent from the published website, not from the editor.
```

---

## **How to Preview and Publish Restaurant Website**

Previewing your website before publishing helps you confirm that guests can navigate the pages, view your menu, and access the ordering and reservation options you have configured.

1. **Click Preview in Restaurant pages, or Preview website on the dashboard, and check every page as a guest would.**
2. **If you made changes, save them first. Publish website asks you to save your changes before it publishes.**
3. **Click Publish website.**

Once published, guests can access the website to place pickup and delivery orders or make reservations, based on your configured services.

Publishing also removes the Ordering off state in Restaurant Orders and makes online reservations available through your website.

```
Important: Before publishing, review Restaurant Settings → Checkout and payments and make sure Live mode is enabled to accept real orders and payments.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need a website to take orders?**

Guests need your website to order pickup and delivery and to book a table online. Your team can take dine-in orders and book tables without it.

**Q: Where does my website get my menu and hours?**

From [Menu](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ddwMlOYygDii3i-qQIL2CJZKcnSgJ_UJSIl_lS7YVgw/edit#bookmark=id.vxpuh5x5bxcn) and [Restaurant Settings](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ddwMlOYygDii3i-qQIL2CJZKcnSgJ_UJSIl_lS7YVgw/edit#bookmark=id.s9ml0565nml1) > Restaurant details. Change them there, and your website shows the change.

**Q: Can I use my own domain?**

Yes. In Setup and sharing > Link and SEO, enter your domain under Custom domain and click Add domain.

**Q: How do guests sign in?**

With their email. They get a one-time 6-digit code, and their details are saved so they check out faster next time.

**Q: How do I hide a section on my home page?**

In Restaurant pages > Home, switch the section off.

**Q: Why does Publish website ask me to save first?**

You have changes that are not saved yet. Save them, then publish.

---
