title_en: How to Use Hubspot Workflow Actions & Triggers in HighLevel
source_md:
[동영상](https://www.youtube.com/embed/UPKkCtqoZA0?&wmode=opaque)

Connect HubSpot directly to HighLevel Workflows so your CRM stays clean, synchronized, and responsive in real time. This guide explains the HubSpot workflow trigger and actions, how to set them up, and practical ways to use them for contact sync, deduplication, and lifecycle-based nurturing.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is HubSpot Workflow Actions & Triggers?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-is-HubSpot-Workflow-Actions-&-Triggers?)
- [Key Benefits of HubSpot Workflow Actions & Triggers](#Key-Benefits-of-HubSpot-Workflow-Actions-&-Triggers)
- [Supported HubSpot Trigger](#Supported-HubSpot-Trigger)
- [Supported HubSpot Actions](#Supported-HubSpot-Actions)
- [How To Set Up HubSpot Workflow Actions & Triggers](#How-To-Set-Up-HubSpot-Workflow-Actions-&-Triggers)
- [Setting Up the HubSpot New Contact Created Trigger](#Setting-Up-the-HubSpot-New-Contact-Created-Trigger)
- [Setting  Up the HubSpot Create Contact Action](#Setting-%C2%A0Up-the-HubSpot-Create-Contact-Action)
- [Common Use Cases](#Common-Use-Cases)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions%C2%A0)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is HubSpot Workflow Actions & Triggers?**

HubSpot Workflow Actions & Triggers allow you to connect HubSpot with HighLevel workflows so data can move between both systems through automation. This helps teams create HubSpot contacts, find existing HubSpot contacts, and start HighLevel workflows when new HubSpot contacts are created. By using HubSpot inside Workflow Builder, you can reduce manual data entry, prevent duplicate contacts, and keep sales or marketing processes moving more consistently.

HubSpot actions and triggers are available inside HighLevel Workflow Builder. A trigger starts the workflow when a specific HubSpot event occurs, while actions perform tasks in HubSpot after the workflow begins.

---

## **Key Benefits of HubSpot Workflow Actions & Triggers**

HubSpot workflow automation helps teams connect contact activity across systems without manually copying information from one CRM to another. These benefits are especially useful when HighLevel is used for marketing automation, lead capture, or customer communication while HubSpot is used for CRM management.

- **Automated contact creation:** Create HubSpot contacts from HighLevel workflow events such as form submissions, appointments, tags, or other workflow triggers.

- **Reduced duplicate records:** Search for an existing HubSpot contact before creating a new one to help keep HubSpot contact records clean.

- **Faster lead routing:** Trigger follow-up workflows in HighLevel when a new HubSpot contact is created.

- **Flexible field mapping:** Send standard and custom contact information from HighLevel into HubSpot contact properties.

- **Improved workflow consistency:** Build repeatable automations that reduce manual steps for sales, marketing, and operations teams.

- **Better CRM coordination:** Keep HubSpot and HighLevel processes aligned when both platforms are part of your business workflow.

---

## **Supported HubSpot Trigger**

The HubSpot trigger starts a HighLevel workflow when a matching event happens in HubSpot. This allows HighLevel to respond automatically when new contact activity begins in HubSpot.

### **New Contact Created**

The **New Contact Created** trigger starts a HighLevel workflow when a new contact is created in the connected HubSpot account.

Use this trigger when you want HighLevel to take action after a new HubSpot contact is added, such as sending notifications, creating tasks, applying tags, or starting follow-up communication.

---

## **Supported HubSpot Actions**

HubSpot actions allow HighLevel workflows to send or retrieve contact information from HubSpot. These actions should be configured carefully so the correct contact data is mapped, searched, or created.

**Internal Review Note:** Confirm the exact supported action list before publishing. The existing article references five actions in some areas but only lists two actions in another section. The final article should only include actions that are currently available in production.

### 

### **Create Contact**

The **Create Contact** action creates a new contact in HubSpot using information mapped from the HighLevel workflow.

Use this action when a HighLevel event captures a new lead or customer and you want that person added to HubSpot automatically.

Common mapped fields may include:

- First name
- Last name
- Email
- Phone
- Company name
- Website
- Lifecycle stage
- Lead source
- Custom HubSpot properties

```
Tip: Use a Find Contact action before Create Contact to check whether the contact already exists in HubSpot.
```

### 

### **Find Contact**

The **Find Contact** action searches HubSpot for an existing contact based on a selected identifier, such as email address.

Use this action before creating a new HubSpot contact so the workflow can check whether a matching contact already exists.

Common uses include:

- Preventing duplicate HubSpot contacts.
- Routing contacts differently when a match is found.
- Confirming whether a lead already exists in HubSpot before creating a record.
- Using workflow conditions based on whether the contact was found.

### 

### **Get Contact by ID**

The **Get Contact by ID** action retrieves a HubSpot contact using the contact’s HubSpot record ID.

Use this action when a previous workflow step already has the HubSpot contact ID and you need to retrieve more details about that contact.

Common uses include:

- Looking up contact data after a HubSpot trigger.
- Pulling HubSpot contact properties into later workflow steps.
- Verifying a specific HubSpot record before continuing the workflow.

### **Search Contact by Email**

The **Search Contact by Email** action searches HubSpot for a contact using the email address provided in the workflow.

Use this action when email is the most reliable way to identify whether a HubSpot contact already exists.

Common uses include:

- Matching HighLevel contacts to HubSpot contacts.
- Avoiding duplicate HubSpot records.
- Branching workflow logic based on whether an email match exists.

### 

### **Create Association**

The **Create Association** action creates a relationship between HubSpot records, such as associating a contact with a company or deal.

Use this action when your HubSpot workflow needs connected records to stay organized for sales or account management.

Common uses include:

- Associating a HubSpot contact with a company.
- Associating a HubSpot contact with a deal.
- Connecting related HubSpot records after a contact is created or found.

---

## **How To Set Up HubSpot Workflow Actions & Triggers**

A successful setup requires connecting HubSpot, selecting the correct trigger or action, mapping the right fields, and testing before publishing. Testing is especially important because it confirms that HighLevel can access HubSpot records and send data in the expected format.

### **Connect HubSpot in Workflow Builder**

1. Go to **Automation** in HighLevel.
2. Open an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
3. Click **Add New Trigger** or **Add Action**, depending on what you want to configure.
4. Select **Apps**.
5. Choose **HubSpot**.
6. Click **Connect** or **Connect Now**.
7. Authorize the HubSpot account you want to use.
8. Review the requested permissions.
9. Complete the authorization.
10. Return to HighLevel and confirm that HubSpot is connected.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072050244/original/lwYVqNwwW5u4fYPoA25WYFhOLm9ajxmS-g.png?1779530590)

## **Setting Up the HubSpot New Contact Created Trigger**

The New Contact Created trigger is useful when HubSpot is the starting point for a workflow. Once a new contact is created in HubSpot, HighLevel can continue the automation with follow-up actions, notifications, tasks, or internal processes.

1. Go to **Automation** in HighLevel.
2. Open the workflow where you want HubSpot to trigger the automation.
3. Click **Add New Trigger**.
4. Select **HubSpot**.
5. Choose **New Contact Created**.
6. Confirm the connected HubSpot account.
7. Configure any available trigger settings.
8. Click **Save Trigger**.
9. Use **Test Trigger** or **Find New Records** to confirm that HighLevel can detect HubSpot contact records.
10. Publish the workflow when testing is successful.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072050325/original/lPh6V0W9bX29EQV2d55QeGTOhqpmeJVoHA.png?1779530677)

## 

## **Setting  Up the HubSpot Create Contact Action**

The Create Contact action sends contact data from a HighLevel workflow into HubSpot. Accurate field mapping ensures that each HubSpot contact is created with the right name, email, phone number, and custom property values.

1. Open the workflow where you want to create a HubSpot contact.
2. Add the workflow trigger that should start the process.
3. Click **Add Action**.
4. Select **HubSpot**.
5. Choose **Create Contact**.
6. Confirm the connected HubSpot account.
7. Map the required HubSpot fields.
8. Map any optional HubSpot properties needed for your process.
9. Save the action.
10. Test the action.
11. Review the test result in HighLevel and confirm the contact was created in HubSpot.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072050394/original/QOAT2Iroh-iwUlMwvQkqqIqhO7OiLI0Txg.png?1779530760)

## 

## 

**Recommended field mapping example:**

- HubSpot First Name → HighLevel Contact First Name
- HubSpot Last Name → HighLevel Contact Last Name
- HubSpot Email → HighLevel Contact Email
- HubSpot Phone → HighLevel Contact Phone
- HubSpot Company → HighLevel Contact Company Name
- HubSpot Lead Source → Workflow source, form name, or custom value

---

## **Common Use Cases**

HubSpot workflow actions and triggers are useful when HubSpot and HighLevel are both part of the customer journey. These examples show how teams can automate contact creation, contact lookup, and follow-up processes.

### 

### **Create a HubSpot Contact from a HighLevel Form Submission**

Use this workflow when leads enter HighLevel through a form and need to be created in HubSpot.

Example workflow:

1. Trigger: Form Submitted.
2. Action: Search Contact by Email or Find Contact.
3. If/Else: Contact found?
4. If no, Create Contact in HubSpot.
5. If yes, continue with the next follow-up step.

### 

### **Start a HighLevel Workflow When a HubSpot Contact Is Created**

Use this workflow when HubSpot is the source of new contact creation and HighLevel should handle follow-up actions.

Example workflow:

1. Trigger: HubSpot New Contact Created.
2. Action: Send internal notification.
3. Action: Add tag in HighLevel.
4. Action: Create task or assign user.
5. Action: Send follow-up communication if appropriate.

### 

### **Prevent Duplicate Contacts in HubSpot**

Use this workflow when multiple lead sources may send the same person into HubSpot.

Example workflow:

1. Trigger: Contact Created, Form Submitted, or another HighLevel trigger.
2. Action: Search HubSpot by email.
3. If contact exists, skip Create Contact.
4. If contact does not exist, Create Contact.

### 

### **Associate a HubSpot Contact with a Company or Deal**

Use this workflow when a contact should be connected to another HubSpot record for account management or sales tracking.

Example workflow:

1. Trigger: Contact created or updated in HighLevel.
2. Action: Find or Create HubSpot Contact.
3. Action: Retrieve the company or deal record ID.
4. Action: Create Association.
5. Test the association inside HubSpot.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Are HubSpot actions premium workflow actions?**

Yes. All five HubSpot actions (Create Contact, Find Contact, Get Contact by ID, Search Contact by Email, Create Association) are premium and consume premium action credits at the standard automation rate.

**Q: Is the New Contact Created trigger premium too?**

No. The premium designation applies to the **actions**. The New Contact Created trigger is powered by a HubSpot webhook and can fire without consuming premium action credits, though any premium actions you add after it will still bill as usual.

**Q: Do I need a paid HubSpot plan to use this integration?**

No. The integration works with HubSpot’s free CRM tier. Some advanced features on the HubSpot side (like certain workflow automations or specialized property types) may require paid Marketing or Sales Hub plans, but those limits are set by HubSpot, not HighLevel.

**Q: How does deduplication work when creating HubSpot contacts?**

Email is the primary deduplication key for HubSpot contacts. To avoid duplicates, use **Search Contact by Email** before **Create Contact**, then only create a new record when no match is found.

**Q: Can I create or update custom properties on HubSpot contacts from a workflow?**

Yes. The Create Contact action supports any property defined on the HubSpot Contact object (standard or custom). Create the property in HubSpot first, then map the appropriate workflow variable to it. Unknown property names are ignored by HubSpot on submit.

**Q: What is Create Association used for in real workflows?**

Create Association links a contact to a Company, Deal, or Ticket in HubSpot. This is useful for account-based selling, deal automation, and support workflows where you want all related records connected and visible from both sides.

**Q: Can I use workflow variables in HubSpot fields?**

Yes. All HubSpot action fields support inline workflow variables (for example, `` or date/time helpers). This lets you dynamically map form responses, contact fields, or values from previous steps into HubSpot properties.

**Q: Will New Contact Created fire for contacts created by imports or other integrations?**

Yes. The trigger fires for any new contact created in HubSpot—via forms, manual entry, imports, or other integrations unless you restrict it with filters. Use trigger filters to narrow enrollment to specific sources or lifecycle stages if needed.

**Q: What happens if a HubSpot action fails (for example, due to an invalid email)?**

If an action like Create Contact fails, the error is logged in the workflow execution details. The workflow can continue based on your branching; for critical paths, add a fallback branch (for example, notify an admin or log to a Slack channel) when an error occurs.

**Q: Can I use multiple HubSpot steps in the same workflow?**

Yes. You can chain multiple HubSpot triggers and actions (where applicable) within a single workflow—for example, trigger on New Contact Created, then Find Contact in HighLevel, Create Contact in HighLevel, and finally Create Association back in HubSpot for that same contact.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Getting Started with Workflows](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000002288?portalId=48000045315)

- [Import Data from HubSpot (HubSpot Importer)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000007947?portalId=48000045315)

- [Hubspot to HighLevel (Migration Guide)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000003388?portalId=48000045315)

- [Workflow Action – Create Company or Associated Contact](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/155000006574?portalId=48000045315)

- [Workflow Action – Update Contact Field](https://help.gohighlevel.com/a/solutions/articles/48001214441?portalId=48000045315)

title_en: Getting Started - Launch an SMS Campaign
source_md:
HighLevel gives you multiple ways to send SMS messages based on how and when you want contacts to receive them. You can send a one-time Bulk SMS to a selected group of contacts or use Workflows to send automated messages when specific events occur. Understanding the difference between these methods helps you choose the right approach, control delivery timing, and monitor message performance.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are SMS Campaigns in HighLevel?](#%E2%80%8B%E2%80%8BWhat-Are-SMS-Campaigns-in-HighLevel?)
- [Key Benefits of SMS Campaigns](#Key-Benefits-of-SMS-Campaigns)
- [Bulk SMS vs. Workflow SMS](#Bulk-SMS-vs.-Workflow-SMS)
- [Before You Send an SMS Campaign](#Before-You-Send-an-SMS-Campaign)
- [How to Launch a Bulk SMS Campaign](#How-to-Launch-a-Bulk-SMS-Campaign)
- [Bulk SMS Delivery Options](#Bulk-SMS-Delivery-Options)
- [Create a Reusable SMS Snippet](#Create-a-Reusable-SMS-Snippet)
- [Monitor Your Bulk SMS Campaign](#Monitor-Your-Bulk-SMS-Campaign)
- [Automate SMS With a Workflow](#Automate-SMS-With-a-Workflow)
- [How to Set Up Your First SMS Campaign](#How-to-Set-Up-Your-First-SMS-Campaign)
  - [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
  - [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are SMS Campaigns in HighLevel?**

SMS campaigns in HighLevel let you communicate with contacts at scale through one-time bulk messages or automated workflow actions. Bulk SMS is useful when you want to send a message to a selected audience, while Workflow SMS is designed for event-based communication such as reminders, follow-ups, and nurture sequences.

HighLevel supports different SMS approaches depending on your goal:

- **Bulk SMS:** Send one message to a selected group of contacts.

- **Scheduled Bulk SMS:** Prepare a bulk message and send it at a future date and time.

- **Bulk SMS with Drip Mode:** Distribute a larger send across smaller batches over time.

- **Workflow SMS:** Send messages automatically when a contact meets defined trigger conditions.

---

## **Key Benefits of SMS Campaigns**

Choosing the right SMS sending method helps you communicate efficiently while matching delivery behavior to your business process. Bulk actions provide fast outreach to selected audiences, while workflows support ongoing, automated communication.

- **Targeted communication:** Send messages to selected groups of contacts based on your audience or campaign goal.

- **Flexible delivery:** Send immediately, schedule messages for later, or distribute larger sends with Drip Mode.

- **Automated follow-up:** Use Workflows to send SMS when contacts complete actions or meet specific conditions.

- **Reusable content:** Save commonly used messaging as snippets to speed up future sends.

- **Campaign visibility:** Review Bulk Action results to understand which messages were sent, delivered, failed, or skipped.

- **Scalable outreach:** Use bulk sends for one-time communication and Workflows for repeatable customer journeys.

---

## **Bulk SMS vs. Workflow SMS**

Bulk SMS and Workflow SMS can both send messages to contacts, but they are designed for different situations. Choosing the correct method before building your campaign makes setup simpler and prevents unnecessary automation.

### **Use Bulk SMS When**

Bulk SMS is best for a one-time message to a defined audience.

Examples include:

- Promotional announcements

- Event reminders

- Important customer updates

- One-time notices

- Offers sent to a selected contact segment

### 

### **Use Workflow SMS When**

Workflow SMS is better when the message should be sent automatically because something happened or a condition was met.

Examples include:

- A lead submits a form
- An appointment is booked
- A contact enters a follow-up sequence
- An opportunity changes stage
- A reminder needs to be sent after a delay
- A customer begins an onboarding process

### 

### **Quick Decision Guide**

- One message to a selected group: Use Bulk SMS.

- One message at a future time: Use scheduled Bulk SMS.

- Large audience with controlled pacing: Use Bulk SMS with Drip Mode.

- Message sent after an event or condition: Use Workflow SMS.

- Multi-step follow-up sequence: Use a Workflow.

---

## **Before You Send an SMS Campaign**

SMS readiness affects whether messages can be sent and delivered successfully. Confirming your sending setup and consent requirements before launching a campaign helps reduce skipped messages, delivery problems, and compliance issues.

Before sending SMS:

- Confirm that your sub-account has an eligible sending number configured.

- Make sure contacts have provided the appropriate consent to receive SMS messages.

- Review applicable messaging and carrier requirements for your region.

- Complete applicable A2P registration when sending application-to-person SMS using US 10DLC numbers.

- Avoid intentionally messaging contacts who have opted out or are marked DND for SMS.

- Review your message content, personalization, and intended audience before launching the send.

For more information about SMS messaging best practices, see [Guide To Bulk SMS: Send Messages People Actually Want To Receive](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002100).

For US 10DLC requirements, see [A2P Campaign Registration Guide](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004539).

---

## **How to Launch a Bulk SMS Campaign**

Bulk SMS lets you select contacts and send a message to that audience without building a Workflow. This is useful for announcements or other one-time communications where the recipients are already known.

- Go to Contacts.
- Select the contacts you want to message.
- Choose the Send SMS Bulk Action.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079173009/original/RDryoDzP4nX6wNk7BWp_gzpdI6sbBIM5kQ.png?1787580020)

- Select the sending phone number when required.
- Enter your SMS message or insert reusable content if available.
- Review the recipients and message.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079173096/original/JQoihYlN-m29UwKsWWy3h5DtIBoIejATuQ.png?1787580100)

- Choose how the message should be delivered:

  - Send immediately
  - Schedule for later
  - Use Drip Mode

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079173305/original/KeoGykJwPY8V-bsCf9Ietcb_nUVD2zm_Zw.png?1787580159)

- Configure any additional delivery settings.
- Review the campaign before confirming the send.

HighLevel excludes contacts from supported bulk sends when they are not eligible to receive the message, such as contacts with applicable SMS opt-out or DND restrictions.

For a broader SMS setup guide, see [Getting Started - Setup Email, Phone, and SMS](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005058).

---

## **Bulk SMS Delivery Options**

Delivery options determine when and how quickly your Bulk SMS is processed. Selecting the right option helps you match the campaign to your audience size and timing requirements.

### **Send Now**

Use Send Now when the entire eligible audience should begin receiving the message immediately.

This is appropriate for:

- Time-sensitive announcements

- Small or moderate contact groups

- Messages that do not require future scheduling

### **Schedule**

Use the scheduling option when you want the campaign to begin at a specific future date or time.

This is useful for:

- Planned promotions

- Event notifications

- Messages prepared ahead of time

### 

### **Drip Mode**

Drip Mode breaks a large Bulk Action into smaller batches and processes those batches over time. This can help you control how quickly a large audience enters the send.

Drip Mode settings can include:

- Start On: When the bulk action should begin.

- Batch Quantity: How many contacts should be processed in each batch.

- Repeat After: How long HighLevel should wait before processing the next batch.

For detailed Drip Mode configuration, see [Set Up Drip Mode for Bulk Actions in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006472-new-drip-mode-architecture-for-bulk-actions).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079173669/original/1782PKtCPCamONch4PJq_tSw2aSboXRaRQ.gif?1787580329)

---

## **Create a Reusable SMS Snippet**

SMS snippets let you save message content that your team sends repeatedly. They are optional, but they can reduce repetitive typing and help keep commonly used messages consistent.

To create a reusable SMS snippet:

1. Go to Marketing > Snippets.
2. Create a new text snippet.
3. Enter a recognizable name for the snippet.
4. Add the SMS content you want to reuse.
5. Add supported personalization where appropriate.
6. Save the snippet.

You do not need to create a snippet before every SMS campaign. Use snippets when the same or similar content is likely to be used repeatedly.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079173845/original/kMLa-DhPikkVWOZtWZcSsiUPUQF8f9bfCQ.png?1787580446)

---

## **Monitor Your Bulk SMS Campaign**

Monitoring a Bulk SMS campaign helps you understand how the send progressed and identify contacts whose messages were not processed successfully. HighLevel provides Bulk Action reporting so you can review the campaign after launch.

To review a Bulk SMS campaign:

1. Go to Contacts.
2. Open Bulk Actions.
3. Locate the SMS Bulk Action you want to review.
4. Open the available campaign details or Show Stats option.
5. Review the available delivery results.

Depending on the campaign and processing status, reporting can include:

- Sent
- Delivered
- Failed
- Skipped

Failure or skipped-message information can help you determine whether a contact was ineligible, whether carrier delivery failed, or whether another messaging restriction affected the send.

Messages that have already been sent cannot be changed retroactively. Available controls for pending Bulk Actions depend on the current campaign status and delivery method.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155079173941/original/_FXKX_qxYgCdxPv-EjOVr8M5TiVM4ral0Q.png?1787580518)

---

## **Automate SMS With a Workflow**

Workflow SMS is designed for messages that should be sent automatically when a contact enters a defined process. Unlike Bulk SMS, the recipients do not have to be manually selected each time because the Workflow trigger determines who enters the automation.

To create an automated SMS process:

1. Go to Automation > Workflows.
2. Create a new Workflow or open an existing one.
3. Choose the trigger that should start the automation.
4. Add the Send SMS action.
5. Enter the message you want to send.
6. Add supported personalization or reusable content where appropriate.
7. Add Wait steps, conditions, or additional actions when needed.
8. Test the Workflow and SMS content.
9. Publish the Workflow when it is ready to run.

The Workflow trigger depends on your business goal. For example, you could send an SMS after a form submission, appointment booking, opportunity update, or another supported event.

For more information about the SMS action, see [Workflow Action - Send SMS](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002474-workflow-action-send-sms).

For a broader introduction to Workflow automation, see [Getting Started with Workflows in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002288).

---

## **How to Set Up Your First SMS Campaign**

A successful SMS campaign starts by choosing the correct sending method and confirming that your messaging setup is ready. Following a consistent preparation process helps you avoid building an unnecessary Workflow for a one-time campaign or using Bulk SMS for a communication that should be automated.

1. Identify the purpose of the message.
2. Determine whether the message is a one-time send or an automated follow-up.
3. Confirm that your SMS sending number and applicable registration are ready.
4. Confirm that the intended recipients are eligible to receive SMS messages.
5. Prepare your message content.
6. Choose your sending method:

   - Bulk SMS for a selected audience
   - Workflow SMS for automated communication
7. If using Bulk SMS, decide whether to send immediately, schedule the send, or use Drip Mode.
8. If using a Workflow, select the correct trigger and configure the Send SMS action.
9. Review the message and audience before launch.
10. Monitor the Bulk Action results or Workflow activity after sending.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What is the difference between Bulk SMS and Workflow SMS?**

Bulk SMS sends a message to contacts you select for a specific campaign. Workflow SMS sends automatically when a contact meets the Workflow's trigger and conditions.

**Q: Can I schedule a Bulk SMS for later?**

Yes. Bulk SMS includes supported delivery options that allow you to schedule a send for a future time instead of launching it immediately.

**Q: What is Drip Mode?**

Drip Mode processes a Bulk Action in smaller batches over time. You can configure when it begins, how many contacts are included in each batch, and how long HighLevel waits before starting the next batch.

**Q: Do I need to create an SMS snippet before sending?**

No. Snippets are optional. They are useful when you want to reuse standardized SMS content across multiple sends.

**Q: Why were some contacts skipped in my Bulk SMS campaign?**

Contacts may be skipped when they are not eligible to receive the message, such as when applicable SMS opt-out or DND restrictions are present. Review the Bulk Action statistics for available details.

**Q: Can I pause or cancel a Bulk SMS campaign?**

Available controls depend on the campaign status and delivery configuration. Review the options available for the specific Bulk Action. Messages that have already been sent cannot be recalled or edited.

**Q: Can a Workflow send SMS automatically after a form is submitted?**

Yes. Form Submitted can be used as a Workflow trigger, but it is only one example. You can use other supported triggers depending on when the SMS should be sent.

**Q: Do I need A2P registration to send SMS?**

A2P requirements depend on the type of number, messaging traffic, and region. Businesses sending application-to-person SMS using US 10DLC numbers should review and complete the applicable A2P registration requirements before sending campaigns.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Getting Started - Setup Email, Phone, and SMS](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005058)
- [Workflow Action - Send SMS](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002474-workflow-action-send-sms)
- [Set Up Drip Mode for Bulk Actions in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006472-new-drip-mode-architecture-for-bulk-actions)
- [Guide To Bulk SMS: Send Messages People Actually Want To Receive](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002100)
- [A2P Campaign Registration Guide](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004539)
- [Getting Started with Workflows in HighLevel](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002288)

title_en: Workflow Action - Add To Google Ads
source_md:
Track real user actions—like form submissions or chat replies—as Google Ads conversions directly inside your workflows using Add to Google Ads workflow action. This article shows you exactly how to set it up, why it matters, and how to troubleshoot it for accuracy and better ROI.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Is the Add to Google Ads Workflow Action?](#What-Is-the-Add-to-Google-Ads-Workflow-Action?)
- [Key Benefits of Add to Google Ads Workflow Action](#Key-Benefits-of-Add-to-Google-Ads-Workflow-Action)
- [How to Use Add to Google Ads Action Workflows](#How-to-Use-Add-to-Google-Ads%C2%A0Action%C2%A0Workflows%C2%A0)
- [Popular Use Cases](#Popular-Use-Cases)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Is the Add to Google Ads Workflow Action?**

The Add to Google Ads action allows you to send conversion events from HighLevel into your Google Ads account. This feature is ideal for tracking offline conversions, such as form submissions, chat replies, purchases, or appointment bookings that happen after a user clicks your ad. By tying those actions back to the original click, you gain deeper insight into your campaign performance and can feed that data into Google’s optimization engine.

To make this work, HighLevel uses unique identifiers like GCLID, GBRAID, or WBRAID that are passed during the ad click. These values must be present on the contact record in order for the conversion to be properly attributed.

```
Note: You must set up the conversion event in Google Ads first before using this workflow action.

Checkout our articles on Setting Up Google Ads Conversion Actions:

1. How To Set Up Google Ads Conversion Actions (Google Platform Side Setup)

2. HighLevel Ad Manager - Create & Manage Google Ads Offline Conversions
```

---

## **Key Benefits of Add to Google Ads Workflow Action**

- **Offline Conversion Tracking:** Tracks offline events like form submissions, chat replies, or booked appointments for better attribution.

- **Direct Event Syncing:**Sends conversion events straight to Google Ads—no need for Zapier or manual data uploads.

- **Enhanced Campaign Optimization:**Improves ad performance by giving Google better data to optimize around.

- **Click ID Support:**Compatible with GCLID, GBRAID, and WBRAID for comprehensive tracking coverage.

- **Flexible Trigger Options:**Works with multiple workflow triggers including form submissions, link clicks, and page views.

- **Lead Quality Attribution:** Helps you accurately measure the source and quality of your leads, improving ROI tracking.

---

## **How to Setup Add to Google Ads****Action****in Workflows**

Understanding how to properly set up the “Add to Google Ads” action ensures your Google Ads campaigns can accurately measure and attribute conversions. This step-by-step guide walks you through how to configure the action inside a workflow, including where to find it, how to set it up, and how to ensure it’s firing correctly.

```
Connect Your Google Ads Account: In order to use the “Add to Google Ads” workflow action, you must first connect your Google Ads account to HighLevel. This integration enables HighLevel to send conversion events directly to Google Ads via API. To set it up, navigate to Settings > Integrations in your HighLevel sub-account, select Google, and follow the prompts to authenticate your account. Be sure to link the correct Google Ads account, especially if you manage multiple. Without this connection, the action will not function, regardless of how well everything else is configured. 

Important: After connecting your Google Ads account to HighLevel, you must already have at least one conversion action created inside your Google Ads account. HighLevel fetches available conversion actions directly from Google Ads during setup. If no conversion actions exist yet, the dropdown menu for selecting a conversion event inside the workflow will be blank. 
```

### **Step 1:**Access the Workflow Builder

1. Log in to your sub-account.
2. Go to **Automations > Workflows**.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/Cnveqtr2TxPJeI2Wif1E+/Screen+Shot+2026-01-05+at+6.02.58+PM.png)
3. Create a **N****ew** **W****orkflow** or **O****pen** an **E****xisting** one.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/vy9UlWTok3ZfxkZZpVLC+/Screen+Shot+2026-01-05+at+6.04.41+PM.png)

### **Step 2:** Add a Relevant Trigger

- Click on the **Add New Trigger** button to add a relevant trigger that reflects the action or event you want to track - like a form submission or an appointment booking.
- **Examples of effective triggers include:** Form Submitted, Appointment Booked, Trigger Link Clicked, or Customer Replied. Workflows can be created for Form Submission, Order Purchases, Number Pool Calling, Survey Submission, and Chat Widget.  
    
  ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/MAFnHtvBfVl4S7D4VC12+/GIF+Recording+2026-02-05+at+7.50.55+PM.gif)

### **Step 3:**Add the “Add to Google Ads” Action

1. After your trigger is in place, click the**“+”** icon at the point in the workflow where you want the conversion to fire.
2. This opens the **action selection panel**. Scroll through the list and choose “**Add to Google Ads**.” This action allows you to send conversion data directly to your connected Google Ads account via API.
3. Once the action is added, you’ll see the configuration panel on the right-hand side.

![](https://jumpshare.com/share/EoFZFizWBeNYO7KKgFT5+/GIF+Recording+2026-02-05+at+8.04.29+PM.gif)

### **Step 4:**Configure the Action Details

```
Preparing Google Ads Conversion Setup

Before configuring the “Add to Google Ads” workflow action in HighLevel, there are three critical steps you must complete within Google Ads:

1. Create the conversion action inside your Google Ads account—this defines the specific event you want to track, such as a form submission or appointment booking.

2. Copy the exact conversion name from Google Ads and use it precisely as-is in your HighLevel workflow action. Any mismatch in the name, even due to capitalization or spacing, will prevent the action from working.

3. Ensure that your ad URLs include proper click tracking parameters: use GCLID for Search campaigns, and GBRAID or WBRAID for iOS and Android app campaigns. HighLevel must capture these identifiers from incoming leads to pass accurate attribution data back to Google Ads. 

Without these prerequisites, conversion syncing will fail. Additionally, be aware of your conversion setting type—if your conversion is set to “One Per Click,” GCLID is required, as GBRAID and WBRAID only support “Many Per Click” tracking. This distinction is especially important when troubleshooting missed or skipped conversions.
```

1. Setting up the conversion action correctly is essential for data to flow from HighLevel to Google Ads. This step involves linking your workflow to the proper conversion event and ensuring all tracking parameters are accurately in place. Missteps here—such as typos in the conversion name or missing click IDs—can prevent your conversion from syncing entirely.
2. **Action Name:**Give your action a clear and descriptive name—something like “Submit Lead Conversion” or “Book Appointment Conversion.” This name will appear in your workflow logs, so it should clearly reflect what the conversion is for.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/CDM31cfFgsxaGIeHU6u1+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-05+at+8.07.49+PM.png)
3. **Conversion:**In this dropdown, select or paste the exact name of the conversion event from your Google Ads account. The name must match exactly—including capitalization, spacing, and punctuation—or the action will be skipped. Your workflow action will not fire the conversion unless the names align perfectly.  
     

   ```
   Please Note: Every time you create a new campaign in Google, you will need to select the conversion action which you just created as your Google Adwords option in your new workflow action.  
     
   It will take approximately 5 minutes once we receive one contact with UTM source and gclid, wbraid or gbraid to get the list populated in workflow trigger as well as in Google Adwords Conversion.
   ```

     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/tQSwMoAGpZa2HEw6aADs+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-05+at+8.23.57+PM.png)
4. **Currency:**Choose the currency in which you want your conversion value to be attributed in.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/KQLZdRT1ATp51P7d6nHB+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-05+at+8.25.36+PM.png)
5. **Conversion Value:**Enter the amount or value of each conversion as per the Currency chosen in the previous step. E.g. a conversion for a dental checkup client is valued at $100.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/7BuIY5OXPzywVfjHQVfx+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-05+at+8.27.08+PM.png)
6. **Custom Mapping:**Toggle on the Custom Mapping switch if you want to manually map specific Google Ads conversion parameters (like GCLID, GBRAID, or WBRAID) to fields within your workflow. This is helpful when you’re working with custom fields or want more granular control over how the click ID is passed back to Google Ads.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/ikSiGaGH3PGjq97Y2K9v+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-05+at+9.05.28+PM.png)

### **Step 5:** Save and Publish Workflow

1. Click on the **Save Action** button.
2. **Publish** the workflow and **Save** it.  
     
   ![](https://jumpshare.com/share/2UEcwKdCdWAp8dCG3uvL+/Screen+Shot+2026-02-05+at+9.40.03+PM.png)

### **Step 6:**Monitor Workflow Execution Logs

Once your workflow is active, it’s important to monitor its execution to ensure the action is firing properly.

Go to the Execution Logs tab within the workflow. Look for the “Add to Google Ads” action and its result:

**Executed:** The conversion was successfully sent to Google Ads.

**Skipped:**Something went wrong (e.g., missing GCLID or mismatched conversion name).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155043968547/original/aFenfQtgfTtqzwvum3qXSNWTGE49Friqhg.png?1742959494)

---

## **Popular Use Cases**

To make sure this action actually sends data to Google Ads, it must be paired with a meaningful conversion event. This is where selecting the right trigger becomes crucial. Popular Triggers Include:

### **1. Form Submission/Order Purchases/Survey Submission**

1. Create the Workflow.
2. Select the trigger - **Form Submission, Order Form Submission, or Survey Submission**.
3. Once the trigger is selected, add the **filters** with which the Form/ Order Form/ Survey and save the trigger details.
4. Click on the **+****plus** icon to add an action and select the "Add to Google Ads" event and select the **conversion action** from the dropdown which was created on Google.
5. Define the **Currency** and **Conversion** Value for the conversion.
6. Click "**Save**" and "**Publish**" your workflow..

[동영상](https://www.loom.com/embed/dcdfb3aa457743d19df4f03a71b8a139)

### **2. Number Pool Calling**

1. Create the Workflow.
2. Select the trigger - **Call Status**.
3. Once the trigger is selected, add the **filters** with **Call Direction > Incoming and Pool Number > Select Pool Number**.
4. **Please add the pool number script on the funnel/website in header settings.**
5. Click on the **+ plus icon**to add an action and select the "**Add to Google Ads**" event and select the conversion action from the dropdown which was created on Google.
6. Define the **Currency** and **Conversion****Value** for the conversion.
7. Click "**Save**" and "**Publish**" your workflow.

[동영상](https://www.loom.com/embed/9e3c67bb2e4d466e881e3d75a76460b6)

### **3. Chat Widget**

1. Create the Workflow.
2. Select the trigger - **Customer Replied Trigger**.
3. Click on the **+ plus icon**to add an action and select the "**Add to Google Ads**" event and select the conversion action from the dropdown which was created on Google.
4. Define the **Currency** and **Conversion** **Value** for the conversion.
5. Click "**Save**" and "**Publish**" your workflow.

[동영상](https://www.loom.com/embed/cad44f9ac32c4f4aa37684ab910f3164)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: I have set up my conversions now how do I know it's working?**

Currently, there is no way to test this event. You can always check your workflow action and check out the history tab⁣. It should show the execution for Google Adword Action.

⁣⁣

**Q:Where can I see my conversions?⁣**

It will take approximately 5 minutes to get the list populated in trigger/workflow as well as in Google AdWords Conversion. ⁣Within the 15 minutes window, you can check the workflow history.⁣

**Q: Does this work with all triggers?⁣**

It **only works** for Form Submission, Order Purchase, Number Pool Calling, Survey Submission, and Chat Widget.

**Q: What should I do if the action says “Skipped” in logs?**

To ensure successful conversion tracking, two key conditions must be met: the contact in HighLevel must have a valid GCLID, GBRAID, or WBRAID—captured from a legitimate Google ad click—and the conversion name used in the workflow must exactly match the one created in your Google Ads account. Even a small mismatch in the conversion name will prevent the event from registering correctly in Google Ads.

**Q: What’s the difference between GCLID, GBRAID, and WBRAID?**

**GCLID:**Used for traditional web tracking.

**GBRAID/WBRAID:** Used in privacy-focused environments (mainly on iOS).

Only “multi-per-click” conversions accept GBRAID/WBRAID. If your conversion setting is “one per click,” GCLID is required.

**Q: Can I track leads that come through the chat widget?**

Yes. Use the Customer Replied trigger and add a filter: Reply Channel = Chat Widget. This ensures the event only fires when a user replies via the widget.

**Q: Do I need to configure anything in Google Ads before using this?**

Yes. Before using the “Add to Google Ads” action in HighLevel, you need to ensure your Google Ads account is properly configured. First, create the conversion action directly within your Google Ads account. Then, copy the exact name of that conversion—making sure it matches character-for-character—and paste it into the workflow action in HighLevel. Finally, confirm that your Google ad URLs are correctly passing tracking parameters like GCLID, GBRAID, or WBRAID to ensure conversions can be properly attributed back to the original ad click.

**Q: Is Google Tag Manager required for this to work?**

No. This action does not require Google Tag Manager. However, GTM can still be helpful if you’re tracking additional client-side events.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [Ad Manager - Create & Manage Google Ads Offline Conversions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005431)
- [How To Set Up Google Ads Conversion Actions (Google Platform Side Setup)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001220947)
- [Overview of Ad Manager](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000002433)
- [Ad Manager - Create a Google Search Ad Campaign](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004543)
- [How to view Google Ad Campaign Statistics in Ad Manager](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000005309)

title_en: How to Customize the Navigation Menu
source_md:
Customize your HighLevel navigation menu to keep frequently used products easy to find. Rename navigation groups, change icons, reorder entries, hide products, and organize items into new groups. Custom Navigation is available on all HighLevel agency plans, but customization capabilities vary by subscription level. All plans include the redesigned navigation experience, while higher-tier plans provide additional customization options.This guide explains how navigation customization works in the **new HighLevel interface**, how shared layouts affect a sub-account, and how to customize and save your navigation.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Is Navigation Menu Customization?](#what-is-navigation-customization)
- [Key Benefits of Navigation Menu Customization](#key-benefits)
- [Availability and Shared Navigation](#availability-shared-navigation)
- [Navigation Levels and Customization Options](#navigation-levels)
- [Naming Rules and Fixed Navigation Items](#naming-rules)
- [Navigation Visibility vs. Product Access](#visibility-vs-access)
- [How to Customize the Navigation Menu](#customize-navigation)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#frequently-asked-questions)
- [Related Articles](#related-articles)

---

## **What Is Navigation Menu Customization?**

Navigation menu customization changes how groups and products appear in the left sidebar. The navigation editor lets you adjust their organization and visibility without changing product functionality or access permissions.

Your changes belong to the sub-account's navigation layout rather than an individual user's personal settings.

---

## **Key Benefits of Navigation Menu Customization**

Organizing the menu around your team's work makes frequently used products easier to locate while keeping their functionality unchanged.

- **Familiar organization:** Rename groups and arrange products around your team's workflows.
- **Less clutter:** Hide groups or products that do not need a prominent place in the sidebar.
- **Faster access:** Reorder frequently used groups and products so they are easier to find.
- **Visual organization:** Change navigation icons to make entries easier to recognize.
- **Consistent navigation:** Give users in the same sub-account a shared layout, subject to their individual product permissions.

---

## **Availability and Shared Navigation**

Navigation customization requires an eligible agency plan and access to the navigation editor. Plan eligibility determines how many sub-accounts can be customized.

| **Agency Plan** | **Navigation Customization** |
| --- | --- |
| **$97/month** | Default navigation only. Customization is not included. |
| **$297/month** | Customize one sub-account. Reusable layouts and application across multiple sub-accounts are not included. |
| **$497/month** | Customize all sub-accounts, create reusable layouts, and apply layouts across multiple sub-accounts. |

Once applied, group names, ordering, hidden items, and product organization affect the sub-account's shared navigation layout.

```
Note: Recents and Pinned remain personal to each user and are not changed by editing a shared layout. Product permissions continue to determine what each user can access.
```

---

## **Navigation Levels and Customization Options**

The available customization actions depend on the navigation level:

- **L1:** A top-level navigation group.
- **L2:** A product or item inside an L1 group.
- **L3:** A nested item beneath an L2 item.

| **Action** | **L1: Navigation Group** | **L2: Product or Item** | **L3: Nested Item** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rename** | Yes | No | No |
| **Change icon** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Reorder** | Among top-level groups | Within its existing L1 group | Within its existing L2 parent |
| **Hide or show independently** | Yes | Yes | No |
| **Create through the editor** | Yes | No | No |
| **Move into another L1 group** | Not applicable | Yes | Yes, directly into the group's menu |

```
Important: Reordering changes an item's position within its current parent. Moving changes which group contains the item. Creating a navigation group does not create a new HighLevel product.
```

---

## **Naming Rules and Fixed Navigation Items**

Navigation group names should be easy to recognize, while protected navigation items remain available for essential navigation.

- Group names cannot be empty or contain only spaces.
- A group name cannot duplicate another L1 group name in the same navigation.
- Leading and trailing spaces are removed.
- **Recents** and **Pinned** are reserved names.
- Long labels can display an ellipsis. Hover over a shortened label to view the full name.
- **Settings** remains in its fixed position.
- **Recents** and **Pinned** cannot be hidden.
- Custom menu links and custom pages cannot be renamed through the navigation editor. Update their names from the area where they were originally created.

---

## **Navigation Visibility vs. Product Access**

Navigation visibility determines whether an item appears in the sidebar. Permissions determine whether a user can access the product.

**Hiding a product does not disable it or restrict access.** Users with the required permissions can still open a hidden product through a direct URL or **All Products**.

Showing a product in a navigation layout also does not override restrictions imposed by user permissions or the SaaS Configurator.

```
Important: Use feature or user permissions when you need to restrict access to a product. Use navigation customization to control how products are organized and displayed in the sidebar.
```

---

## **How to Customize the Navigation Menu**

Start in the sub-account whose navigation you want to change. Use the navigation editor to organize the menu, then review the layout and its application scope before saving.

### **Step 1:**Locate the Navigation Editor

The editing entry point is located at the bottom of the sidebar and is separate from controls used to edit the page currently displayed.

1. Open the sub-account in the **new HighLevel interface**.
2. Locate **Edit** at the bottom of the left navigation.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084247746/original/vwdp8cdADFozwHW4WwQzSA8jGU_RAt7F4A.png?1793042218)**

```
Note: Select Edit in the sidebar. Do not select Edit dashboard from the Dashboard toolbar.
```

### 

### **Step 2:**Open Editing Mode

Editing mode displays customization controls beside the navigation entries so you can organize the menu without opening individual products.

1. Click **Edit** at the bottom of the sidebar.
2. Review the navigation in editing mode.

The main page appears dimmed, and the sidebar displays controls such as drag handles, three-dot menus, **Add a category or product**, and the **Editing** panel at the bottom.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084247866/original/mOIP0tBPsgRSEv5fp1Xa-7C8lkK6diE5Ng.png?1793042522)**

### **Step 3:**Reorder Navigation Groups and Items

Reordering changes an entry's position within its current navigation level.

1. Click and hold the **drag handle** beside the group or item.
2. Drag it to the desired position.
3. Use the horizontal placement indicator to identify where the item will appear.
4. Release the item to place it in that position.

****![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084249807/original/jNAPjRK-NRh79m-cUeQB73XplScUPG-GiA.png?1793044610)****

For top-level groups, you can also select **Move up** or **Move down** from the group's three-dot menu.

- L2 items can be reordered within their existing L1 group.
- L3 items can be reordered within their existing L2 parent.
- Moving an item into another group is a separate action.
- **Settings** cannot be reordered.

### **Step 4:**Rename a Group or Change an Icon

Group names and icons help your team recognize where products belong. Renaming is available for L1 groups only, while supported navigation icons can be changed at all three levels.

1. Click the **three-dot menu (⋮)** beside the group or item you want to customize.

**To rename a group:**

2. Select **Rename**.
3. Enter a short, descriptive group name that follows the naming rules above.
4. Complete the change using the available confirmation control.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084250710/original/crv3QW537s6dqdkbdYMlXC7kBsStVSNDwQ.png?1793046238)

**To change an icon:**

1. Open the item's **three-dot menu (⋮)**.
2. Select **Change icon**.
3. Choose the navigation icon you want to use.
4. Complete the change using the available control.

```
Note: Changing a navigation icon changes the icon beside that navigation entry. It does not change the account avatar or logo.
```

### **Step 5:**Review Available Navigation Layouts

Use the **Navigation Layouts** picker to identify the layout you are editing and review how other saved layouts are being used.

The picker includes a **Search layouts** field. A check mark identifies the selected layout, and usage labels can indicate whether another layout is not in use or is applied to a sub-account.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084248845/original/GclxQoHtwugckCnxRBlC1h-aUeqoj7P87w.png?1793043346)**

```
Note: The Navigation Layouts picker shows layout selection and usage. It is not a save-confirmation screen.
```

### 

### **Step 6:**Manage Visibility and Organize Groups

Visibility controls simplify the sidebar, while group-organization controls let you arrange products around your team's work.

Open a group's **three-dot menu (⋮)** to access available actions such as **Hide** and **Add a product**.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084249655/original/1bzQa-QxBe9L1G2nAZxOVI4YdTwG9ww0EQ.png?1793044384)**

### **Hide or Show a Group or Product**

Use visibility controls when you want to remove an item from the sidebar without removing access to the underlying product.

- L1 groups can be hidden or shown.
- Individual L2 products can be hidden or shown.
- L3 items cannot be hidden independently.

Select **Hide** from the available menu to hide a supported group or product. Hidden items can be restored through the navigation editor's available visibility controls.

### **Create a Navigation Group**

Create a new navigation group when you want to organize related products together. The editor can use the term **category** to refer to a navigation group.

1. Select **Add a category or product**.
2. Choose the available option for creating a category.
3. Enter a name for the new group.
4. Complete the creation using the available control.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084250696/original/2C5z1wZD5ozUPfQwJFHPFuiDk3Evt4EXqg.png?1793046214)

New groups can be renamed, assigned an icon, and reordered alongside existing groups.

### **Add Products to a Group**

1. Open the group's **three-dot menu (⋮)**.
2. Select **Add a product**.
3. Use the available product-selection controls to organize products within the group.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084249478/original/XjBWlqQbiXE_blsxblRuA76hH6zgB_5m8Q.png?1793044101)

### **Move Products Between Groups**

Moving changes which navigation group contains an item. This is different from reordering an item within its current group.

- An L2 product can be moved into another L1 group, including a renamed or newly created group.
- An L3 item can be moved out of its L2 parent and placed directly inside an L1 group's menu.

Moving an L3 item into an L1 group does **not** create another top-level navigation group.

### **Step 7:**Review and Save the Layout

Review the navigation before saving, especially when the layout is already used by other sub-accounts.

1. Review the group names, icons, order, visibility, and product placement.
2. Check whether the layout is already used by other sub-accounts.
3. Click **Save layout** in the bottom **Editing** panel.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084249330/original/yP5AAvwT1x63B9eqiJFmmmXmCNtVHqIQnA.png?1793043843)**

4. If an application-scope prompt appears, review where the changes will be applied.
5. Complete the save.
6. Review the resulting navigation to confirm the layout appears as intended.

Saving records the configuration and, by default, applies it to the sub-account being edited. Applying a saved layout to additional sub-accounts is a separate action.

```
Important: Updating a saved layout already used by multiple sub-accounts can affect those sub-accounts. On the $497 plan, a one-off edit can update the shared layout or be saved separately for the current sub-account. Review layout usage before saving.
```

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: How can I find a product when the navigation groups have unfamiliar names?**

Select **View all** beside **Recents** to open **All Products**. The directory lists products under their original HighLevel names regardless of customized group labels.

**Q: Does hiding a product remove access to it?**

No. Hiding a product changes its visibility in the navigation. Users with the required permissions can still access it through **All Products** or a direct URL.

**Q: Are navigation layouts included in snapshots?**

No. Navigation layouts and snapshots operate independently in this release. Applying a snapshot does not replace the existing navigation layout or restore items hidden through navigation customization.

**Q: Do newly created sub-accounts automatically inherit an agency's custom navigation layout?**

No. Layouts are applied to the sub-accounts selected by the agency. Newly created sub-accounts do not automatically inherit an agency's custom base navigation.

**Q: What happens to existing layouts when an agency downgrades from $497 to $297?**

Existing customizations remain in place across sub-accounts. Future editing is limited to one sub-account. The first sub-account edited after the downgrade becomes the editable sub-account, while other sub-accounts retain their existing layouts but cannot be modified under the $297 entitlement.

**Q: Will my customization be preserved if I disable the new navigation?**

No. Disabling the new navigation discards the customization. Re-enabling the new navigation starts from the default navigation rather than restoring the previous customized layout.

**Q: Are Recents and Pinned shared with everyone using the navigation layout?**

No. **Recents** and **Pinned** remain personal to each user and are not changed by editing the shared navigation layout.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Getting Started with Custom Navigation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000009418)
- [Using Custom CSS and JavaScript with the Custom Navigation](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000009423)

A complete reference of every system-generated email — what it is, what triggers it, and how to disable it where possible.

Every outgoing system email the platform sends, organized by scope. **Sub-Account / Location Level** emails are tied to individual locations (appointments, reviews, social planner, payments). **Agency Level** emails are sent from the agency itself (password resets, user provisioning, payment failures, registration status).
