title_en: How to Use Rich Elements in Conversation AI
source_md:
HighLevel Conversation AI supports Rich Elements, allowing agents to send interactive replies with buttons, lists, images, files, links, and formatted text. Instead of relying only on plain text, agents can automatically select suitable message elements to help contacts interact more easily.

You can also control which elements are available and create Response Rules for specific conversation scenarios.

[동영상](https://jumpshare.com/embed/FwnrXBr8PmVIPpUIqToJ)

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What are Rich Elements in Conversation AI?](#What-are-Rich-Elements-in-Conversation-AI?)
- [Types of Rich Elements](#Types-of-Rich-Elements)
  - [Formatted Text](#Formatted-Text)
  - [Quick Replies](#Quick-Replies)
  - [Link Buttons](#Link-Buttons)
  - [Lists](#Lists)
  - [Images](#Images)
  - [Files](#Files)
- [Supported Channels and Message Behavior](#Supported-Channels-and-Message-Behavior)
- [Response Rules](#Response-Rules)
- [Response Rule Settings](#Response-Rule-Settings)
- [How to Set Up Rich Elements in Conversation AI](#How-to-Set-Up-Rich-Elements-in-Conversation-AI)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What are Rich Elements in Conversation AI?**

Rich Elements are interactive message components that help Conversation AI agents present information and guide customer interactions beyond plain text. The AI automatically selects appropriate elements based on the conversation, while optional Response Rules provide additional control over when specific elements are used.

For example, a real estate agent can display neighborhoods as a list, provide booking buttons, or share property images and listing links.

Rich Elements are available on WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Instagram (mobile app), and Live Chat. Other channels continue using plain-text responses.

---

## **Types of Rich Elements**

Conversation AI provides six Rich Element types, each designed to make information easier to present or interact with.

You can enable the elements that best support your customer conversations.

### **Formatted Text**

Uses bold or italic formatting to emphasize important information, such as pricing, business hours, or instructions. The release specifically supports formatted text on WhatsApp; behavior on other channels may vary.

### **Quick Replies**

Displays tappable response options, such as **Buy** or **Rent**, so contacts can answer questions without typing.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084079834/original/d09DgXYV0rZurdDyGaFr6v_5enNhsDf3Xg.png?1792767580)**

### **Link Buttons**

Provides clickable buttons that open webpages, such as booking pages, property listings, or product catalogs.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084080241/original/FftCpnAsoT5vun_KxLISRPoN94z5hw70-g.png?1792767776)

### **Lists**

Organizes multiple choices into a selectable menu, making it easier for contacts to choose neighborhoods, services, products, or other options.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084080284/original/ajW9WMdvI7JJQP2AHN8CgTF6QJpLr1rhCQ.png?1792767811)**

### **Images**

Displays images directly in conversations, helping contacts view products, properties, or other visual information without leaving the chat.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084080375/original/e7JAX_zLRF8tN8ahr4T9f5DSul_Y-9cTNA.png?1792767857)**

### **Files**

Allows agents to share supported PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, and presentations when contacts request additional information.

The agent needs access to an appropriate supported file URL. Specific extensions, file-size limits, and hosting restrictions require verification.

---

## **Supported Channels and Message Behavior**

Rich Elements work across supported messaging channels, although individual elements may display differently depending on the platform. Knowing these differences helps ensure contacts can still access important information.

| Channel | Availability |
| --- | --- |
| WhatsApp | Supported |
| Facebook Messenger | Supported |
| Instagram | Supported in the mobile app |
| Live Chat | Supported |
| Other channels | Plain text |

**Automatic Selection:** Conversation AI can choose a suitable enabled element based on the conversation without requiring a separate template for every message.

**Plain-Text Fallback:** If a channel cannot display an element or a response exceeds channel limits, the content is moved into message text.

```
Note: Individual element availability and fallback formatting may vary by channel. Test important scenarios on the platforms your business uses.
```

---

## **Response Rules**

Response Rules provide situation-specific instructions that guide Conversation AI toward a particular Rich Element.

They are useful when you want to control message presentation without manually configuring every response.

For example, you can instruct the agent to display a list whenever a contact asks which neighborhoods your business serves.

### **Response Rule Settings**

Each rule includes the following controls:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Rule Name | Identifies the rule. |
| Rule Toggle | Enables or disables the rule. |
| Situation, in your words | Describes when the element should be used. |
| Element | Selects the Rich Element for the situation. |
| Element supported on | Displays supported messaging channels. |
| Save rules | Saves the configuration. |

Additional controls let you add, edit, or delete rules. Only enabled Rich Elements are available for selection.

**Example: Neighborhood Selection**

- **Rule Name:** Neighborhoods
- **Situation:** "The lead asks which areas we cover or wants to see homes without naming a neighborhood. Reply with the list of neighborhoods we serve."
- **Element:** List

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084080544/original/dowQeUucgO_YBAEVj0LGg9RV6Ngtp9y43w.png?1792767941)**

The interface also includes an **Only honor these rules** toggle. Its exact enforcement behavior requires verification before relying on it to restrict automatic element selection.

---

## **How to Set Up Rich Elements in Conversation AI**

Setting up Rich Elements involves enabling the feature, choosing permitted message types, and optionally adding media URLs or Response Rules. Proper configuration helps your agent deliver useful interactive responses on supported channels.

### **Step 1: Enable Rich Elements in Labs**

Activate the feature before configuring it in your agent.

1. Open your HighLevel account and navigate to **Labs**.
2. Find **Conversations AI Rich Elements**.
3. Turn the feature **ON**.

```
Note: Confirm whether Labs activation is still required at publication time.
```

### **Step 2: Open Your Conversation AI Agent**

Rich Elements are configured in the agent's Response Behavior settings.

1. Navigate to **AI Agents → Conversation AI → Agents List**.
2. Open the prompt-based agent you want to edit.
3. Locate **Response Behavior** in the Build interface.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084081959/original/XzHB1bXCwACRTTlzbVtAIXQwg6Oi2AlT8A.png?1792768630)**

**Note:** The release documents setup for prompt-based agents. Support for other agent types requires confirmation.

### **Step 3: Enable and Configure Rich Elements**

Choose which interactive message formats the agent is allowed to send.

1. Expand **Response Behavior**.
2. Turn **Enable Rich Elements Support** ON.
3. Under **Allow this bot to send**, enable or disable the following elements:

   - Formatted text
   - Quick replies
   - Link button
   - List
   - Image
   - File

Only enabled elements can be selected when creating Response Rules.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084082134/original/V7GlTSInPIJtuWz_RwJA63RXmK3PvizUzQ.png?1792768690)**

### **Step 4: Add Media URLs (Optional)**

Provide publicly accessible URLs when you want the agent to share specific images or files.

1. Open the agent's prompt editor.
2. Add URLs for supported images or documents.
3. Include context explaining what each resource represents.
4. Save the updated prompt.

For example:

**Property:** 4812 Aldrich Street  
**Description:** Four-bedroom home with a two-car garage.  
**Image:** `https://example.com/images/4812-aldrich.jpg`  
**Listing:** `https://example.com/listings/4812-aldrich`

```
Note: Media URLs are optional. Supported formats, maximum file sizes, and URL restrictions should be verified.
```

### **Step 5: Configure Response Rules (Optional)**

Add rules when you want the agent to use a particular element in specific situations.

1. Under **Response Behavior**, click **Setup Your Response Rules**.
2. Click **Add rule**.
3. Enter a **Rule Name** and describe the **Situation, in your words**.
4. Choose an **Element** from the dropdown.
5. Review the **Element supported on** indicators.
6. Enable the rule if necessary, then click **Save rules**.

**Example:** Create a rule named *Book a Viewing* with the instruction: "When a contact asks to schedule a property viewing, offer the booking link using a link button." Select **Link button** as the element.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084082965/original/Nus-VBRzp-YPect-jcpVDoR-MpgCLsj_4w.png?1792768977)**

**Tip:** Describe situations naturally rather than relying on exact customer phrases.

### **Step 6: Save and Test Your Agent**

Testing confirms that enabled elements and Response Rules produce appropriate replies before customers interact with the agent.

1. Click **Save** in the agent editor after reviewing your settings.
2. Open **Test your agent** and select an available preview option.
3. Send test messages such as:

   - "Which neighborhoods do you cover?"
   - "I want to book a viewing."
   - "Can you show me available properties?"
   - "Do you have a brochure?"
4. Confirm the agent uses suitable elements and accurate information.
5. Repeat on the messaging channels your business uses.

**Tip:** A successful Live Chat preview does not guarantee identical behavior on other messaging channels.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Do I need Response Rules for every Rich Element?**

No. Conversation AI can automatically select enabled elements. Response Rules provide additional guidance for specific situations.

**Q: Why is an element missing from the Response Rules dropdown?**

Only enabled Rich Elements can be selected. Check the individual toggles under Response Behavior.

**Q: Can I enable Rich Elements without changing my agent prompt?**

Yes. Prompt changes are optional, although adding relevant image, file, or webpage URLs can help the agent share specific resources.

**Q: Can Rich Elements analyze images sent by contacts?**

Not by themselves. Outgoing image messages and incoming image analysis are separate Conversation AI capabilities.

**Q: Are Response Rules different from prompt instructions?**

Yes. Prompts guide overall conversational behavior, while Response Rules provide instructions for using specific interactive message formats.

**Q: Does a booking link button automatically schedule an appointment?**

No. A link button directs contacts to a booking page. Actual appointment scheduling depends on the configured booking functionality.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Set Up a Conversation AI Bot](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004401)
- [Conversation AI Bot Explained](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001335)
- [Configure Response Settings in Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007421)
- [Customize Conversation AI Agent Responses with Prompts and Instructions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002255-customize-conversation-ai-agent-responses-with-prompts-and-instructions)
- [Conversations AI Bots can now Respond to Images](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006537)
- [How to Use Knowledge Base Triggers in Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007791)

title_en: Prospecting at Sub Accounts
source_md:
Prospecting • CRM • Automation

Prospecting in HighLevel Sub-Accounts

HighLevel Prospecting helps you find businesses, generate marketing audit reports, and move prospects into your CRM. Running Prospecting inside a sub-account adds access to Contacts, Opportunities, workflows, email, SMS, and pipeline automation. Eligible agency-owned sub-accounts can use the Prospecting Free Tier, while Prospecting Premium provides additional prospecting, enrichment, and reporting capabilities.

What You'll Learn

Learn how to enable Prospecting in a sub-account, understand how prospects become CRM contacts, automate follow-up, route Prospect AI leads into pipelines, and migrate existing Agency prospects into a sub-account.

Important

Agency-level Prospecting focuses on lead discovery and reporting. CRM functionality such as Contacts, Opportunities, email, SMS, and workflow automation is available when Prospecting is used inside an eligible sub-account.

# What Is Prospecting in Sub-Accounts?

Prospecting inside a sub-account combines business discovery and marketing audit reporting with HighLevel's CRM and automation tools. This makes it possible to move from finding a business to creating a contact, starting follow-up, and managing the sales process without leaving the sub-account.

Depending on your Prospecting access, sub-account Prospecting can work with:

- Contacts
- Opportunities and pipelines
- Workflows
- Email and SMS outreach
- Marketing audit reports
- Prospect AI and other Premium capabilities, when included with your access

Agency-level Prospecting is useful for lead discovery and reporting. Sub-account Prospecting is the better fit when the team also needs CRM follow-up, sales pipelines, and automation.

## Key Benefits of Prospecting in Sub-Accounts

Using Prospecting where your CRM already lives reduces manual handoffs between lead discovery and sales follow-up, helping teams act on newly generated prospects faster.

- **Sync Prospects to CRM:** Save generated prospects as usable CRM contacts inside the same sub-account.
- **Automate Follow-Up:** Trigger workflows when new prospects are generated.
- **Route Leads to Pipelines:** Create or update Opportunities through workflows or supported Prospect AI pipeline integration.
- **Use Prospect AI:** Discover prospects automatically and route future qualifying leads into selected CRM pipelines when the feature is available.
- **Reach Prospects Directly:** Use email, SMS, assignments, tags, and other CRM tools from the sub-account.
- **Reduce Context Switching:** Keep discovery, CRM management, and follow-up in one working environment.

## Prerequisites and Limitations

Prospecting access depends on whether the sub-account qualifies for the Prospecting Free Tier or has Prospecting Premium. Confirm the account type and subscription before troubleshooting missing features.

### Prospecting Free Tier for Agency Sub-Accounts

The Free Tier is designed primarily for an agency's own internal sub-accounts and provides core Prospecting access where the agency's CRM and automation workflows are managed.

- The location must be marked as an **Agency Sub-Account**.
- The Prospecting Free Tier feature must be enabled through the applicable **Agency Labs** toggle.
- HighLevel's current Prospecting Free Tier documentation states that marking a location as an Agency Sub-Account requires the **$497 Agency plan**.
- Free Tier access is intended primarily for internal agency prospecting rather than advanced client-facing Prospecting use cases.

### Prospecting Premium

Prospecting Premium is intended for expanded prospecting, reporting, enrichment, and client-facing use cases and can be enabled directly for a sub-account.

Premium can be activated by:

- Enabling and reselling Prospecting from **Agency View → Reselling**.
- Purchasing Prospecting Premium directly inside the sub-account.
- Linking an eligible Agency Prospecting Premium subscription to one sub-account.

## How To Enable Prospecting in a Sub-Account

Choose the activation method that matches the sub-account's intended use. Agency-owned internal locations can use the Prospecting Free Tier when eligible, while client-facing and advanced use cases generally use Prospecting Premium.

### Option 1: Enable the Prospecting Free Tier

Marking the location as an Agency Sub-Account identifies it as an agency-owned location that can receive eligible Free Tier Prospecting access.

1. From **Agency View**, go to **Sub-Accounts**.
2. Locate the applicable sub-account.
3. Open the **three-dot menu**.
4. Select **Add as Agency Sub-Account**.
5. Confirm the applicable Prospecting Free Tier feature is enabled in **Agency Labs**.
6. Open the sub-account.
7. Go to **Marketing → Prospecting**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081376385/original/O29M1z8HmcANnosYaxhtf0n18jT04Xq5mw.png?1789883221)
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081376391/original/pWQzqWEZHwP1gtRxfgCBfzsrFldnWARQrg.png?1789883236)

### Option 2: Enable Prospecting Premium

Premium can be activated through agency reselling, direct sub-account purchase, or by linking an eligible Agency Premium subscription.

**Using Reselling:**

1. From **Agency View**, open **Reselling**.
2. Enable the option to resell Prospecting.
3. Configure the offer as needed.
4. Open the applicable sub-account.
5. Go to **Marketing → Prospecting**.
6. Complete the Prospecting Premium activation or purchase flow.

Premium can also be purchased directly from the sub-account. Agencies that already have an eligible Agency Prospecting Premium subscription can link one sub-account to that subscription through the Agency Prospecting subscription settings.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081376382/original/FylOEr7a90cqjRF6iUbDd-EmMXy529wFsw.png?1789883206)

## How Prospects Enter the CRM

Prospecting can automatically turn saved businesses into CRM contacts inside the sub-account. The Contact Creation setting controls this behavior and helps determine whether a saved prospect should also become a contact record.

### Contact Creation

Contact Creation is enabled by default and can be managed from the Prospecting settings. When enabled, saving a prospect creates a business contact using the prospect information available at that time.

1. Go to **Marketing → Prospecting**.
2. Open **Settings**.
3. Open **Contacts**.
4. Review the **Contact Creation** setting.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081376400/original/guk6mFRryQFr-9C9cj9cyeBWQv9CyRsU5w.png?1789883289)

When Contact Creation is enabled:

- Saving a prospect creates one business contact in the CRM.
- Available phone numbers, emails, website information, and location data can be mapped into standard contact fields.
- Additional unnamed phone numbers and emails remain attached to the business contact.
- The Contact Source is identified as **Prospecting Tool**.

**Premium enrichment:** Contact Enrichment is a Premium feature and is off by default. When enabled, it can find additional phone numbers, emails, and named points of contact. Named points of contact can be stored as separate CRM contacts depending on the configured Prospecting contact settings.

## How To Automate Prospect Follow-Up

The **Prospect Generated** workflow trigger lets you start automation as soon as a new prospect is generated. Filters help separate leads based on how they entered Prospecting or their conversion potential.

1. Go to **Automation → Workflows**.
2. Create a workflow or open an existing workflow.
3. Add the **Prospect Generated** trigger.
4. Add filters when needed.

Available Prospect Source filters include:

- In-App
- Widget
- Prospect AI

You can also use supported filters such as **Conversion Rate** to create different follow-up paths for higher- or lower-priority prospects.

5. Add the actions you want the workflow to run.
6. Save the trigger and actions.
7. Publish and test the workflow.

Common follow-up actions include:

- Send an email
- Send an SMS
- Add a tag
- Notify a team member
- Create or update an Opportunity
- Start a nurture sequence

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081376270/original/uTKir1Sxihh9dtZDAfSV2IIF2VRn1P0jdg.png?1789882641)

## How To Send Prospect AI Leads to a Pipeline

Prospect AI can automatically route newly discovered prospects into a selected CRM pipeline and stage when the agent is configured inside a sub-account. Pipeline integration is not available for Agency-level Prospect AI agents.

1. Open the applicable sub-account.
2. Go to **Marketing → Prospecting**.
3. Open **Prospect AI**.
4. Open an existing AI agent or create a new one.
5. Click **Edit**.
6. Locate the **Lead Enrichment** portion of the agent configuration.
7. Enable **Save new prospects to Contacts**.
8. Enable **Also add to a pipeline stage**.
9. Select the **Pipeline**.
10. Select the destination **Stage**.
11. Save the agent.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081376354/original/y0rdYNhkfX1LZgdgt4cAfFVkaVmhSrXBJw.png?1789883081)

**Important:** Pipeline settings apply to prospects discovered after the configuration is saved. Existing prospects are not retroactively moved into the selected pipeline or stage.

## How To Migrate Agency Prospects to a Sub-Account

Prospect migration copies existing Agency-level prospects into a Premium-enabled sub-account so the destination team can use its CRM, workflows, pipelines, and communication tools for follow-up.

**Requirement:** The destination sub-account must have an active Prospecting Premium subscription. Only eligible Premium-enabled sub-accounts appear as migration destinations.

1. From **Agency View**, open **Prospecting**.
2. Go to **Settings**.
3. Open **Migrate**.
4. Click **Migrate Prospects**.
5. Select the destination sub-account.
6. Click **Select Prospects**.
7. Select one, multiple, or all eligible prospects.
8. Click **Migrate**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081376500/original/PskKCF08JiUZ9Nbokqe_o-yC4_pUROp-oA.png?1789883745)

After migration, the selected prospects are added to the destination sub-account's Contacts and retain their relevant data, notes, and history. The original prospects remain available at the Agency level for future use.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Why should I use Prospecting inside a sub-account?

Sub-account Prospecting connects lead discovery with CRM tools such as Contacts, Opportunities, workflows, email, and SMS, allowing teams to move directly from discovery to follow-up.

Q: Is the Prospecting Free Tier available in every sub-account?

No. The Free Tier is limited to eligible sub-accounts marked as **Agency Sub-Accounts** and requires the applicable Labs feature.

Q: Why did a Prospecting lead automatically appear in Contacts?

Contact Creation is enabled by default in sub-account Prospecting. When it is on, saving a prospect automatically creates a CRM business contact.

Q: Can I save prospects without automatically creating Contacts?

Yes. Go to **Marketing → Prospecting → Settings → Contacts** and turn off Contact Creation if you want to save prospects without automatically creating CRM contacts.

Q: Can Prospecting trigger workflows?

Yes. Use the **Prospect Generated** workflow trigger. Supported Prospect Source filters include In-App, Widget, and Prospect AI.

Q: Can Prospect AI automatically add prospects to Opportunities?

Yes. At the sub-account level, an eligible Prospect AI agent can save newly discovered prospects to Contacts and add them to a selected pipeline and stage. The configuration applies only to future prospects discovered by that agent.

Q: Can I migrate the same Agency prospect to more than one sub-account?

Yes. Agency prospects remain available after migration and can be copied to other eligible Premium-enabled sub-accounts later.

Q: Can an Agency Prospecting Premium subscription be shared with a sub-account?

Yes. An eligible Agency Prospecting Premium subscription can be linked to one sub-account. Review the current subscription-linking requirements before choosing the sub-account.

title_en: Change an Agency Owner Email When Verification Fails
source_md:
Agency Owner • Login Email • Ownership Transfer

Change an Agency Owner Email When Verification Fails

HighLevel normally lets users change their login email using an available verified authentication method, such as email, SMS, or an Authenticator App. If the Agency Owner cannot complete that standard process, a replacement Agency Admin can be created with the preferred email and Agency Ownership can be transferred to that user. This guide explains when to use the fallback workflow, how to prepare the replacement user, and how to complete the ownership transfer safely.

What You'll Learn

Learn when an ownership-transfer fallback is appropriate, how to create an eligible replacement Agency Admin, how to transfer the Agency Owner role, and when to contact HighLevel Support for account-access assistance.

Important

Do not create a replacement user simply because the current email address cannot receive verification messages. If the existing Agency Owner can verify the login-email change through another available method, such as SMS or an Authenticator App, use the standard email-change process instead.

# What Is the Agency Owner Email Change Fallback Process?

The Agency Owner email change fallback process provides an alternate way to establish the correct Agency Owner login when the standard verified email-change workflow cannot be completed. Instead of modifying the existing user profile, you create another Agency-level Admin using the preferred email address and transfer Agency Ownership to that user.

HighLevel's standard login-email change process can use available verified authentication methods, including email, SMS, or an Authenticator App. If one of those methods lets the current Agency Owner complete the email update successfully, a replacement profile is not necessary.

Use the ownership-transfer workflow only when the standard email change still cannot be completed, account-access issues prevent the normal process, or HighLevel Support directs you to use the replacement-user method.

## Key Benefits of the Agency Owner Email Change Fallback Process

Using a replacement Agency Admin provides a controlled alternative when the current Agency Owner profile cannot complete the normal login-email update. The existing Owner remains in control until the replacement account is ready and ownership is intentionally transferred.

- **Preserves Agency Access:** Keep the existing Agency Owner active until the ownership transfer is complete.
- **Corrects Login Credentials:** Move Agency Ownership to a user profile that contains the correct and accessible email address.
- **Supports Credential Validation:** Test the replacement user's credentials before transferring ownership to reduce the risk of another access issue.
- **Maintains Controlled Ownership Transfer:** Transfer ownership to an eligible Agency Admin through the documented Agency Owner controls.
- **Provides a Support Path:** Escalate login or verification problems to HighLevel Support when the self-service process cannot be completed.

## When to Use This Process

Choosing the standard email-change workflow whenever possible avoids unnecessary user creation and role changes. The replacement-user method is intended for situations where verified login-email changes remain blocked.

Use this fallback workflow when:

- The Agency Owner cannot complete the standard verified login-email change using the available authentication methods.
- The current login email is incorrect or inaccessible and another verification method does not resolve the email-change issue.
- Account-access or verification problems prevent the normal email update from being completed.
- HighLevel Support directs you to create another Agency Admin and transfer Agency Ownership.

**Use the standard process first:** If the existing Agency Owner can verify the login-email change through email, SMS, an Authenticator App, or another available verified method, update the existing profile instead of creating a replacement user.

**Important:** The Agency Owner login email belongs to the individual user profile used to sign in. It is different from the company email configured under Agency Company Settings.

## Before You Begin

Maintaining access to the current Agency Owner is essential because the ownership transfer must be initiated from the current Owner profile. Verify access, the replacement email, and the new user's role before starting the transfer.

- Confirm that you can access the current Agency Owner account.
- Confirm that the preferred replacement email address is correct and accessible.
- Use an available verified authentication method when HighLevel requests identity verification.
- Prepare the replacement user as an Agency-level Admin.
- Contact HighLevel Support before continuing if you cannot access the current Agency Owner account or complete required verification.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081706457/original/cLCIKOYi44doDLIR3FA3nY6DWB9Q9Qtgrw.png?1790217810)

## Requirements for the Replacement User

Agency Ownership can only be transferred to an eligible Agency Admin. Creating the replacement user with the correct user type and role ensures that the user can be selected during the ownership-transfer process.

Configure the replacement profile with:

- The Agency Owner's correct name.
- The correct or preferred login email.
- A valid phone number when applicable.
- **User Type: Agency**
- **Role: Admin**

### Recommended Credential Check

Before transferring ownership, it is a good practice to sign in to the replacement profile and confirm that its credentials and verification methods work. This reduces the risk of transferring ownership to a user who cannot successfully access the agency.

## When to Contact HighLevel Support

Login and verification problems can prevent the current Agency Owner from completing either the standard email update or the ownership-transfer fallback. Escalate the issue before changing roles when secure access to the current Owner profile cannot be maintained.

Contact HighLevel Support when:

- You cannot sign in to the current Agency Owner profile.
- You cannot receive or complete the required verification method.
- The available authentication methods continue to fail.
- The **Transfer Owner** control is unavailable.
- The expected replacement Agency Admin does not appear as an ownership-transfer option after the user has been configured correctly.

If you can access HighLevel, use the Support options available from the Help menu. If you cannot log in, use the external contact options documented in [24/7 Customer Support Options](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000000969).

## How To Change an Agency Owner Email When Verification Fails

Create the replacement Agency Admin before changing ownership, verify that the replacement credentials are usable, and then return to the current Agency Owner profile to complete the transfer. Keeping the current Owner active until the final transfer helps preserve continuous agency access.

### Step 1: Sign In to the Current Agency Owner Account

Start from the current Agency Owner profile because only the current Owner can complete the final ownership transfer.

1. Go to the HighLevel login page.
2. Enter the current Agency Owner login email.
3. Enter the current password.
4. Complete verification using an available verified authentication method.
5. Open **Agency View**.

**Cannot access the current Owner?** Contact HighLevel Support before continuing. Do not attempt to work around an inaccessible Agency Owner account by changing other users or permissions.

### Step 2: Create the Replacement Agency Admin

The ownership target must be an Agency-level Admin. Configure the replacement user with the preferred login email before starting the ownership transfer.

1. From **Agency View**, go to **Settings → Team**.
2. Click **+ Add User**.
3. Enter the Agency Owner's name.
4. Enter the **correct or preferred login email**.
5. Complete the other required user information.
6. Under the user's roles and permissions, set **User Type** to **Agency**.
7. Set the user's **Role** to **Admin**.
8. Save the new user.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081706341/original/YvPc7Qdr4MAzgPD7EKQO0SlMex4CElXOYg.png?1790217368)

### Step 3: Validate the Replacement User

Testing the replacement credentials before transferring ownership helps confirm that the preferred email and authentication setup work correctly.

1. **Log out** of the current Agency Owner profile.
2. Sign in using the newly created Agency Admin's email and credentials.
3. Complete any required authentication or verification.
4. Confirm that the replacement user can successfully access HighLevel.
5. **Log out** of the replacement profile.

**Recommended:** Testing the replacement login is a precaution that confirms the new credentials work before Agency Ownership is moved to that profile.

### Step 4: Transfer Agency Ownership

Return to the current Agency Owner profile to transfer the Agency Owner role to the replacement Agency Admin. An agency can have only one Agency Owner at a time.

1. Sign back in using the **current Agency Owner profile**.
2. Complete the required verification.
3. Go to **Agency View → Settings → Team**.
4. Edit the current Agency Owner.
5. Open **User Roles**.
6. Select **Transfer Owner**.
7. Choose the replacement **Agency Admin**.
8. Confirm the ownership transfer.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081706406/original/e4gZ8_keURAuCr7NhmNlmTTvTNyooivBWg.png?1790217604)

**After the transfer:** The selected Agency Admin becomes the Agency Owner. The previous Agency Owner automatically becomes an Agency Admin.

### Step 5: Verify the New Agency Owner

A final login confirms that the replacement account has the expected Agency Owner access and that the preferred login email is working correctly.

1. Log out of the previous Agency Owner profile.
2. Sign in using the **new Agency Owner email and credentials**.
3. Open **Agency View**.
4. Go to **Settings → Team**.
5. Confirm that the replacement user is identified as the Agency Owner.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081706305/original/qpGu9SYPNBkZpw2vlhk40gMwW9OQDAbksA.gif?1790217170)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Should I always create another user when changing an Agency Owner email?

No. Use the normal login-email change process first. If the Agency Owner can verify the change through an available method such as email, SMS, or an Authenticator App, a replacement user is not necessary.

Q: What if the Agency Owner cannot receive a verification email?

Use another available verified authentication method when possible. If no usable verification method is available or verification continues to fail, contact HighLevel Support.

Q: Why can't I select the replacement user when transferring ownership?

Confirm that the replacement user is configured with **User Type: Agency** and **Role: Admin**. If the correctly configured Agency Admin still does not appear, contact HighLevel Support.

Q: Do I have to sign in to the replacement user before transferring ownership?

Testing the replacement login is recommended because it confirms that the new credentials work before ownership is transferred. The replacement user must still meet the Agency Admin requirements to be an eligible ownership target.

Q: What happens to the previous Agency Owner after ownership is transferred?

The previous Agency Owner automatically becomes an Agency Admin after the ownership transfer is completed.

Q: Can an agency have more than one Agency Owner?

No. An agency can have only one Agency Owner at a time.

Q: Is changing the Agency Company email the same as changing the Agency Owner login email?

No. The Agency Company email is part of the agency's company information. The Agency Owner login email belongs to the individual user profile used to sign in.

Q: What should I do if I cannot log in to the current Agency Owner account at all?

Contact HighLevel Support for account-access assistance before attempting the replacement-user or ownership-transfer workflow.

title_en: Google Dedicated Sending Domain Setup (LC Email)
source_md:
Email Infrastructure

LC Email Dedicated Domain Setup — Google Domains

A step-by-step guide to adding and verifying your dedicated sending domain using Google Domains DNS.

What You'll Learn

This article walks you through connecting a dedicated sending domain to LC Email using Google Domains as your DNS provider. You will add 5 DNS records in total: 2 TXT records, 2 MX records, and 1 CNAME record.

You can set up either your root domain (companyname.com) or a subdomain (e.g. replies.companyname.com). If you already use Google Workspace for email on your root domain, you must use a subdomain instead.

## Add Your Domain in Email Services

Step 1

Navigate to Dedicated Domain settings

In your sub-account, go to **Settings → Email Services → Dedicated Domain** and click **+ Add Domain**.

![Navigating to Settings > Email Services > Dedicated Domain > + Add Domain](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292765242/original/jQLugI8wtvQRfs38XJDujiQd2QnIgjQqSA.gif)

Navigating to Settings → Email Services → Dedicated Domain → + Add Domain

Step 2

Choose your domain type

If your domain is **companyname.com**, you can register either the root domain or a subdomain as your dedicated sending domain.

**Main domain** (companyname.com) — must not already be in use with Google Workspace or another email provider.

**Subdomain** — enter any prefix before your root domain, for example **replies.companyname.com** or **support.companyname.com**.

Note

If you use Google Workspace to send and receive mail on your root domain (e.g. user@companyname.com), you **must** use a subdomain here. Adding the root domain will conflict with your existing Google Workspace MX records. See [Can I use the same domain for Mailgun and Google Apps?](https://help.mailgun.com/hc/en-us/articles/203357040-Can-I-Use-the-Same-Domain-Name-for-Mailgun-and-for-Google-Apps-Or-Another-Email-Server-)

Step 3

Click Add & Verify

After entering your domain name, click **Add & Verify**. The next screen will display the 5 DNS records you need to add. Keep this tab open — you will copy values from it in the steps below.

![Add & Verify button](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292766472/original/5TxDqQG542C3YtKLt6stGIAfwcbDmmcesg.png)
![DNS records screen showing 5 records to add](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48293298198/original/xGMUZ9x0JoahqbofrVsYVWEjEF9LDDvsMQ.png)

Keep this DNS records screen open — you will copy values from it in the steps below.

Tip

Migrating from Mailgun? See [How to move a sending domain from Mailgun to LeadConnector](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001226115-how-to-set-up-a-dedicated-sending-domain-lc-email-#How-to-move-sending-domain-from-Mailgun-to-LeadConnector?).

## Open Google Domains DNS

In a new browser tab, log in to [domains.google.com](https://domains.google.com/), click into the domain you are setting up, then click **DNS** in the left panel. You will add all 5 records here.

![Google Domains DNS panel](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48299273463/original/nvtEdnUCOa_aEuQG29TmvxEc8zT-TEDQbw.png)

Reminder

Do **not** click Save after each individual record. Add all 5 records first, then save once at the end.

DNS Setup Guide

Adding Your 5 DNS Records

Follow sections 3–6 to add 2 TXT records, 2 MX records, and 1 CNAME. Don't save until all 5 are entered.

## Add the 1st TXT Record (SPF)

Click **Create new record** in Google Domains and fill in the fields below.

Host Name

Enter only the subdomain prefix — do not include the root domain

Google Domains appends your root domain automatically. Enter only the prefix part:

- Setting up **lc**.companyname.com → enter **lc**
- Setting up **replies**.companyname.com → enter **replies**
- Setting up root domain companyname.com → enter **@**

![Host name field in Google Domains — enter subdomain prefix only](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48299273966/original/QyOvl4oeTZwm5vxk_Qr4E9axVI_3VmGQbQ.png)

Type

Select **TXT** from the Type dropdown.

Data — same for everyone

Paste the following SPF record value exactly as shown:

v=spf1 include:mailgun.org ~all

![SPF TXT record filled in Google Domains](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292767368/original/n_1Mu3Av0f2EYEvZG9iBeM-knKybDa2RPg.png)

Next Step

Do **not** click Save yet. Click **Create new record** to continue to the 2nd TXT record.

## Add the 2nd TXT Record (DKIM)

Important

Everyone's 2nd TXT record hostname and value is **unique to their domain**. Copy both values directly from your platform's DNS records screen — do not use values from screenshots in this article.

Type

Select **TXT** from the dropdown.

![Selecting TXT from the type dropdown](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48299274267/original/tgkjiuJTNQWqB0YufpMnGh7eGG8ju2BhYQ.png)

Host Name

Copy everything before your root domain — do not include the root domain itself

Look at the 2nd TXT hostname in your DNS records screen. Copy only the portion before your root domain name. The examples below show which part to copy.

![2nd TXT host name field — copy highlighted portion only](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48299274349/original/QZx8yVWaSu8EU88v7eBp1CPDH4P80GKGXg.png)

| Scenario | Copy this as hostname | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Using a subdomain | mx.\_domainkey.helpdesk | Subdomain DKIM hostname example |
| Using the root domain | mailo.\_domainkey | Root domain DKIM hostname example |

Data

Paste the full 2nd TXT record value from your platform's DNS records screen. This value is unique to your domain — copy it as-is from the highlighted field.

![2nd TXT record value — copy the highlighted value](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292768735/original/cUIeRsQGsIF81ZCW8a-cj-v7iGlndoLiKw.png)

Next Step

Do **not** click Save yet. Click **Create new record** to add the MX records.

## Add MX Records

Click **Create new record** in Google Domains and fill in the fields below.

Google Workspace Users

If you have a Google Workspace account that sends and receives mail on your root domain, adding MX records to the root domain will break existing email. Use a subdomain for LC Email. See [Can I use the same domain for Mailgun and Google Apps?](https://help.mailgun.com/hc/en-us/articles/203357040-Can-I-Use-the-Same-Domain-Name-for-Mailgun-and-for-Google-Apps-Or-Another-Email-Server-)

Host Name

Same logic as the TXT records — enter only the subdomain prefix:

- **lc**.companyname.com → enter **lc**
- **replies**.companyname.com → enter **replies**
- Root domain companyname.com → enter **@**

![MX record host name field](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000003027/original/5aF_dZ_ziXuTz59XlBASIHTyI7uQ7bOo_g.png)

Type

Select **MX** from the dropdown.

Data

Paste the first MX value, then click **+ Add more to this record** and paste the second:

10 mxa.mailgun.org

10 mxb.mailgun.org

![MX records data entry](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000003013/original/7ZgVLhVdhJ7tXtoJ_8k_TFkrR5RA2pUb4g.png)
![MX records completed](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000003080/original/w3lgIZMfVu8zipEIyYvMh72IQgpl6HADcA.png)

Next Step

Do **not** click Save yet. Click **Create new record** to add the final CNAME record.

## Add the CNAME Record

Click **Create new record** in Google Domains and fill in the fields below.

Host Name

The CNAME hostname is prefixed with **email.** followed by your subdomain prefix:

- lc.companyname.com → enter **email.lc**
- replies.companyname.com → enter **email.replies**
- Root domain companyname.com → enter **email**

Type

Select **CNAME** from the dropdown.

Data — same for everyone

mailgun.org

![CNAME record fields filled in](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000003126/original/UjjcYWc_abbbgStIJ5Q7rOwoXfIFdaAT4g.png)
![CNAME record completed](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155000003129/original/4CjEilgb6jZy-PnRXT7Eyoxf94_AeHGPcw.png)

All 5 Records Added

You have now entered all 5 DNS records. Proceed to Section 7 to save and verify.

## Save & Verify Your Domain

Step 1

Save in Google Domains

Now that all 5 DNS records are entered, click **Save** in Google Domains.

Step 2

Verify in Email Services

Switch back to the platform tab and click **Verify Domain** on the Email Services screen.

![Verify Domain button in Email Services](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/48292771391/original/DSHng9iQ27K8gMmkLYLkL7mpGKnMfyFSkA.png)

Some records still not green?

DNS propagation can take a few minutes. Click **Verify Domain** again after waiting a moment. If records remain unverified after 10+ minutes, double-check the values you entered in Google Domains against the platform's DNS records screen.

You're All Set

Once all records show a green checkmark, your dedicated sending domain is active. Next, confirm your [SSL Certificate for Dedicated Sending Domain (LC Email)](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001227438) is properly set up.

Then send a test email to confirm everything is working. [Learn how to send a test email in the Conversation.](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001208887)

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I use my root domain if I already use it with Google Workspace?

No. Adding MX records for a root domain that is already used with Google Workspace will conflict with your existing Google Workspace MX records and break email delivery. Use a subdomain (e.g. **replies.companyname.com**) for LC Email instead.

Q: How long does DNS propagation take in Google Domains?

Changes in Google Domains typically propagate within a few minutes, though it can occasionally take up to 24–48 hours. If records are not verifying after 10 minutes, wait a bit and try again before troubleshooting values.

Q: Why is the 2nd TXT record hostname different from examples I see online?

The 2nd TXT record is a DKIM key that is generated uniquely for your domain. Its hostname and value will always differ from other accounts. Always copy both from your own DNS records screen — never from this article or another account's setup.

Q: What is the difference between a dedicated domain and a shared domain?

A **shared domain** is a common sending domain shared across multiple accounts — quick to enable, but your sender reputation is pooled with others. A **dedicated domain** is exclusive to your account, giving you full control over your sender reputation and deliverability.

Q: Can I set up multiple dedicated domains for different sub-accounts?

Yes. Each sub-account can have its own dedicated sending domain. Each domain requires its own set of DNS records to be added and verified separately.

Q: Will my contacts notice a change after I switch to a dedicated domain?

Not directly — the sending domain appears in email headers but not in the visible "From" name. Over time, a dedicated domain improves deliverability as your sender reputation builds independently.

Q: My domain shows as verified but emails still aren't delivering — what should I check?

Send a test email from the Conversations area first to confirm basic sending works. Then check that the [SSL Certificate for your Dedicated Sending Domain](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/48001227438) is active. If issues persist, review your SPF and DKIM values in Google Domains for any typos.

Q: Is there a cost to use a dedicated sending domain?

Setting up a dedicated sending domain through LC Email does not require a separate paid plan beyond your existing subscription. You do need to own and manage the domain through your DNS provider (in this case, Google Domains).

title_en: How to Filter and View Associated Records in Smart Lists
source_md:
HighLevel lets you filter Contacts by records associated with them, such as Companies, Pets, and Policies. You can save these filters as Smart Lists and display linked records directly in the Contacts table. Association columns help you review relationships without opening each Contact. This article explains how to filter Contacts, save Smart Lists, and customize association columns.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Association Filters and Columns in Smart Lists?](#What-Are-Association-Filters-and-Columns-in-Smart-Lists?)
- [Key Benefits of Association Filters and Columns](#Key-Benefits-of-Association-Filters-and-Columns)
- [How to Filter Contacts by Associated Records](#How-to-Filter-Contacts-by-Associated-Records)
- [How to Display Association Columns](#How-to-Display-Association-Columns)
- [Understanding Association Labels](#Understanding-Association-Labels)
- [Association Filter Operators](#Association-Filter-Operators)
- [Viewing Associated Records in Columns](#Viewing-Associated-Records-in-Columns)
- [Primary Company and Additional Company](#Primary-Company-and-Additional-Company)
- [Custom Object Associations](#Custom-Object-Associations)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What Are Association Filters and Columns in Smart Lists?**

Association filters find Contacts based on their relationships with other records. Association columns display those linked records in the Contacts table.

For example, a veterinary clinic can filter Contacts associated with pets named Mango or Jasper, save the results as a Smart List, and display each Contact's associated pets.

An **association label** describes the relationship between records, such as *Owned Pet*, *Additional Company*, or *Policy*.

These features use existing associations; they do not create new relationships.

---

## **Key Benefits of Association Filters and Columns**

Association filters and columns help you organize Contacts using the relationships most relevant to your business.

- **Targeted Segmentation:** Find Contacts linked to specific Companies, Pets, Policies, or other supported records.
- **Reusable Smart Lists:** Save association filters for future use.
- **Better Visibility:** View linked records directly in the Contacts table.
- **Relationship-Based Filtering:** Find Contacts with or without associations.
- **Clearer Company Details:** Distinguish Primary Company from other Company relationships.
- **Customizable Columns:** Display only the association labels you need.

---

## **How to Filter Contacts by Associated Records**

Association filters let you find Contacts based on specific linked records. The following example finds Contacts associated with Mango or Jasper.

### **Step 1: Open Filters**

1. Go to **Contacts → Smart Lists**.
2. Open the Contact list you want to filter.
3. Click **Filters**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084297142/original/N01KLdcvwGUEBhZfbHYpbsH28d1-FYgBKw.png?1793100206)

### **Step 2: Choose an Association Field**

1. Expand **Associations** in the Filters panel.
2. Select the relationship you want to filter.

For this example, select **Owned Pet (Associated Pet)**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084297405/original/d1-Kk4NT870QryhCMoQOQgc48-0IbIrq9w.png?1793100263)

### **Step 3: Select an Operator**

1. Open the operator dropdown.
2. Choose the operator that matches your goal.

For this example, select **Contains any**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084297479/original/hNJTvxTOLa4LHh5elOsY8-WtXpLwQbplEA.png?1793100309)

### **Step 4: Select Records and Apply**

1. Select the associated records you want to match.
2. Click **Apply**.

For this example, select **Mango** and **Jasper**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084297625/original/TJGi_qrC_4TfH8EmEE0ubVhkLdwKIAY-pA.png?1793100381)

### **Step 5: Review Matching Contacts**

The Contacts table displays records matching the applied filter.

Review the results to confirm they match your intended audience.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084297754/original/y-5lks8Gm6_Hvc_Qlwu5imaY5Eh_t-X3Gg.png?1793100423)

### **Step 6: Save the Smart List**

Saving your filter lets you reopen the segment without configuring it again.

1. Click **Unsaved changes**.
2. Select **Save as new smartlist**.
3. Enter a name.
4. Click **Create**.

The saved Smart List appears as a tab.

```
Tip: Combine association filters with other Contact filters to create more specific audiences.
```

---

## **How to Display Association Columns**

Association columns let you see linked records beside Contact information.

### **Step 1: Open Manage Fields**

1. Go to **Contacts → Smart Lists**.
2. Open the relevant Contact list.
3. Click the column-count control to open **Manage fields**.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084297990/original/upddgkxEaEUSMl7Jb5-E6y7mm8qulQp5Uw.png?1793100525)

### **Step 2: Select Association Labels**

1. Expand **Associations** under Add fields.
2. Select the relationship labels you want to display.
3. Click **Apply**.

For example, select Additional Company, Policy, Owned Pet, and Car.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084298183/original/liwR4gKFdHhUiUUSLF4SBcUMyXGAQe9ggQ.png?1793100641)

### **Step 3: Review the Added Columns**

The selected relationships appear as separate columns in the Contacts table.

Each column displays records associated through its selected label.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084298253/original/NVJlvvoyVmDW8KQSdCIdiBE3x4yat4qC7g.png?1793100681)

### **Step 4: View Additional Linked Records**

If a cell contains more linked records than it displays, hover over **+N** to see additional entries.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084298342/original/rdqdhGSnCAUVHAIasnt4gQ2OwNFeM2RGcQ.png?1793100734)

```
Tip: Select only the association columns needed for your workflow to keep the table easy to read.
```

  

---

## **Understanding Association Labels**

Association labels describe how records are connected. Different labels can represent different relationships to the same type of record.

| Association Label | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Primary Company | A Contact's primary linked Company |
| Additional Company | Other Companies associated with the Contact |
| Owned Pet | Pets linked to the Contact |
| Policy | Policies linked to the Contact |
| Car | Cars linked to the Contact |

Available labels depend on the objects and relationships configured in your HighLevel location.

For setup instructions, see [Associating Contacts using Custom Labels](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003918-associating-contacts-using-custom-labels).

## **Association Filter Operators**

Association filters provide four operators for finding Contacts based on linked records.

| Operator | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Contains any** | Find Contacts linked to at least one selected record |
| **Does not contain any** | Find Contacts not linked to the selected records |
| **Is not empty** | Find Contacts with a record linked under the selected label |
| **Is empty** | Find Contacts without a record linked under the selected label |

For example, select **Owned Pet (Associated Pet)**, choose **Contains any**, and select **Mango** and **Jasper** to find Contacts linked to either pet.

**Contains any** and **Does not contain any** require record selection. **Is empty** and **Is not empty** check whether a relationship exists under the selected label.

```
Note: Does not contain any is different from Is empty. The exact handling of Contacts with no associations under Does not contain any should be verified.
```

  

---

## **Viewing Associated Records in Columns**

Association columns display linked records directly in the Contacts table.

You can select individual relationship labels through **Manage fields → Associations**. Each label appears as a separate column, even when multiple labels refer to the same object type.

### **Linked-Record Chips and +N**

Linked records appear as chips containing their names.

When more records are linked than can be displayed in a cell, a **+N** indicator appears. Hover over the indicator to view additional records.

The release also describes opening a linked record by selecting its chip.

---

## **Primary Company and Additional Company**

The **Primary Company** column identifies a Contact's primary linked Company. It replaces the previous *Company name* column label described in the release.

Other Company relationships, such as **Additional Company**, can appear in separate association columns.

This helps distinguish primary Company information from additional relationships.

```
Note: The updated column label does not establish changes to existing Company records or association limits.
```

---

## **Custom Object Associations**

Supported Custom Object associations can also appear in Contact filters and columns.

For example, a location with a configured Pet object and Owned Pet relationship can use that label to filter Contacts associated with specific pets.

Available options depend on the objects and relationships configured in your location.

For object setup instructions, see [Creating and Editing Custom Objects](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003897).

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What is an association label?**

A: It identifies the relationship between records, such as Owned Pet or Additional Company.

**Q: Can I filter by multiple associated records?**

A: Yes. Use Contains any and select multiple records to find Contacts linked to at least one of them.

**Q: How do I find Contacts without a particular relationship?**

A: Select the association label and choose Is empty.

**Q: What is the difference between Contains any and Is not empty?**

A: Contains any matches selected records. Is not empty checks whether a linked record exists under the chosen label.

**Q: Can I combine association filters with other filters?**

A: Yes. Association filters can be combined with other Contact filters.

**Q: Can I save my association filters?**

A: Yes. Apply the filters, then select Unsaved changes → Save as new smartlist.

**Q: Why can't I see a particular association label?**

A: Available labels depend on the objects and relationships configured in your location.

**Q: What does +N mean in an association column?**

A: It indicates additional linked records that are not currently displayed in the cell.

**Q: Are Primary Company and Additional Company the same?**

A: No. Primary Company identifies the primary linked Company, while Additional Company represents a separate labeled relationship.

**Q: Can I filter Contacts using Custom Object associations?**

A: Supported Custom Object associations can be used where available. The options depend on your location's configured objects and relationships.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [How to Create & Manage Smart Lists](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001062094-how-to-create-manage-smart-lists)
- [Advanced Filters in Smart Lists](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007530-advanced-filters-in-smart-lists)
- [Associating Contacts using Custom Labels](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003918-associating-contacts-using-custom-labels)
- [Contacts – Revamped List View & SmartLists](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006504)
- [Creating and Editing Custom Objects](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003897)
- [Company Object Feature: A Manual Way to Organize Contacts](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001223777)
