- [What is the Transfer Bot Action?](#What-is-the-Transfer-Bot-Action?%E2%80%8B)
- [Key Benefits of Transfer Bot Action](#Key-Benefits-of-Transfer-Bot-Action%E2%80%8B)
- [How to Configure the Transfer Bot Action](#How-to-Configure-the-Transfer-Bot-Action%E2%80%8B)
- [Transfer Bot Action Requirements](#Transfer-Bot-Action-Requirements%E2%80%8B)
- [Transfer to Another Bot](#Transfer-to-Another-Bot%E2%80%8B)
- [Using Trigger Conditions and Example Phrases](#Using-Trigger-Conditions-and-Example-Phrases%E2%80%8B)
- [Important Workflow Note](#Important-Workflow-Note%E2%80%8B)
- [Best Practices for Transfer Bot Action](#Best-Practices-for-Transfer-Bot-Action)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions%E2%80%8B)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles%E2%80%8B)

---

## **What is the Transfer Bot Action?**

The Transfer Bot Action allows a Conversation AI bot to hand off a conversation to another AI bot when a specific intent, phrase, or condition is detected. Instead of building one large bot to handle every possible scenario, you can create specialized bots for different services, departments, languages, or customer needs.

For example, if a contact starts with a general service bot but mentions “My AC is not working,” the conversation can automatically transfer to an AC repair bot configured to handle that specific service.

---

## **Key Benefits of Transfer Bot Action**

The Transfer Bot Action improves bot routing, simplifies automation setup, and helps contacts reach the right AI agent faster.

- **Improves user experience:** Routes contacts to the most relevant bot based on what they need.
- **Reduces complex workflows:** Allows bot-to-bot handoffs without building unnecessary workflow branches.
- **Supports modular bot setups:** Lets businesses create separate bots for different services, teams, departments, or languages.
- **Improves automation accuracy:** Keeps each bot focused on a specific topic or use case.
- **Preserves conversation flow:** Helps the destination bot continue the conversation naturally after the transfer.
- **Simplifies bot maintenance:** Makes it easier to update individual bots instead of managing one large bot.

---

## **How to Configure the Transfer Bot Action**

Proper setup ensures the source bot can identify when a transfer is needed and route the conversation to the correct destination bot. Both bots should be active, compatible, and configured before enabling the transfer.

1. From your sub-account, navigate to **AI Agents**.
2. Select **Conversation AI** from the top navigation.
3. Open the **Agents List** tab.
4. Click the three-dot menu next to the bot you want to edit.
5. Select **Edit**.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072660209/original/XDJHljwzVjx-WlXhCn32pa5GCra41T4-wQ.png?1780377865)**

6. Open the **Bot Goals** tab.
7. Under **Setup your Actions**, click **Transfer Bot**.  
     
   Note: If you don't see the Transfer Bot button, open the **Flow Editor** with the **Edit Flow Builder**button, add an action, and search for "transfer" then click**Transfer Bot.**  
     
   Note: If you see a totally different editor when you open the bot for editing, then click **Setup Your Actions** and click Transfer Bot in the dropdown.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072660313/original/VVMaW8SY1OU9lOM5RmmTsnpM5JqlwbZZtA.png?1780377955)**

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080790179/original/Ly_7l6eVghMaLtvuQt0mO0F8wdmk-yMCfg.png?1789243091)  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080790346/original/7__d-qSUNTEajWJjCEqKGrrKEQLCwFhVtQ.png?1789243464)

8. In the **Bot Transfer** window, enter an **Action name**. Use a clear name that explains where the conversation will be transferred, such as “Transfer to AC Repairing Bot.”

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072660372/original/lK2kq4vNYRyfy5ayx_MezQBxY1_b5fQdUg.png?1780378010)**

9. Select the destination bot from the **Select Bot to Transfer to** dropdown.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072660464/original/2emfeweEMaZNgs_0gznzCWYIrCr4rtupVw.png?1780378094)**

10. Confirm that the current bot and selected bot are compatible. The bots should be active on the same channel and both should be in **Auto Pilot** mode.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072660510/original/PeMEFZl2Ohysc7PSXnIuFoOGQmdB0Nqhhg.png?1780378117)**

11. Add a **Trigger Condition** to define when the transfer should happen. For example: “The customer says AC repairing or needs AC repairing services.”

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072660527/original/Q3AtGLKvB-Sk7DzhPP5viycgozcsLvL_hg.png?1780378146)**

12. Add **Example Phrases** that contacts may use to trigger the transfer action. For example: “AC repairing,” “My AC is not working,” or “I need AC repair.”

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072660530/original/3xP_mJSmrdeUfr1rccI_dG5VAAY8yGRXsg.png?1780378168)**

13. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

---

## **Transfer Bot Action Requirements**

Transfer Bot Action depends on compatibility between the source bot and destination bot. If these requirements are not met, the transfer may not work as expected.

- The source bot and destination bot must be active on the same channel.
- For example, if the source bot is active on Live Chat, the destination bot must also be active on Live Chat.
- Both bots must be in **Auto Pilot** mode.
- The destination bot should be published and tested before using it in a live transfer.
- Trigger conditions and example phrases should be specific enough to avoid accidental transfers.

---

## **Transfer to Another Bot**

Transferring to another bot is useful when your business has multiple services, departments, or conversation paths that are better handled by separate AI agents. This allows each bot to stay focused while still creating a connected experience for the contact.

Common examples include:

- A general intake bot transferring to a sales bot.
- A support bot transferring to a billing bot.
- A home services bot transferring to an HVAC, plumbing, electrical, or roofing bot.
- A multilingual bot transferring to a language-specific bot.
- A general appointment bot transferring to a service-specific booking bot.

Example: A contact asks, “Do you repair AC units?” The general services bot detects the intent and transfers the conversation to the AC repair bot.

---

## **Using Trigger Conditions and Example Phrases**

Trigger conditions tell Conversation AI when the transfer should happen. Example phrases help the bot understand the types of contact messages that should match the transfer scenario.

Use clear, realistic phrases that contacts are likely to send, such as:

- “My AC is not working.”
- “I need help with billing.”
- “Can I book a dental cleaning?”
- “I want to speak with someone about roofing.”
- “Do you offer emergency plumbing?”

Avoid vague trigger conditions that could match too many conversations. Specific examples help improve transfer accuracy.

---

## **Important Workflow Note**

If you are using the **Update Conversation AI Bot and Status** workflow action, add a **Wait** step before or after the update action as needed. Without a Wait step, the original bot may continue reassigning the conversation, which can break the transfer logic.

Use this note when combining Transfer Bot Action with workflow automation:

Add a Wait step when using the Update Conversation AI Bot and Status workflow action to prevent the original bot from reassigning the conversation and interrupting the transfer.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155072660830/original/rzrC0LtdqopjE57rsbnqCtFltrEOxM-9Eg.png?1780378485)**

---

## **Best Practices for Transfer Bot Action**

A well-configured transfer creates a smoother handoff and helps prevent contacts from reaching the wrong bot or experiencing a dead end.

- Use clear action names that describe the destination bot.
- Keep each bot focused on a specific topic, service, department, or language.
- Make sure all destination bots are published before selecting them.
- Confirm that both bots are active on the same communication channel.
- Keep both bots in **Auto Pilot** mode.
- Test each transfer scenario before using it with live contacts.
- Add enough example phrases to help Conversation AI understand user intent.
- Avoid overlapping trigger conditions across multiple transfer scenarios.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: What does the Transfer Bot Action do?**  
The Transfer Bot Action transfers a conversation from one Conversation AI bot to another bot based on user intent, trigger conditions, or example phrases.

**Q: Can I transfer a conversation to any bot?**  
You can transfer to a compatible destination bot. The source and destination bots must be active on the same channel, and both bots must be in Auto Pilot mode.

**Q: Will the conversation history be preserved after transfer?**  
Yes. The conversation context is preserved so the destination bot can continue the conversation more naturally.

**Q: Why is my transfer not working?**  
The most common causes are channel mismatch, one of the bots not being in Auto Pilot mode, the destination bot not being published, or trigger conditions that are too vague.

**Q: Can I use Transfer Bot Action instead of building complex workflows?**  
Yes. Transfer Bot Action can reduce the need for complex workflow routing by allowing one bot to hand off the conversation directly to another bot.

**Q: What happens if I use the Update Conversation AI Bot and Status workflow action?**  
Add a Wait step when using this workflow action. Without it, the original bot may keep reassigning the conversation and break the transfer logic.

**Q: Can I use Transfer Bot Action for different departments or services?**  
Yes. You can create separate bots for sales, support, billing, service booking, or other departments and transfer contacts based on their needs.

**Q: Should the destination bot be tested before using it?**  
Yes. Always publish and test the destination bot before enabling it in a live transfer scenario.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Conversation AI Bot - Explained](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000001335)
- [Setting Up Conversation AI](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000004401)
- [Conversation AI Flow Builder](https://help.gohighlevel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/155000006515)

title_en: How to Use Your Automatically Created Profile and Business Cards
source_md:
HighLevel automatically creates a personal Profile Card and a shared Business Card the first time an authorized user opens the QR icon in a sub-account. Both cards use existing account information, so you can start sharing without building them manually. You can customize card details and appearance, share cards by link or QR code, track scans, and optionally collect leads through Exchange Contact. This guide explains how to access, customize, share, and manage permissions for automatically generated Profile and Business Cards.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What Are Automatically Generated Profile and Business Cards?](#what-are-profile-business-cards)
- [Key Benefits of Profile and Business Cards](#key-benefits)
- [Prerequisites and Limitations](#prerequisites-limitations)
- [How to Set Up and Use Your Cards](#set-up-use-cards)
- [Card Permissions and System Folders](#permissions-system-folders)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#frequently-asked-questions)
- [Related Articles](#related-articles)

---

# **What Are Automatically Generated Profile and Business Cards?**

Profile and Business Cards are digital cards that share personal or business information through a link or QR code. HighLevel creates both cards automatically the first time an authorized user opens the QR icon in a sub-account.

| **Card** | **Details** | **Access** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Profile Card** | Uses your name, title, and contact details. | Personal to each team member. |
| **Business Card** | Uses the sub-account's business information. | Shared by users with the appropriate permission. |

Each card has its own shareable link, downloadable QR code, and scan analytics. You can update the card later without creating it again.

---

## **Key Benefits of Profile and Business Cards**

Automatically generated cards make it easier to share contact information while providing customization, lead collection, and scan tracking.

- **Ready to use:** Both cards are created automatically using existing account details.
- **Easy sharing:** Copy a link, download a QR code, or save a supported QR code to a digital wallet.
- **Custom links:** Add X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, YouTube, websites, booking pages, portfolios, and other links.
- **Contact sharing:** Let visitors save your contact details directly to their phones.
- **Lead capture:** Enable Exchange Contact to collect visitor details in your CRM.
- **Scan analytics:** Track how often each card is scanned.
- **Flexible design:** Customize card colors, appearance, and landing-page details.

---

## **Prerequisites and Limitations**

Access to automatically generated cards depends on the user's QR Codes access and card permissions. View access allows a user to view and share a card, while Manage access is required to edit it.

- You must have **QR Codes** access and the appropriate card permission.
- **Save Contact** is enabled automatically on both cards.
- **Exchange Contact** is disabled by default.
- Regular users can access only their own Profile Cards.
- The Business Card is shared within the sub-account.
- These permissions do not affect manually created QR codes.

```
Note: If a user does not have permission to access either card, the QR icon is not displayed.
```

---

## **How to Set Up and Use Your Cards**

Profile and Business Cards are generated automatically on first access, so no manual card creation is required. Once available, you can review their information, customize them, and share them with others.

### **Access Your Profile and Business Cards**

The QR icon in the top navigation bar provides quick access to both cards from inside a sub-account.

1. Open your HighLevel **Sub-Account**.
2. Click the **QR icon** in the top navigation bar.
3. On first access, HighLevel automatically generates your Profile Card and the sub-account's Business Card.
4. Review the cards shown in the popover. Available actions depend on your permissions.

![Top navigation QR icon showing automatically generated Profile and Business Cards](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084015809/original/zIgYBaq87MQejLor6BP1M_ToOwi7kkZVIw.png?1792728115)

### **Customize Your Cards**

Both cards remain editable after automatic creation. Users with Manage permission can update card information, links, and appearance.

1. From your **Sub-Account**, click the **QR icon**.
2. Locate the card you want to customize.
3. Open the card editor.
4. Update the available personal or business details.
5. Add social profiles or custom links, such as a website, email address, booking page, or portfolio.
6. Adjust the card's design, colors, or landing-page options as needed.
7. Save your changes.

![Profile and Business Card editor showing customization options](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084015996/original/hoS_dSptOzlkU_XMTZ9oUMg6qdQ4k-GdxQ.png?1792728806)

### **Enable Exchange Contact to Collect Leads**

Exchange Contact allows someone viewing your card to submit their information through a form. When submitted, HighLevel creates a CRM contact and records which card generated the submission.

1. From your **Sub-Account**, click the **QR icon**.
2. Open a card you have permission to manage.

![Card editor showing the Exchange Contact option](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084016306/original/kWPxzOQtB5c8EV-1mLSTw08GE_dnGo2IYw.png?1792729712)

3. Open the card's **Exchange Contact** settings and enable the feature.
4. Choose the available built-in form option or select an existing HighLevel form.
5. Review the configuration and save your changes.

![Exchange Contact settings and form selection](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084016427/original/DDF6NScykxV_Jggi3fpEv1Yf8Z8zUjkqJQ.png?1792730024)

```
Note: Exchange Contact is optional. Visitors can still use Save Contact to save your details without submitting their own information.
```

### **Share Your Cards and Review Scans**

Each card has its own link and QR code. You can share the card digitally, download its QR code for print or in-person use, and review scan activity.

1. From your **Sub-Account**, click the **QR icon**.
2. Locate the card you want to share.
3. Use the available sharing controls to copy the card link or download its QR code.
4. Share the link online or use the QR code on printed materials.
5. Open the card's analytics to review scan activity.

![Card sharing controls and QR code scan analytics](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084017058/original/cKeEM8gScPUc40kUVcMNjB0LmuowUx7bSg.png?1792731648)

---

## **Card Permissions and System Folders**

HighLevel provides separate permissions for personal Profile Cards and the shared Business Card. System folders keep automatically generated cards organized separately from manually created QR codes.

### **Manage Card Permissions**

Administrators can control which users can view or manage automatically generated cards.

1. Open the relevant HighLevel **Sub-Account**.
2. Select **Settings** from the left navigation.
3. Click **Users**.
4. Open the user whose permissions you want to change.
5. Select **Roles & Permissions**.
6. Find the **QR Codes** permission area and enable the required QR Codes access.

![QR Codes permissions for Profile and Business Cards](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084016918/original/_tHWp7gQTYo7tP548iJx09y-20u-ZakaZA.png?1792731284)

7. Configure the appropriate card permissions.
8. Click **Save**.

**The four card permissions are:**

| **Permission** | **What It Allows** |
| --- | --- |
| **View location level business card** | View the Business Card, analytics, and downloads. |
| **View & manage location level business card** | View and edit the shared Business Card. |
| **View user level profile card** | View permitted Profile Cards, analytics, and downloads. |
| **View & manage user level profile card** | View and edit permitted Profile Cards. |

**Important permission rules:**

- **Manage includes View.** You do not need to enable both.
- The four permissions are enabled by default for users, subject to QR Codes access.
- Disabling QR Codes access clears and disables the card permissions.
- Regular users can access only their own Profile Cards.
- Administrators with the appropriate permission can manage other users' Profile Cards.
- Users with Business Card access see the same shared card for their sub-account.

### **Find Cards in System Folders**

Automatically generated cards are stored in protected system folders separately from manually created QR codes.

1. From your HighLevel **Sub-Account**, select **Sites**.
2. Open **QR Codes**.
3. Locate the **System folders** section.
4. Open **Profile Cards** or **Business Cards** to view the cards available to your role.

![QR Codes System folders for Profile Cards and Business Cards](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155084016881/original/EJJ3Mqrw_TPbRKOCF2mrzI4G1aKLPhsfZA.png?1792731169)

```
Note: System folders cannot be renamed or deleted, and new QR codes cannot be created inside them. Automatically generated cards remain editable when the user has the appropriate Manage permission.
```

Only agency or sub-account administrators with matching permissions can access these cards through the QR Codes list. Regular users can access their own Profile Card through the top-bar QR icon.

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Why can't I see the QR icon?**

You need QR Codes access and the appropriate card permission. If neither card is accessible, the QR icon is hidden.

**Q: Can someone save my contact information without sharing theirs?**

Yes. **Save Contact** is enabled automatically. **Exchange Contact** is separate and optional.

**Q: Can I use an existing HighLevel form for Exchange Contact?**

Yes. You can select an existing form instead of using the built-in form option.

**Q: Can team members edit the shared Business Card?**

Only users with the appropriate Business Card Manage permission can edit it.

**Q: Do these card permissions change my existing QR codes?**

No. The four card permissions apply only to automatically generated Profile Cards and Business Cards.

---

### **Related Articles**

- [How to Create Custom Profile Card QR Codes](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008361-how-to-create-custom-profile-card-qr-codes)
- [How to Create Custom Business Card QR Codes](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005740)
- [Manage QR Codes with Search, Filters, Views, and Bulk Actions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006540-manage-qr-codes-with-search-filters-views-and-bulk-actions)
- [Sub-account: User Roles, Permissions and Assigned data](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000002544)
- [Saving QR Codes to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000009239-saving-qr-codes-to-apple-wallet-or-google-wallet)

title_en: Ring Incoming Calls to Multiple Users
source_md:
Phone System

# Ring Incoming Calls to Multiple Users

Distribute incoming calls across multiple team members simultaneously to improve response times and ensure no call goes unanswered.

What You'll Learn

This article explains how to configure ring groups in HighLevel to simultaneously ring multiple team members when a call comes in. You'll learn how to set up call distribution, manage ring strategies, and optimize your team's call handling workflow.

Ring groups help businesses improve call coverage, reduce missed opportunities, and ensure customers connect with available team members faster.

## What is Multiple User Ring?

Multiple User Ring, also known as ring groups or simultaneous ring, is a call distribution feature that rings multiple team members' phones at the same time when an incoming call arrives at your HighLevel phone number.

When a caller dials your business number, the system rings all designated users simultaneously. The first team member to answer the call connects with the caller, while the other phones automatically stop ringing. This ensures faster call pickup times and reduces the likelihood of missed calls.

Ring groups are ideal for sales teams, customer support departments, and any business scenario where multiple people need to be available to handle incoming calls without routing callers through a time-consuming menu system.

## Key Benefits

Configuring multiple users to receive incoming calls provides several operational and customer experience advantages.

**Faster Response Times** — Callers connect with an available team member immediately without waiting in queue or listening to hold music.

**Reduced Missed Calls** — If one team member is unavailable or busy, another can answer the call, minimizing lost opportunities.

**Improved Customer Satisfaction** — Customers appreciate immediate human connection rather than navigating phone trees or waiting on hold.

**Better Team Collaboration** — All team members have equal opportunity to engage with incoming leads and customers.

**Flexible Coverage** — Teams can maintain call coverage during breaks, meetings, or varied schedules without formal call forwarding.

**Scalable Distribution** — Add or remove team members from ring groups as your business needs change without complex configuration.

## Ring Strategy Options

HighLevel supports multiple ring strategies to match your team's workflow and call handling preferences. Each strategy determines how incoming calls are distributed among team members.

Strategy 1

Ring All (Simultaneous Ring)

All designated users' phones ring at the same time. The first person to answer connects with the caller. This strategy maximizes speed and minimizes wait time but may create competition among team members for call pickup.

Strategy 2

Round Robin

Calls are distributed sequentially to team members in rotation. Each incoming call rings one person at a time, cycling through the group. If the first person doesn't answer within the specified timeout period, the call moves to the next person in the rotation. This strategy ensures even call distribution across team members.

Strategy 3

Priority Order (Hunt Group)

Calls ring users in a predefined order. The system tries the first person in the priority list, then moves to the second if no answer, then the third, and so on. This strategy is ideal when you have a primary contact person with backup coverage from other team members.

## How to Set Up Multiple User Ring

Follow these steps to configure ring groups and distribute incoming calls across your team members.

Step 1

Access Phone Settings

Navigate to **Settings** > **Phone Numbers** in your HighLevel account. Locate the phone number you want to configure for ring groups and click the Edit Configuration.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080023210/original/NE_VVoUBr9Q4lGydF2YxjlKn104ZZr_yGA.png?1788444650)

Step 2

Configure Call Forwarding

In the phone number settings panel, locate the **Call Forwarding** section. Select the option to **Forward to Multiple Users** or **Create Ring Group**.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080023307/original/26aqgii5THzn4W0ejFkRtMD3lOwE7APJ3g.png?1788444726)

Step 3

Select Team Members

Choose which team members should receive incoming calls by checking the boxes next to their names. You can select as many users as needed. Ensure each selected user has a valid phone number configured in their user profile and has enabled call forwarding in their personal settings.  
  
![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155080023497/original/_jtcu5ySCsBRoLsLBjU8XB5c6GJUPCrdWQ.jpeg?1788444787)

Step 4

Choose Ring Strategy

Select your preferred ring strategy from the dropdown menu:

- **Ring All** for simultaneous ringing
- **Round Robin** for sequential rotation
- **Priority Order** for hierarchical fallback

Step 5

Set Ring Duration

Configure how long each user's phone should ring before timing out or moving to the next person (for Round Robin or Priority strategies). Typical values range from 15 to 30 seconds. For Ring All strategy, this determines how long all phones ring before going to voicemail.

Step 6

Configure Voicemail Fallback

Specify what happens if no one answers the call. Options typically include routing to a shared voicemail box, a specific user's voicemail, or playing a custom message. This ensures callers always have a way to leave information even when your team is unavailable.

Step 7

Save and Test

Click **Save** to apply your ring group configuration. Test the setup by calling your HighLevel phone number from an external phone. Verify that all selected team members' phones ring according to your chosen strategy.

Success

Your ring group is now active. Incoming calls to this phone number will be distributed to your team members according to the configured strategy. You can modify the ring group settings at any time by returning to the phone number settings.

Pro Tip

Monitor Ring Group Performance

Review call analytics regularly to identify which team members answer the most calls and adjust your ring strategy or team composition accordingly. Look for patterns in missed calls to optimize ring duration and voicemail settings.

## Best Practices for Ring Groups

Optimize your ring group configuration with these proven strategies to improve call handling efficiency and team coordination.

**Verify User Phone Numbers** — Ensure all team members have valid, working phone numbers configured in their user profiles before adding them to ring groups.

**Set Appropriate Ring Duration** — 20-25 seconds is usually optimal. Too short and users miss calls; too long and callers hang up.

**Limit Ring Group Size** — Keep ring groups between 3-7 users. Larger groups can create confusion and reduce individual accountability.

**Match Strategy to Team Structure** — Use Ring All for small, collaborative teams; Round Robin for even distribution; Priority Order when you have designated primary contacts.

**Create Multiple Ring Groups** — Set up different ring groups for different phone numbers or departments (sales vs. support) to route calls to the appropriate specialists.

**Configure Business Hours** — Pair ring groups with business hours settings to automatically route after-hours calls directly to voicemail or an answering service.

**Test Regularly** — Conduct monthly test calls to verify the ring group functions correctly and all team members receive calls as expected.

**Document Call Handling Procedures** — Create team guidelines for answering ring group calls, including greeting scripts and escalation protocols.

Tip

Enable call recording for ring group calls to maintain quality standards and provide training material. Review recorded calls during team meetings to identify improvement opportunities and share successful call handling examples.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I add users from different locations or time zones to the same ring group?

Yes. Ring groups work across locations and time zones. However, be mindful of time zone differences when configuring business hours settings. You may want to create separate ring groups for different regions or implement time-based routing rules to avoid ringing users outside their working hours.

Q: What happens if all users in the ring group are on other calls?

If all ring group members are busy on other calls, the system handles the incoming call according to your configured fallback behavior. Typically, this means the call will ring for the specified duration and then route to voicemail. Some configurations may allow call queuing, where callers hear hold music until a user becomes available.

Q: Can users temporarily remove themselves from a ring group without admin intervention?

Users can typically enable Do Not Disturb mode in their personal settings to temporarily stop receiving ring group calls without being removed from the configuration. This is useful for users in meetings or needing focused work time. Alternatively, users can update their personal forwarding settings, though this may affect all incoming calls to their user number, not just ring group calls.

Q: Does the caller know they're calling a ring group versus a single person?

No. From the caller's perspective, they're simply calling your business phone number. They won't hear multiple ring tones or any indication that multiple people are being contacted. The experience is identical to calling a standard phone number.

Q: Can I see which team member answered a ring group call in the call logs?

Yes. HighLevel call logs record which user answered each ring group call, along with the call duration, time, and recording (if enabled). This data helps you analyze team performance and call distribution effectiveness. You can access these reports in the Phone section under Analytics or Reports.

Q: Can I use ring groups with workflow automations?

Yes. You can trigger workflow automations based on ring group call events, such as missed calls, completed calls, or voicemails. For example, you might send a follow-up text message when a ring group call goes unanswered or create a task for the team member who answered the call.

Q: Is there a limit to how many ring groups I can create?

Ring group limits vary by HighLevel plan. Most accounts can create multiple ring groups, with each HighLevel phone number supporting one ring group configuration. If you need more advanced call routing with multiple simultaneous ring groups, contact HighLevel support to discuss your plan options and potential custom configurations.

Q: What types of phones can receive ring group calls?

Ring group calls can be forwarded to any phone number type, including mobile phones, landlines, VoIP phones, or the HighLevel desktop/mobile app. Each user specifies their preferred forwarding number in their user profile settings. The system supports both domestic and international phone numbers based on your account configuration.

title_en: WhatsApp Flows: In app Appointment Booking
source_md:
WhatsApp Automation

# WhatsApp Flows for Appointment Booking

Create guided, in-chat booking experiences that increase conversions and reduce drop-offs

What You'll Learn

This article explains how WhatsApp Flows enable interactive appointment booking directly inside WhatsApp, reducing friction and increasing booking completion rates.

You'll learn how to create appointment booking Flows, send them through templates or workflows, and use Ask AI to manage Flows conversationally.

## Why Flows Increase Booking Rates & Reduce Drop-offs

WhatsApp Flows is a feature that allows businesses to create interactive, guided conversations within WhatsApp. It enables the creation of structured, multi-step interactions that can collect information, provide choices, and guide users through specific processes—like booking an appointment.

**Reduced Friction** — Users can complete the entire booking process within WhatsApp, eliminating the need to switch to external websites or apps.

**Familiar Interface** — WhatsApp is a widely used platform, so users are already comfortable with the interface.

**Immediate Interaction** — Users can start the booking process instantly from a conversation, capitalizing on their initial interest.

**Personalization** — User details can be pre-filled, reducing effort and improving the booking experience.

**Reduced Load Times** — Unlike external websites, Flows operates within WhatsApp, typically resulting in faster load times and interactions.

## How to Create an Appointment Booking Flow

Step 1

Navigate to WhatsApp Flows Settings

Go to **Settings > WhatsApp > Flows**.

![WhatsApp Flows settings page](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155034646684/original/NVp_HaDFK6wayVWYNpnobSJJdlt_XL0ltA.png?1728907137)

Step 2

Create a New Flow

Click **Create new Flow**, add a flow name, pick the calendar where appointments should be booked, then click **Next**.

![Create new Flow form](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155034969111/original/JPfD77SO7WK3PD2OJA-qTqKNYjpyjlNGxg.png?1729254396)

Step 3

Arrange Form Fields

Arrange the default form fields for your appointment booking Flow.

![Form field arrangement](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035181602/original/_B5k1a8IdV7Ri5ExOnW6FH9_hoUDVMvQCA.png?1729599697)

Step 4

Configure Flow Content and Publish

Add the Header, Body, Footer, and Button text, then click **Publish**.

![Flow content configuration](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035182484/original/FO0nEdCva9goQYT6lRIBHPE-jv4wVhIbAQ.png?1729600214)

Note

Calendars which have payments enabled will not be supported through WhatsApp Flows, since WhatsApp currently does not have payment capabilities.

## How to Send WhatsApp Flows Through Templates

Step 1

Navigate to WhatsApp Templates

Go to **WhatsApp > Templates > Create Template**.

![Create WhatsApp template](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035183476/original/MLEVHH87wrWLYCygp9xjE4rlF8iUeYe_RA.png?1729600770)

Step 2

Configure Template Content

Add the template name, category, language, header text, body, and footer.

![Template configuration](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035184031/original/8GtcOZvkunN9KntkgRlzMdNfRcSysmnYMA.png?1729601046)

Step 3

Add a Flow Button

Add a button and select **Flow** to link it to your WhatsApp Flow.

![Add Flow button](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035184085/original/LCkagOXfbXIFZ-3wcIbK1ZqEaqwucam1kw.png?1729601081)

## How to Send WhatsApp Flows from Workflows

Note

Recurring calendar events are currently not supported through WhatsApp Flows.

### Option 1: Send WhatsApp Flow via a WhatsApp Template

Step 1

Create a New Workflow

Go to **Automations > Create Workflow > Start from Scratch**.

![Create workflow](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035062857/original/b4eyIMVE8ocE8xLR7vp4AfwkIovWWtBbeQ.png?1729493072)

Step 2

Add WhatsApp Action with Flow Template

Add the **WhatsApp Action**, select the template with the WhatsApp Flow, then click **Save Action**.

![WhatsApp action with Flow](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035184319/original/bvxkgYVoIdIOtvCziiWAcuseq8bHnShx5g.png?1729601212)

### Option 2: Send WhatsApp Flow Inside an Open Conversation (Free of Cost)

Step 1

Create a New Workflow

Go to **Automations > Create Workflow > Start from Scratch**.

![Create workflow](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035062857/original/b4eyIMVE8ocE8xLR7vp4AfwkIovWWtBbeQ.png?1729493072)

Step 2

Add Customer Service Window Check

Click the **+** button, add **WhatsApp: Customer Service Window Check**, then click **Save Action**.

![Customer service window check](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035062955/original/MkcpQ6kS0vmVceanLIkud9dp6cNbDsBDtQ.png?1729493170)

Step 3

Add Send Flows Action

Under the **Open** branch, add **WhatsApp: Send Flows**, then select the WhatsApp Flow to send.

![Send Flows action](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035063231/original/NM7MrrswjF12yTOuFb65GeBUiQ46MhYybA.png?1729493428)

Step 4

Save the Action

Click **Save Action** to complete the workflow configuration.

![Save action](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155035063241/original/EUKYLlZmty06UbUsEW9TxeLqQ51bje-wLg.png?1729493465)

## Managing Flows with Ask AI

You can now create, update, publish, deprecate, and delete WhatsApp appointment-booking Flows using conversational prompts through Ask AI for WhatsApp. This eliminates manual Flow configuration and lets you deploy self-serve booking experiences at speed.

What Ask AI Can Do

Full Lifecycle Flow Management

- Create new Appointment Booking Flows by saying which calendar or pipeline to use
- Update existing Flows conversationally (for example, changing questions or availability rules)
- Publish, deprecate, or delete Flows when they're no longer needed
- Use a guided calendar-selection wizard to link Flows to the correct HighLevel calendar (for example, "Sales Calendar" or "Clinic Appointments")

Example Prompts

- "Create a WhatsApp flow for appointment booking linked to my Sales Calendar, and publish it"
- "Update my clinic booking Flow to ask for insurance information"
- "Build a WhatsApp appointment booking Flow for my Therapy Calendar, publish it, and show me how to attach it to my reminder template"

For more details on using Ask AI to manage WhatsApp Flows, templates, campaigns, and analytics, see the [Ask AI for WhatsApp](#) article.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I send a WhatsApp Flow for appointment booking?

There are two options:  
  
**Option 1 — Using a WhatsApp Template:** Go to Automations > Create Workflow > Start from Scratch. Select the WhatsApp Action, choose a template with the WhatsApp Flow for appointment booking, then save the action.  
  
**Option 2 — Using an Open Conversation:** Go to Automations > Create Workflow > Start from Scratch. Click the + button, add WhatsApp: Customer Service Window Check, then save the action. Under the Open branch, add WhatsApp: Send Flows and select the Flow to send, then save.

Q: How do I create an appointment booking flow?

Go to Settings > WhatsApp > Flows, create a new flow, add a name and select the calendar for appointments, arrange the default form fields, add header, body, footer, and button text, then publish.  
  
Note: Calendars with payment options are not supported, as WhatsApp currently does not process payments.

Q: How do I send WhatsApp Flows through templates?

Go to WhatsApp > Templates > Create Template. Add a template name, category, language, header text, body, and footer. Add a button and select Flow to link it to the WhatsApp Flow.

Q: Can I use Ask AI to create and manage WhatsApp Flows?

Yes. Ask AI for WhatsApp provides full lifecycle control of appointment-booking Flows through conversational prompts. You can create, update, publish, deprecate, and delete Flows without manual configuration. For example, you can say "Create a WhatsApp flow for appointment booking linked to my Sales Calendar, and publish it" and Ask AI will handle the entire Flow setup.

Q: Why does integrating flows for appointment booking increase booking rates and reduce drop-offs?

- **Reduced Friction:** Users complete the booking process entirely within WhatsApp, avoiding external sites or apps.
- **Familiar Interface:** Customers feel more comfortable since WhatsApp is a widely used platform.
- **Immediate Interaction:** Customers can start booking directly from a conversation, capturing interest instantly.
- **Personalization:** Key details like name and contact info are pre-filled, reducing effort.
- **Faster Load Times:** Interactions happen quickly without the lag of external websites.

Q: What are the key benefits of using WhatsApp Flows for appointment booking?

- **Reduced friction:** Everything happens inside WhatsApp, leading to a smoother booking experience.
- **Pre-filled customer details:** Critical information such as name, email, phone number, and time zone is automatically filled in.
- **Increased engagement:** Step-by-step guided conversations help reduce confusion and increase completion rates.
- **Faster load times:** Flow interactions happen directly within WhatsApp, speeding up the process.
- **Free conversations:** The first 1,000 service conversations for appointment booking are free each month.

Q: What limitations should I be aware of with WhatsApp Flows for appointment booking?

- **No payment processing:** Appointments that require payments cannot be booked through the WhatsApp Flow, as WhatsApp currently does not support payments.
- **Custom fields:** Only default form fields are supported. Custom fields must be handled manually.
- **Recurring appointments:** Recurring calendar events are not supported.
- **Guest support:** Guest booking functionality is not available within the WhatsApp Flow.

Q: How can I create a personalized appointment booking experience using WhatsApp Flows?

Use customer-specific data fields like name, email, and phone number, which are automatically pre-filled. Customize the messaging templates with variables that match customer preferences, offering a tailored and seamless booking experience.

Q: Are there any costs associated with sending WhatsApp Flows for appointment booking?

The first 1,000 service conversations for appointment booking using WhatsApp Flows are free each month. After that, charges may apply based on WhatsApp's pricing model.  
  
Note: If the sub-account's WhatsApp integration is Coex, Flows is not supported, because Meta does not support Flows for Coex integrations.

title_en: How to Use Pricing Table Element
source_md:
Discover the new **Pricing Table** element in HighLevel—a versatile way to showcase pricing plans, packages, and service tiers. Choose from multiple layouts, apply flexible pricing models, and add conversion-focused details like badges and previous-price strikethroughs. With clear CTAs and mobile-ready behavior, this element helps visitors compare options and take action quickly.

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Pricing Table element?](#What-is-the-Pricing-Table-element?)
- [Key Benefits of Pricing Table element](#Key-Benefits-of-Pricing-Table-element)
- [How to set up the Pricing Table element](#How-to-set-up-the-Pricing-Table-element)
  - [Dynamic Layout Modes](#Dynamic-Layout-Modes)
  - [Pricing Models & Formatting](#Pricing-Models-&-Formatting)
  - [Feature Lists](#Feature-Lists)
  - [Smart Pricing Features](#Smart-Pricing-Features)
  - [Buttons & Actions](#Buttons-&-Actions)
  - [Appearance & Styling](#Appearance-&-Styling)
  - [Mobile & Responsiveness](#Mobile-&-Responsiveness)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

# **What is the Pricing Table element?**

The Pricing Table element lets you present one or more plans in a clean, comparable layout. It supports multiple display modes (grid, carousel, classic table, comparison table), several pricing models, and configurable actions so you can tailor the experience to your offer, page design, and audience.

- **Where it’s available:** Funnels, Websites, Blogs, and the E‑Commerce Store builders in HighLevel.

---

## **Key Benefits of Pricing Table element**

Understanding core benefits makes it easier to decide when and how to use the element for maximum impact on conversions and clarity.

- **Layout flexibility:** Choose Grid, Carousel, Classic Table, or Comparison Table to match your content and page goal.
- **Clear plan comparison:** Use horizontal scrolling, arrows, and sticky head column (Comparison mode) to keep features readable.
- **Multiple pricing models:** Communicate one‑time, recurring, tiered, or variable pricing without workarounds.
- **Conversion cues:** Add previous price (strikethrough), discount badges, and captions that highlight offers.
- **Action control:** Point buttons to URLs, open popups, jump to sections, download files, or have no action.
- **Brand consistency:** Customize colors, spacing, and column gaps to blend with your site design.
- **Mobile readiness:** Columns adapt for smaller screens while preserving comparison clarity.

---

## **How to set up the Pricing Table element**

A quick, repeatable setup flow reduces build time and keeps pricing consistent across pages.

1. **Navigate to the Page Builder:** In the left-hand menu of your sub-account dashboard, click on **Sites** and Open your chosen funnel or website. Click the blue **Edit** button of the page to launch the page builder  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053691733/original/VC4L91-VZN3tIpoEPJMgWKHpxQ8pkP9ZQQ.png?1757698028)
2. **Add the element**: Drag the **Pricing Table** from the Elements panel onto the canvas.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053305519/original/zAldnKQPIgXaNRHEy6Fl20qX2yxJJYVtYA.gif?1757341448)
3. **Choose a layout**: Select **Grid**, **Carousel**, **Classic**, or **Comparison** from the right settings bar.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053322294/original/JAGhBNsHYRyAvO5okG3-NgDyMkPs-GIwrw.png?1757352474)
4. **Configure the Layout**(Pricing, features, buttons etc)**and Styling**of the pricing table.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053691242/original/GigWLk63VmdwkkJ3AdSXGPi-IDMABBlU1w.png?1757697302)
5. **Preview & publish**: Use Desktop/Mobile preview to confirm responsiveness, then **Save** and **Publish**.  
     
   ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053675368/original/abInH4Z6V5QvNPbtH7iusKr9t5iJojvC8Q.png?1757687698)

---

## **Dynamic Layout Modes**

Selecting the right layout helps visitors understand differences between plans and speeds up decision‑making.

| Mode | Description / Best For | Columns & Spacing | Navigation / Controls | Animation & Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Grid Mode** | Clean, card-based layout for side-by-side comparison. | **Column gap:** 0–100 px; **Columns per row:** up to 5. | — | — |
| **Carousel Mode** | Slide-based presentation with optional auto-advance. | **Columns per slide:** 1–5. | Auto-advance interval; pause on hover; infinite loop. | **Fade** or **Slide**animation. |
| **Classic Table Mode** | Traditional table for wide, detailed comparisons. | Uses horizontal width; ideal for long feature lists. | **Horizontal scroll with arrow controls.** | — |
| **Comparison Table Mode** | Deep, column-heavy comparisons where context matters. | Wide tables; **sticky head column** remains visible. | **Horizontal scroll with arrow controls;** sticky head column for context. | — |

**Tips**

- Prefer **Grid** for simple tiers (e.g., 3–4 plans).
- Use **Carousel** if you want to feature plans one group at a time or conserve vertical space.
- Choose **Classic/Comparison** for long feature lists that won’t fit within fixed‑width cards.

---

## **Pricing Models & Formatting**

Choosing the right pricing model clarifies cost expectations and avoids surprises, which increases trust and conversions.

| Pricing Model | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed Price | One-time payment. |
| Subscription | Recurring billing with periods: daily, weekly, monthly, yearly. |
| Price From | Display “Starting at” pricing for variable services. |
| Price Range | Show min–max for customizable services. |
| Per Unit | Price by item, hour, day, seat, person, etc. |
| Free | Highlight complimentary offerings (optionally show previous price). |
| Custom | Enter custom pricing text for niche cases. |

---

## **Feature Lists**

Clear, scannable feature lists help buyers recognize what’s included and compare tiers quickly.

- Add, reorder, or remove features for each plan **(Columns)**
- Group related items and keep phrasing consistent across plans **(Columns)**
- For long lists, prefer **Classic** or **Comparison** layouts to leverage horizontal navigation.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053691450/original/McypElQnXoDL_h13dKz4hRMqJ9sDh6WIEA.png?1757697575)

---

## **Smart Pricing Features**

Visual pricing cues guide attention and make offers feel time‑sensitive or valuable without adding confusion.

- **Previous Price Display** (strikethrough) to highlight a discount.
- **Discount Text Badges** to emphasize promotions.
- **Optional Pricing Captions** for billing notes, taxes, or disclaimers.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053674324/original/4FutUIHlHQONWzmvGoMWMfnMhlLq8aezTQ.png?1757687057)

---

## **Buttons & Actions**

The call‑to‑action is where comparisons turn into conversions. Configure actions that match your funnel strategy.  
**Action types**

- **Open URL** (external or internal).
- **Open Popup** (launch a specific on‑page popup).
- **Step/Anchor Navigation** (jump to a section on the page).
- **No action** (useful for teaser plans or disabled states).

### **Button content**

- **Custom text:** Clear, action‑oriented labels (e.g., “Start Free Trial”) for Personalized call-to-action buttons
- **Optional caption:** Add supporting text below the button.
- **Show/Hide controls** for button and caption visibility.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053677278/original/1ggPubjroBVdI5A_hF5KlvXeqsb-CdXYVQ.png?1757688625)

---

## **Appearance & Styling**

Styling ensures the Pricing Table blends with your brand while remaining readable and accessible.

- Adjust **colors**, **typography**, **spacing**, **borders**, and **column gaps (0–100 px)**.
- Maintain adequate contrast for text, badges, and buttons.
- Keep card padding consistent to prevent visual jumpiness between plans.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053673658/original/4310YTG8WYxqs5uGfyeslODsvuLvuAfk_Q.png?1757686739)

---

## **Mobile & Responsiveness**

Optimizing for small screens preserves readability and ensures users can still compare plans and take action without friction.

- Multi‑column layouts may **collapse** to fewer columns on mobile for legibility.
- **Classic/Comparison** layouts retain **horizontal scroll** with **arrows** when content exceeds viewport width.
- **Sticky head column** remains visible in **Comparison** mode to keep plan names in context.
- Preview both **Desktop** and **Mobile** views and adjust spacing/typography as needed.  
    
  ![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155053673363/original/S58ebKxxtuarpZzm39q4Wk3_oxEL92GJAA.png?1757686623)

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Where can I use the Pricing Table?**  
In the **Funnels**, **Websites**, **Blogs**, and **E‑Commerce Store** builders.

**Q: How many columns can I show at once?**  
**Grid** supports up to **5 columns per row**; **Carousel** supports **1–5 columns per slide**.

**Q: Can I show old vs. new pricing?**  
Yes. Enable **Previous price** (strikethrough) and optionally add a **Discount badge**.

**Q: Can a plan button open a popup checkout or form?**  
Yes. Set the action to **Open Popup** and choose the popup you created for that page.

**Q: What happens on mobile?**  
Columns may collapse, and table layouts allow **horizontal scroll** with **arrows**. In Comparison mode, the **sticky head column** remains visible.

**Q: Which pricing models are included?**  
**Fixed**, **Subscription** (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly), **Price From**, **Price Range**, **Per Unit**, **Free**, and **Custom**.

**Q: Can I hide buttons or captions?**  
Yes. Use **Show/Hide** controls in the Button settings.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [Sites Overview](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001633-sites-overview)
- [Drag & Drop with Auto‑Hierarchical Layout](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005796-drag-and-drop-with-auto-hierarchical-layout-in-funnel-website-builder)
- [Show Popup on Entering Funnel/Website](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001150093-show-popup-on-entering-funnel-website)
- [How to Use the Download File Action for Buttons](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005540-how-to-use-the-download-file-action-for-buttons)
- [Scroll to Elements or Sections](%20https%3A//help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/48001158589-scroll-to-elements-or-sections-in-websites-or-funnels)

title_en: How to Set Up Multi-Tier Commissions
source_md:
Affiliate Manager

# How to Set Up Multi-Tier Commissions

Configure up to seven commission tiers in an Affiliate Manager campaign and set default or product-specific commission rates for each tier.

What You'll Learn

Multi-tier commissions let you distribute commissions across an affiliate hierarchy instead of rewarding only the affiliate who generates a qualifying sale. This guide explains how the tier structure works and how to configure it during affiliate campaign creation.

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [How to Set Up Multi-Tier Commissions](#How-to-Set-Up-Multi-Tier-Commissions)
- [What is Multi-Tier Commission Setup?](#What-is-Multi-Tier-Commission-Setup?)
- [Key Benefits of Multi-Tier Commissions](#Key-Benefits-of-Multi-Tier-Commissions)
- [Prerequisites and Limitations](#Prerequisites-and-Limitations)
- [Affiliate Recruitment Beyond Commission Tier Limits](#Affiliate-Recruitment-Beyond-Commission-Tier-Limits)
- [Commission Tiers vs. Affiliate Recruitment Depth](#Commission-Tiers-vs.-Affiliate-Recruitment-Depth)
- [How To Set Up Multi-Tier Commissions](#How-To-Set-Up-Multi-Tier-Commissions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)

## What is Multi-Tier Commission Setup?

Multi-tier commissions let a campaign distribute commissions across multiple levels of an affiliate hierarchy. The affiliate responsible for a qualifying sale can receive the Tier 1 commission, while eligible parent affiliates can receive commissions from higher configured tiers.

Each campaign can contain up to seven commission tiers. Each tier can use its own commission rate, allowing the reward structure to change as commissions move through the affiliate hierarchy.

TIER 1

Sale-producing affiliate

The affiliate responsible for the qualifying sale receives the applicable Tier 1 commission.

TIER 2

Parent affiliate

The eligible parent affiliate can receive the configured Tier 2 commission.

TIER 3

Next eligible parent

The next eligible parent in the hierarchy can receive the configured Tier 3 commission.

Example 1: Five-Tier Commission Distribution

Let's say your commission structure is set up as follows:

- **1st Tier:** 20%
- **2nd Tier:** 10%
- **3rd Tier:** 5%
- **4th Tier:** 3%
- **5th Tier:** 2%

The affiliate who generates the sale receives the first-tier commission. The remaining commissions are distributed to eligible referring affiliates higher in the chain according to their configured tier percentages.

![Five-tier affiliate commission distribution example](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081346043/original/Dg7nq_zncnIujoV3L7mBqMWbUx4CyGKGyw.jpeg?1789781243)

If Jan generates a $100 sale:

1. **Jan** (1st tier affiliate) earns **$20**.
2. **Toby** (Jan's recruiter, 2nd tier) earns **$10**.
3. **Ryan** (Toby's recruiter, 3rd tier) earns **$5**.
4. **Jim** (Ryan's recruiter, 4th tier) earns **$3**.
5. **Michael** (Jim's recruiter, 5th tier) earns **$2**.

Total Paid to Affiliates: $40

$20 + $10 + $5 + $3 + $2

In this example, all five configured tiers are represented in the affiliate chain, so commissions are distributed across all five levels.

Example 2: Shorter Affiliate Chain

Using the same commission structure, assume Stanley generates a $100 sale but only three affiliate levels are represented in the referral chain.

![Three-level affiliate commission distribution example](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081346045/original/cmC3MVEikYQy97Sy-4u5fozYCdB9fYj3yQ.jpeg?1789781253)

If Stanley generates a $100 sale:

1. **Stanley** (1st tier affiliate) earns **$20**.
2. **Dwight** (Stanley's recruiter, 2nd tier) earns **$10**.
3. **Michael** (Dwight's recruiter, 3rd tier) earns **$5**.

Total Paid to Affiliates: $30

$20 + $10 + $5

In this example, the referral chain contains only three affiliate levels, so commissions are distributed across those three represented tiers.

  

## Key Benefits of Multi-Tier Commissions

Multi-tier commissions give you more control over how affiliates and their referral networks are rewarded within a campaign.

**Flexible commission structures** — Configure up to seven tiers within one affiliate campaign.

**Tier-specific rewards** — Set different commission values for different levels of the affiliate hierarchy.

**Product-level control** — Use product-specific commissions when individual products require different payout rates.

**Support for sub-affiliate networks** — Reward eligible parent affiliates when affiliates beneath them generate qualifying sales.

## Prerequisites and Limitations

A multi-tier campaign needs the appropriate campaign and commission settings before HighLevel can distribute commissions through a sub-affiliate hierarchy.

- Create or select an Affiliate Manager campaign.
- Configure at least **2 tiers** if the campaign will use sub-affiliates.
- HighLevel supports a maximum of **7 commission tiers** per campaign.
- If you use product-specific commissions, make sure the applicable products are included in the campaign product list.
- Campaign-level tier structure: The campaign controls the number of commission tiers. Individual affiliate commission settings can change commission rates, but they do not change the campaign's tier count.

---

## **Affiliate Recruitment Beyond Commission Tier Limits**

Affiliates can continue recruiting sub-affiliates beyond the campaign's configured commission tiers. The number of commission tiers limits commission payouts, not affiliate recruitment depth.

When an affiliate generates a sale, commission eligibility is calculated backward from the affiliate making the sale. Only eligible affiliates within the configured commission tier limit receive commissions.

This behavior applies automatically and requires no additional configuration. Existing commission behavior within the configured tier limit remains unchanged.

---

## **Commission Tiers vs. Affiliate Recruitment Depth**

The number of commission tiers determines how many levels of affiliates can receive commissions for a qualifying sale. It does not limit how many levels of sub-affiliates can join the recruitment network.

- Affiliates can continue recruiting beyond the last configured commission tier.
- When a sale occurs, commission eligibility is calculated backward from the affiliate generating the sale.
- Only eligible affiliates within the configured tier limit receive commissions.
- This behavior applies automatically. No additional configuration is required.

## How To Set Up Multi-Tier Commissions

Multi-tier commissions are configured during the **Commissions** stage of affiliate campaign creation. Start from the Sub-Account view so the campaign source, products, tier count, and commission values are configured in the correct order.

STEP 1

Open the Affiliate Campaign creation flow

1. From the **Sub-Account view**, select **Marketing** in the left menu.
2. Select **Affiliate Manager**.
3. Select **Campaign**.
4. Click **+ Add** to create a campaign.

![Affiliate Manager Campaign page with the Add button highlighted](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081345917/original/tPzMf1pMMkjhVsLDlvxbjn1WzaS1exG-8Q.png?1789780142)

STEP 2

Configure the campaign details

The campaign source determines what the campaign tracks and which products are available for commission configuration.

1. In **Campaign details**, select the campaign source.
2. Select the applicable source details.
3. Configure the campaign link or landing destination shown for the selected source.
4. Review the product list associated with the campaign.
5. Add or remove products so the list contains the products eligible for commissions.
6. Continue to the **Commissions** step.

![Campaign details step with source settings and product list](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081345960/original/l5UM4sz1QWOKhWNTF1e4tLnTo6FNXa1O1w.png?1789780334)

STEP 3

Set the campaign's default commission

The default commission provides the base commission value for the campaign before you configure additional tiers.

1. In the **Commissions** step, enter the default commission.
2. Select whether the commission is a percentage of the product price or a flat amount.
3. If individual products need different rates, use the product-level commission controls to configure those products separately.

![Commissions step with default and product-specific commission controls](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081345965/original/udEvWWSri_kbZPmySYUoy7loU75Guhcp_Q.png?1789780439)

STEP 4

Open Advanced commission settings

Advanced commission settings control the campaign's multi-tier structure.

1. From the **Commissions** step, select **Advanced commission settings**.
2. Locate **Number of tiers**.
3. Select the number of commission tiers required for the campaign.

Tier count

HighLevel supports up to seven tiers. Leave the number of tiers at **1** when the campaign does not need a multi-tier commission structure.

![Advanced commission settings showing the Number of tiers control](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081345966/original/oqLIRT7EMlGTpm2QohjXEYpH4TFLG6Ws_A.png?1789780488)

STEP 5

Configure the commission for each tier

Each additional tier can have its own default commission or product-specific commission values.

1. After selecting the tier count, open the next tier, such as **Tier 2**.
2. Enter the **Default commission for all products** for that tier.
3. If needed, use **Customize commission by products** to assign different rates to individual products.
4. Repeat these steps for each additional tier.
5. Review the rates across all configured tiers before continuing.

![Tier 2 commission settings with default and product-specific commission options](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081346018/original/uWjzhF7US5ZRhHdI_Q7y-88rF4UKD5Ailg.png?1789780917)

Optional commission controls

Commission Length and Variable Commissions provide additional control for recurring product commissions. They are separate from the campaign's multi-tier structure.

STEP 6

Finish the campaign setup

After configuring commissions, complete the remaining campaign settings before making the campaign available to affiliates.

1. Continue to **Finish**.
2. Add a campaign description if needed.
3. Select **Assign Affiliate** if you want to assign affiliates during campaign creation.
4. Review the remaining campaign settings.
5. When the campaign is ready, select **Finish**.

![Finish step showing affiliate assignment and campaign completion options](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155081346030/original/MLqn1rRm24EAUOCxGJs2XeAt6-AgiEd6RA.png?1789781003)

title_en: Getting Started with the Flow-Based Builder for Voice AI
source_md:
**The Flow-Based Builder for Voice AI** in HighLevel lets you design AI-powered call experiences using a visual, node-based canvas.

Connect multiple AI agents, route conversations based on caller needs, and automate tasks using actions and integrations.

This makes it easier to build and manage complex conversations without relying on a single agent prompt.

```
Note: This article provides an overview of the Flow-Based Builder for Voice AI, including its key features, available nodes, and integrations. For step-by-step instructions on creating, configuring, testing, and deploying a Voice AI flow, refer to How to Create and Configure Voice AI Flows in HighLevel.
```

[동영상](https://www.loom.com/embed/42a7b59c2f39401eab0d29d451dcfb41)

---

**TABLE OF CONTENTS**

- [What is the Flow-Based Builder for Voice AI?](#What-is-the-Flow-Based-Builder-for-Voice-AI?)
- [Key Benefits of the Flow-Based Builder](#Key-Benefits-of-the-Flow-Based-Builder)
- [Understanding the Flow-Based Builder Interface](#Understanding-the-Flow-Based-Builder-Interface)
- [Types of Nodes in the Flow-Based Builder](#Types-of-Nodes-in-the-Flow-Based-Builder)
- [Multi-Agent Flows](#Multi-Agent-Flows)
- [Native Actions, Custom API, and MCP Integrations](#Native-Actions,-Custom-API,-and-MCP-Integrations)
- [Voice AI Settings and Capabilities](#Voice-AI-Settings-and-Capabilities)
- [How to Access the Flow-Based Builder](#How-to-Access-the-Flow-Based-Builder)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently-Asked-Questions)
- [Related Articles](#Related-Articles)

---

## **What is the Flow-Based Builder for Voice AI?**

The Flow-Based Builder is a visual tool for creating structured Voice AI conversations using connected nodes. Each node performs a specific task, such as speaking with a caller, choosing a conversation path, or executing an action.

Unlike the traditional prompt-based builder, Flow-Based Builder allows you to assign different responsibilities to multiple AI agents within a single flow.

For example, a call can move through a **Greeter Agent → Qualification Agent → Booking Agent**, with each agent handling a different stage of the conversation.

---

## **Key Benefits of the Flow-Based Builder**

Flow-Based Builder helps you organize conversations into smaller, manageable steps, giving you more control over how calls are handled and how agents perform their tasks.

- **Visual Flow Design:** Build and manage conversations by connecting nodes on a single canvas.
- **Multi-Agent Conversations:** Assign different prompts, AI models, and tools to individual agents.
- **Flexible Routing:** Direct callers to different conversation paths based on their needs.
- **Automated Actions:** Send messages, interact with APIs, and perform supported CRM operations.
- **MCP Integration:** Connect agents to tools for managing contacts, calendars, appointments, and other supported operations.
- **Built-In Testing:** Test conversations using Web Call or Phone Call before deployment.

---

## **Understanding the Flow-Based Builder Interface**

The builder provides a visual workspace for designing conversations, configuring individual components, and testing how they interact. Its main areas help you organize the flow without managing everything through one prompt.

- **Canvas:** The workspace where nodes are added, connected, and arranged.
- **Node Library:** Contains available AI agents, routing controls, actions, and integrations.
- **Node Configuration:** Allows you to customize supported settings for individual nodes.
- **Build and Deploy:** Provides access to flow editing and deployment configurations.
- **Test Your Agent:** Allows you to test conversations using Web Call or Phone Call.

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083205989/original/m-826c4mfLu_FKxB_ypLRashlHPJ4O22eg.png?1791897875)**

---

## **Types of Nodes in the Flow-Based Builder**

Nodes control how a conversation starts, progresses, and ends. You can combine conversational, routing, and action nodes to create call experiences suited to different business needs.

| Node | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Start Call** | Marks the starting point of the conversation. |
| **AI Agent** | Handles conversations using its own prompt, model, and assigned tools. |
| **Router** | Directs the conversation to different paths based on configured routing logic. |
| **End Call** | Concludes a conversation path. |
| **Search Knowledge Base** | Retrieves information from connected knowledge resources. |
| **Search the Web** | Retrieves web information for supported use cases. |
| **MCP Server** | Connects agents to external tools and supported HighLevel operations. |
| **Actions** | Performs tasks such as sending SMS, sending email, or making Custom API requests. |

Available nodes and actions may vary as new Voice AI capabilities are introduced.

---

## **Multi-Agent Flows**

Multi-Agent Flows allow multiple AI Agent nodes to work together during a single conversation. Each agent can have its own prompt, model, tools, and responsibilities, while Router nodes determine which path the conversation follows.

Common use cases include:

- **Lead Qualification:** Greeter → Qualification Agent → CRM Update
- **Appointment Scheduling:** Greeter → Booking Agent → Calendar Integration
- **Customer Support:** Greeter → Router → Support Agent

This approach helps keep individual agent instructions focused while supporting more complex call experiences.

---

## **Native Actions, Custom API, and MCP Integrations**

Actions and integrations extend Voice AI beyond answering questions. They allow agents to interact with contacts, send messages, retrieve information, and complete supported tasks during conversations.

**1. Native Actions**

Built-in actions provide ready-to-configure functionality within the builder. The initial release included:

- Send SMS
- Send Email
- Custom API

Additional Voice AI actions have been introduced since the initial release. Check the current Actions list for the options supported by your Flow-Based Builder.

**2. Custom API**

Custom API allows agents to communicate with external systems using API requests. This is useful when a required operation is not available as a native action.

**3. MCP Server**

Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations connect agents to supported tools and services, including operations related to:

- Contacts and CRM records
- Calendars and appointment availability
- Appointment creation
- Other supported HighLevel capabilities

For example, contact information can be updated using a supported native action where available, or through MCP or Custom API integrations.

MCP and Custom API integrations may require additional authentication and configuration.

For advanced setup instructions, refer to [Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration for Voice AI Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008533-model-context-protocol-mcp-integration-for-voice-ai-agents).

---

## **Voice AI Settings and Capabilities**

Flow-Based Builder includes essential Voice AI settings for controlling how agents communicate with callers. These settings help you customize the calling experience without changing the underlying flow structure.

Supported capabilities include:

- Inbound and outbound calling
- Voice and language selection
- Inbound and outbound welcome messages
- Call settings and noise cancellation
- Transcription and translation
- Post-call settings
- Outbound compliance settings
- Web Call and Phone Call testing

**![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083206502/original/wL7kyLYmxt8Eg_VHDZDzSSdBxDU-W-xAuQ.png?1791898079)**

---

## **How to Access the Flow-Based Builder**

You can access the visual builder when creating a new Voice AI agent. Selecting Flow Based Builder opens a canvas where you can start designing the conversation.

1. Navigate to **AI Agents → Voice AI** in your HighLevel sub-account.
2. Open **Agent List** and click **+ Create Agent**.
3. Select **Flow Based Builder**.
4. Click **Continue** to open the builder.

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155083206779/original/fcY7rWoRPFrLgzTj4Gh1_XaQsTjE8937ww.png?1791898162)

A new blank flow begins with a **Start Call** node connected to an **AI Agent** node. Save the agent to retain your work.

For detailed instructions on adding nodes, configuring routing, setting up integrations, and deploying your flow, refer to **How to Create and Configure Voice AI Flows Using the Flow-Based Builder.**

---

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q: Can each AI Agent node use a different AI model?**

Yes. Each AI Agent node can have its own supported AI model, prompt, and tools.

**Q: Do I need MCP to use the Flow-Based Builder?**

No. You can build conversations using AI Agent nodes, routers, and native actions without MCP. Use MCP when your flow requires supported external tools or additional integrations.

**Q: Can Flow-Based Voice AI agents be included in Snapshots?**

Yes. Flow-Based Voice AI agents can be included in Snapshots, allowing supported flow configurations to be reused across sub-accounts. Phone numbers and live call data are not transferred.

**Q: Can Flow-Based Builder agents book appointments?**

Appointment booking can be supported through configured integrations or available native actions. The setup method depends on the capabilities available in your builder.

**Q: Can I use the Flow-Based Builder for outbound calls?**

Yes. Flow-Based Builder supports inbound and outbound calling, subject to the applicable configuration and outbound compliance requirements.

**Q: Is a multi-agent flow the same as Agent Transfer?**

No. Multi-agent flows connect AI Agent nodes within one visual conversation. Agent Transfer is a separate feature that hands a live conversation to another Voice AI agent.

---

## **Related Articles**

- [How to Create Voice AI Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004107-how-to-create-voice-ai-agents)
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration for Voice AI Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008533-model-context-protocol-mcp-integration-for-voice-ai-agents)
- [Build with AI for Voice AI Flows](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008311-build-with-ai-for-voice-ai-flows)
- [How to Use Voice AI Flow Builder Templates and Guided Setup](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008604-how-to-use-voice-ai-flow-builder-templates-and-guided-setup)
- [How to Test Voice AI Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000004108-testing-voice-ai-agents)
- [Snapshot Support for Flow-Based Voice AI Agents](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008490-snapshot-support-for-flow-based-voice-ai-agents)

title_en: Ask AI Skills and Connectors
source_md:
Ask AI

# Ask AI Skills and Connectors

Connect Ask AI to your favorite apps and teach it your workflows—with complete control over every tool and instruction.

What You'll Learn

Ask AI Connectors let you link your Notion, Canva, GitHub, HubSpot, or any Model Context Protocol (MCP) app directly to Ask AI. You authenticate once, grant per-app or per-tool permissions, and Ask AI acts inside your accounts—securely, without exposing credentials.

Ask AI Skills let you codify how you want work done. Write a custom instruction set, upload an existing playbook or SOP, and Ask AI will apply it automatically when your request matches—or on demand via the **/** command in any text or voice chat.

## What Are Connectors?

Connectors let Ask AI act inside the apps you already use—Notion, Canva, GitHub, HubSpot, or any app in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) marketplace. You authenticate under your own login (not a sub-account's), and Ask AI can read, create, update, or search within the connected service on your behalf.

Every connector is linked to your user account within a company, so your credentials and tool selections never leak across agency or sub-account boundaries.

**Marketplace browser in Ask AI** — Open **Customize → Connectors → Manage Connectors** to browse and connect any MCP app without leaving Ask AI.

**Per-app and per-tool control** — Toggle an entire connector on or off, or pick exactly which tools (e.g., "create page", "search database") the AI may invoke.

**Two-way sync with the marketplace** — Connect an app anywhere in HighLevel and it appears in Ask AI ready to use. Renames and new icons follow automatically; your enable/tool choices are preserved.

**Browser Control connector** — Enable the Browser Control connector to let Ask AI open pages, click, fill forms, and complete multi-step tasks in Chrome, Edge, Brave, or Arc (requires the Ask AI Chrome extension).

![](https://s3.amazonaws.com/cdn.freshdesk.com/data/helpdesk/attachments/production/155078134050/original/2zJmC3T6KiF9fhBcEnBAqd6Y4_8J9cbTxg.gif?1786453754)

## What Are Skills?
